732	=================== motion/add-a-transition
733	---
734	title: "Add or remove a transition"
735	description: "Put a transition on a cut, change the style of one you already have, get past a cut with no spare footage, and take a transition off again."
736	---
737	
738	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
739	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
740	
741	A transition plays across an overlap between two clips on the same track. **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** makes that overlap for you at a cut, restyles one that's already there, and takes a transition off.
742	
743	<AtAGlance
744	  menu="Clip ▸ Transition ▸"
745	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Transition ▸ Kind"
746	  tools={['add_transition', 'set_transition']}
747	/>
748	
749	## Add a transition
750	
751	<Steps>
752	
753	1. Select the clip after the cut. A transition belongs to the clip it leads into. To do several cuts at once, select the clip after each cut.
754	
755	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** and a [style](/motion/transition-styles/).
756	
757	</Steps>
758	
759	The overlap appears on the timeline as a hatched zone, with the style's name in it when the word fits. To change its length or easing, use [the Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
760	
761	## The Transition menu
762	
763	The menu lists the thirteen styles, then **None**. It has no keyboard shortcuts. It works on every selected clip at once, as one undo step called **Set Transition**, and what each clip gets depends on where it sits.
764	
765	| Where the clip sits | What happens |
766	| --- | --- |
767	| It starts exactly where the clip before it ends | A new overlap is made. See [At a hard cut](#at-a-hard-cut). |
768	| It already overlaps the clip before it | It gets the new style. See [Restyle an overlap](#restyle-an-overlap). |
769	| After a gap, or first on its track | Nothing. See [Clips that are skipped](#clips-that-are-skipped). |
770	
771	A style is available only when at least one selected clip is at a hard cut or an overlap. **None** is available for any selection.
772	
773	The checkmark shows the style of the earliest selected clip, or **None** when that clip has no transition.
774	
775	## At a hard cut
776	
777	A clip that starts exactly where the clip before it ends gets a new half-second overlap, centred on the cut.
778	
779	The overlap is made from footage the two clips aren't showing. The first clip plays on past its out point, and the second starts earlier than its in point. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and the outer edges of the pair stay where they were.
780	
781	If there isn't half a second to spare, the transition comes out shorter. The length is limited by:
782	
783	- The footage each clip has beyond the cut. When one side runs short, the other side gives more if it can, so the overlap can end up off-centre.
784	- The neighbours. The first clip can't grow into the clip after the second, and the second can't grow into the clip before the first.
785	- [The overlap rules](/motion/transitions/), which hold an overlap to half the shorter clip.
786	
787	Text, shape, still, image and graphic clips have no file to run out of, so they can always give their share. A [nest](/editing/nests/) clip gives nothing before its start, and past its end it gives only what's left of the nest.
788	
789	The incoming clip now starts earlier, and what's timed to its picture stays in step. Its [actions](/motion/actions/) stay on the frames they were drawn over, so a zoom stays on its click, and timed caption words stay on their speech. A fade-in or a text reveal now starts at the clip's new first frame, so it begins under the transition.
790	
791	If the clip still holds a transition from an earlier overlap, it takes the style you chose and keeps that transition's curve and crossfade. Otherwise the new transition starts with the [default values](/motion/transition-settings/#default-values).
792	
793	## Restyle an overlap
794	
795	A clip that already overlaps the clip before it takes the style you choose, and keeps its curve and crossfade. The **Kind** row in [the Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/#kind) does the same for one clip.
796	
797	## Clips that are skipped
798	
799	A clip after a gap has nothing to overlap, and neither does the first clip on its track, so the menu skips them. If you select a run of clips that starts after a gap or at the start of its track, the first one is skipped and every cut after it gets the style.
800	
801	## No extra footage
802	
803	Two clips that each use their whole file have nothing beyond the cut to overlap with. When none of the cuts you chose can take a transition, Frame Job shows a sheet that says "There’s no extra footage at this cut for a transition.", or "at these cuts" for several.
804	
805	| Button | What it does |
806	| --- | --- |
807	| **Shift Clips Left** | Makes the overlap another way. See [Shift Clips Left](#shift-clips-left). |
808	| **Cancel** | Changes nothing. |
809	
810	A cut with footage to spare gets a shorter transition instead of the sheet, unless its clips are so short that the overlap rules leave no room for even one frame. If you chose several cuts and at least one takes a transition, there's no sheet either, and the cuts with no footage stay as they are.
811	
812	## Shift Clips Left
813	
814	**Shift Clips Left** makes the overlap by sliding the second clip, and everything after it on unlocked tracks, left by half a second. The second clip's first frames then blend over the first clip's last ones.
815	
816	- The project gets shorter by the same amount.
817	- No clip's footage changes.
818	- The shift is capped at half the shorter clip, and at the longest shift that keeps every moved track within [the overlap rules](/motion/transitions/).
819	- Markers don't move.
820	- A clip on another track that ends up overlapping its neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve.
821	- Clips on locked tracks stay where they are, so they fall out of step with what moved.
822	- The whole shift is one undo step, **Add Transition**, however many cuts it covers.
823	
824	Frame Job won't shift a second clip on a locked track. With only that cut chosen it beeps and nothing moves.
825	
826	## Overlap two clips by hand
827	
828	You can make a transition without the menu. When an edit makes a clip overlap the clip before it on the same track, and that clip has no stored transition, Frame Job adds a Cross Dissolve. That holds whether you drag, trim an edge, paste, add a clip, close a gap or shift clips.
829	
830	See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/) for the overlap rules, and [Default values](/motion/transition-settings/#default-values) for how that Cross Dissolve starts out.
831	
832	## Remove a transition
833	
834	Select the later clip of the pair and choose **Clip ▸ Transition ▸ None**, or choose **None** in the **Kind** row of [the Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/#kind).
835	
836	**None** in the menu is available for any selected clip, because a clip can hold a transition the timeline doesn't draw, such as one left behind when an overlap was dragged apart. It clears every selected clip, wherever each one sits.
837	
838	### None keeps the overlap
839	
840	**None** removes the transition but not the overlap. While the two clips still overlap they keep blending, as a plain linear dissolve with no hatch and no sound crossfade.
841	
842	To get a hard cut back, move or trim the clips so they no longer overlap.
843	
844	:::caution
845	An overlap with no transition doesn't stay that way. The next time you move or trim a clip on that track, or change the overlap's **Duration**, Frame Job gives it a Cross Dissolve again.
846	:::
847	
848	A transition you don't clear stays on the clip after you pull the overlap apart. It draws nothing until the clip overlaps something again, then comes back with its style. Choose **None** as well if you don't want that.
849	
850	## Good to know
851	
852	- An adjustment clip can't take a transition, on either side of a cut. Fade it with opacity instead. At a hard cut beside one, the no-extra-footage sheet still appears, and **Shift Clips Left** only beeps.
853	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the menu works on the clips inside it.
854	
855	## With an agent
856	
857	The menu uses the same two tools: `add_transition` for a clip at a hard cut, and `set_transition` for a clip that already overlaps.
858	
859	`add_transition` needs a `clip` and a `duration`. The menu always asks for half a second, centred on the cut. An agent can ask for any length of one frame or more, take the footage from [one side of the cut](/motion/transition-settings/#alignment), or shift clips with `ripple: true`, without going through the sheet. A request too long for the footage lands shorter, and one under a frame fails with a message naming the shortest length that works. With no `kind`, it uses the style the clip already holds, or Cross Dissolve if it holds none. The tool only works at a hard cut. On any other clip it fails, saying whether the clip is first on its track, follows a gap or already overlaps.
860	
861	`set_transition` needs a `clip` and a `kind`. Setting `kind: null` removes the transition, and because `kind` is required, leaving it out by mistake can't clear one. The tool can also put a style on a clip with no overlap, where it draws nothing until the clip overlaps something. See [Tools: transitions](/mcp/tools-transitions/).
862	
863	## Related

867	- [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/)
868	- [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/)

871	---
872	title: "The Transition section"
873	description: "Set one transition's style, easing and length in the inspector, and see what values a new transition starts with."
874	---
875	
876	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
877	
878	The **Transition** section is where you fine-tune one transition: its style, how it's eased and how long it lasts.
879	
880	<AtAGlance
881	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Transition"
882	  tools={['set_transition', 'set_transition_style', 'set_transition_duration']}
883	/>
884	
885	## Open the section
886	
887	Select the later clip of an overlapping pair, then look on the **Clip** sub-tab of the [Clip tab](/getting-started/inspector/). A transition belongs to the clip it leads into, so the earlier clip of the pair won't show it unless it overlaps a clip before it too.
888	
889	The section appears only when exactly one clip is selected and that clip overlaps the clip before it. To change several transitions at once, use [**Clip ▸ Transition ▸**](/motion/add-a-transition/#the-transition-menu).
890	
891	It starts closed. Its header sums it up, for example "cross dissolve · ease in out · 0.50 s", or "none" when the overlap has no stored transition.
892	
893	| Row | What it does | Values |
894	| --- | --- | --- |
895	| [**Kind**](#kind) | The style, or none | None and the thirteen [styles](/motion/transition-styles/) |
896	| [**Curve**](#curve) | How the transition's progress is eased | Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In Out |
897	| **Crossfade Audio** | Whether the sound crossfades. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/). | On or off |
898	| **Crossfade Shape** | The crossfade's curve. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/). | Linear, S-Curve, +3 dB, −3 dB |
899	| [**Duration**](#duration) | The length of the overlap | 0.02 to 10 s |
900	
901	Each change is one undo step.
902	
903	## Kind
904	
905	**Kind** lists **None**, then the thirteen styles in the same order as the **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** menu. Changing the style keeps the **Curve** and the crossfade settings.
906	
907	Choosing **None** removes the transition but not the overlap. See [None keeps the overlap](/motion/add-a-transition/#none-keeps-the-overlap).
908	
909	## Curve
910	
911	**Curve** changes how the transition moves through its length, not how long it lasts.
912	
913	| Curve | How it moves |
914	| --- | --- |
915	| **Linear** | At a steady rate from start to finish |
916	| **Ease In** | Starts slowly and speeds up |
917	| **Ease Out** | Starts quickly and slows down |
918	| **Ease In Out** | Starts and ends slowly |
919	
920	The sound crossfade follows the same curve.
921	
922	The curve also moves the swap in a [Fade Through Black or White](/motion/transition-styles/#fade-through-black-and-fade-through-white). With **Linear** or **Ease In Out** the clips swap halfway through the overlap. With **Ease In** it's about 71% of the way through, and with **Ease Out** about 29%.
923	
924	## Duration
925	
926	**Duration** is the length of the overlap, in seconds. Type a value, or pick 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 from the arrow at the end of the field. A number outside 0.02 to 10 s is pulled to the nearer end of that range, and the result snaps to the frame grid. A value that rounds to no frames at all closes the overlap and leaves a hard cut.
927	
928	The overlap is the transition's length, so changing **Duration** moves the later clip to match: earlier for a longer transition, later for a shorter one. Only that clip moves.
929	
930	- Clips after it stay where they are, so a longer transition can open a gap after the clip.
931	- A shorter transition can run the clip into the one after it, and that new overlap gets a Cross Dissolve.
932	- A linked clip doesn't move with it.
933	
934	Frame Job won't let an overlap pass half the shorter clip, or move the clip anywhere that breaks [the overlap rules](/motion/transitions/) with its other neighbours. The message at the foot of the inspector names the limit, and nothing changes.
935	
936	## Alignment
937	
938	Alignment decides which clip's footage a new overlap at a hard cut is made from. The section has no control for it. **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** always centres a new overlap on the cut: half of it comes from each clip, an odd frame comes from the incoming clip, and a side that runs short passes its share to the other.
939	
940	An agent can choose the side with the `align` argument of `add_transition`:
941	
942	| Choice | Where the footage comes from | What stays put |
943	| --- | --- | --- |
944	| `center`, the default | Half from each clip | The moment of the cut |
945	| `before` | All from the start of the incoming clip | The outgoing clip's last frame |
946	| `after` | All from the end of the outgoing clip | The incoming clip's first frame |
947	
948	## Default values
949	
950	A transition Frame Job makes starts with **Curve** at **Ease In Out** and **Crossfade Audio** on, with **Crossfade Shape** at **+3 dB**. When you didn't choose a style, it's a Cross Dissolve.
951	
952	[An overlap with no stored transition](/motion/transitions/#an-overlap-with-no-stored-transition), such as one you set to **None**, draws as a linear Cross Dissolve with no crossfade. The section says so: **Kind** reads **None**, **Curve** reads **Linear** and **Crossfade Audio** is off. From there:
953	
954	- Changing **Curve** or **Crossfade Audio** stores a Cross Dissolve with exactly the values showing, and your one change. **Crossfade Shape** stays dimmed until **Crossfade Audio** is on.
955	- Choosing a **Kind** makes a new transition with the defaults above, not the values that were showing.
956	
957	## Good to know
958	
959	Two overlapping clips with no picture get the same section. Only their sound changes, so **Kind** has no visible effect.
960	
961	## With an agent
962	
963	`set_transition_style` sets **Curve**, **Crossfade Audio** and **Crossfade Shape** through `curve`, `audio` and `audio_shape`. Anything left out stays as it is, and with none of the three given nothing changes. Unlike the section, it works on any clip. A clip with no transition gets a Cross Dissolve with that style.
964	
965	`set_transition_duration` does what **Duration** does, and it fails on the first clip of a track, which has nothing to overlap. `set_transition` sets **Kind**.
966	
967	See [Tools: transitions](/mcp/tools-transitions/).
968	
969	## Related
970

972	- [Transition styles](/motion/transition-styles/)
973	- [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/)
974	- [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/)

976	=================== motion/transition-styles
977	---
978	title: "Transition styles"
979	description: "What each of the thirteen transition styles looks like, and how each one treats small layers and clips of different sizes."
980	---
981	
982	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
983	
984	A transition's style decides how one clip gives way to the next across their overlap. Frame Job has thirteen: Cross Dissolve, two fades, four pushes, four wipes, Slide and Zoom.
985	
986	<AtAGlance
987	  menu="Clip ▸ Transition ▸"
988	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Transition ▸ Kind"
989	  tools={['add_transition', 'set_transition']}
990	/>
991	
992	To put a style on a cut, see [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/). To change how it's eased or how long it lasts, see [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
993	
994	## Cross Dissolve
995	
996	The outgoing clip fades out as the incoming clip fades in. The two always add up to a whole picture, so the frame doesn't dip dark in the middle.
997	
998	Where only one of the two clips covers part of the canvas, that part fades to whatever is behind it.
999	
1000	This is the style Frame Job uses when it adds a transition without being asked, such as when you drag one clip over the end of another.
1001	
1002	## Fade Through Black and Fade Through White
1003	
1004	**Fade Through Black** takes the outgoing clip down to black over the first half of the transition. At the halfway point the clips swap, and the incoming clip fades up from black over the second half.
1005	
1006	**Fade Through White** does the same through white. In an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), the white is SDR white as it sits in that project, not the brightest white HLG can show.
1007	
1008	The two clips are never on screen together. See [Fades on small layers](#fades-on-small-layers) for what these styles do to a clip that doesn't fill the canvas.
1009	
1010	## Push
1011	
1012	Both clips move together, as if the incoming clip were shoving the outgoing one off the canvas.
1013	
1014	| Style | The outgoing clip leaves | The incoming clip comes in from |
1015	| --- | --- | --- |
1016	| **Push Left** | To the left | The right |
1017	| **Push Right** | To the right | The left |
1018	| **Push Up** | Upward | The bottom |
1019	| **Push Down** | Downward | The top |
1020	
1021	## Wipe
1022	
1023	An edge sweeps across the picture, taking the outgoing clip away and revealing the incoming clip behind it. Neither clip moves. The edge is very slightly soft, so it doesn't crawl.
1024	
1025	| Style | The edge sweeps |
1026	| --- | --- |
1027	| **Wipe** | Left to right |
1028	| **Wipe Left** | Right to left |
1029	| **Wipe Up** | Bottom to top |
1030	| **Wipe Down** | Top to bottom |
1031	
1032	## Slide
1033	
1034	The incoming clip slides in from the right over the outgoing clip, which stays where it is. Slide only comes in from the right. For the other directions, use a [Push](#push).
1035	
1036	## Zoom
1037	
1038	The outgoing clip grows toward you, from 100% to 125% of its size, while the incoming clip grows into place from 75% to 100%. The two dissolve into each other as they go. Each clip grows around its own centre.
1039	
1040	## Small layers and clips of different sizes
1041	
1042	A transition plays on each clip where that clip sits, not on the canvas as a whole. You won't see any of what follows on two full-frame clips of the same size. It matters for a picture-in-picture, or for a pair that differ in size, position, crop or rotation.
1043	
1044	### Wipes on mismatched clips
1045	
1046	A wipe's edge is measured in each clip's own frame, so two clips of different sizes don't meet at one line. Halfway through, the edge is halfway across each clip, wherever each one sits. The frame is the clip as it's cropped and placed, so on a rotated clip the edge turns with the clip.
1047	
1048	Between the two edges you can see whatever is behind the pair, or both clips at once.
1049	
1050	### Fades on small layers
1051	
1052	A fade through a colour changes the clip's own pixels toward that colour. On a clip smaller than the canvas, such as a picture-in-picture, you see a black or white box over what's behind it, not a see-through fade.
1053	
1054	For a small clip that should melt into the picture behind it, use [Cross Dissolve](#cross-dissolve).
1055	
1056	### Push and Slide on small layers
1057	
1058	A Push or a Slide always travels one whole canvas width, or one whole canvas height for Push Up and Push Down, whatever the size of the clip. A small incoming clip starts one canvas away from where it lands, so it doesn't begin at the edge of the frame unless it's placed there.
1059	
1060	Slide leaves the outgoing clip at full strength until the overlap ends. If the incoming clip is smaller, the outgoing clip stays visible around it for the whole transition, then disappears when the overlap ends.
1061	
1062	## Good to know
1063	
1064	- The style only changes the picture. Whether the sound crossfades is a separate choice, and it works the same with all thirteen. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/).
1065	- A clip always draws with the Normal blend mode during a transition, whatever [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/) it has.
1066	- Cross Dissolve and Zoom treat a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip as one picture. The other styles play on each layer inside the nest, so a wipe's edge is measured in each layer's own frame.
1067	
1068	## With an agent
1069	
1070	An agent names a style by its `kind`, which is the style's name in lower case with underscores: `cross_dissolve`, `push_left`, `wipe_up`, `slide`. The plain **Wipe** is `wipe`, and the two fades are `fade_black` and `fade_white`. See [Tools: transitions](/mcp/tools-transitions/).
1071	
1072	## Related
1073	
1074	- [Transitions](/motion/transitions/)
1075	- [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/)
1076	- [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/)
1077	- [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/)

1	=================== mcp/tools-animation
2	---
3	title: "Tools: animation"
4	description: Add actions to a clip from an agent, set what they animate to, zoom to a region, and move, re-curve or remove them.
5	---
6	
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	An [action](/motion/actions/) is a span on a clip over which its properties ease from what they are to an end state. These tools add one, say what it ends at, change its timing and take it away.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  tools={['add_action', 'add_zoom_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
14	  keys="⌥⌘K"
15	  where="Clip tab ▸ action lane"
16	/>
17	
18	The usual order is two calls. First, `add_action` with these arguments:
19	
20	```json
21	{ "clip": 12, "at": 600000, "duration": 1200000 }
22	```
23	
24	Then `set_action_end`, with the id it answered in `new_actions`:
25	
26	```json
27	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "video": { "scale": 1.4 } } }
28	```
29	
30	Every time here is in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and is rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). An action's times are clip time, measured from the clip's own start, not the timeline's. `get_project` lists each clip's actions and their ids.
31	
32	For a speed ramp in one step, see `add_speed_ramp` on [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
33	
34	## `add_action`
35	
36	Adds an action to a clip. Its end state starts empty, so nothing changes until `set_action_end` fills it in. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>) and the **+** button in the Clip tab's action lane. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/).
37	
38	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
39	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
40	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
41	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the action starts, in clip time. |
42	| `duration` | integer | No | How long it runs. The default is 1 s (600,000). |
43	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
44	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
45	
46	**What it answers.** `ok`, `clip`, `new_actions` (a list holding the new action's id) and the `project` summary. A new action's curve is `linear`. Use `set_action` to change it.
47	
48	**When it refuses.**
49	
50	- It would overlap another action on the clip, or run past the clip's end. Both sentences give the times involved.
51	- A negative `at` or a `duration` that isn't positive is an error.
52	
53	## `add_zoom_action`
54	
55	Adds an action that zooms the picture to a rectangle, the screencast zoom, or back out to the clip's own framing. It mirrors the canvas's Z mode and the **Zoom to Region** and **Zoom Back** buttons in the Clip tab's action lane. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/).
56	
57	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
58	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
59	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
60	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the zoom starts, in clip time. |
61	| `region` | object or null | Yes | The rectangle to zoom to, as `{x, y, width, height}`. `null` zooms back to the clip's own scale and position. |
62	| `duration` | integer | No | How long it runs. The default is 1 s (600,000). |
63	| `fit` | string | No | `fit`, the default, shows the whole region. `fill` covers the whole canvas, cropping whatever the region's shape doesn't match. |
64	| `curve` | string | No | How the zoom eases: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. The default is `ease_in_out`. |
65	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
66	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
67	
68	```json
69	{ "clip": 12, "at": 0, "region": { "x": -320, "y": 180, "width": 640, "height": 360 } }
70	```
71	
72	`region` is in source pixels. `x` and `y` are its centre, measured from the centre of the clip's cropped picture, and `width` and `height` are its size. All four are required, and the key itself is required, so a forgotten rectangle can't turn into a zoom back.
73	
74	Over the action, the clip's `scale`, `x` and `y` ease to the values that bring the region to the canvas, measured through the clip's rotation. Rotation and crop are read as they are at `at`. The scale is held to the largest a clip can take, with the position worked out from that, so a region too small to fill the canvas still lands centred.
75	
76	**What it answers.** As `add_action`. The action is an ordinary one, so `set_action_end` can add to what it animates.
77	
78	**When it refuses.**
79	
80	- It would overlap another action or run past the clip's end, as `add_action`.
81	- A clip with no picture is an error: "clip 7 has no video properties".
82	- A `width` or `height` that isn't above 0, or a member the region doesn't have, is an error naming it.
83	
84	## `set_action`
85	
86	Moves an action, changes its length or changes its easing curve. It mirrors the selected action's start, length and curve controls in the Clip tab's action lane, and dragging a band. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
87	
88	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
89	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
90	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
91	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
92	| `start` | integer | No | The new start, in clip time. |
93	| `duration` | integer | No | The new length. |
94	| `curve` | string | No | How the values ease: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. |
95	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
96	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
97	
98	Give at least one of `start`, `duration` and `curve`. Any you leave out keep their value.
99	
100	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. When the action's end names a speed, captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are re-timed in the same step: `captions_retimed` lists them, and `captions_removed` lists those whose speech it no longer plays. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
101	
102	**When it refuses.**
103	
104	- It would overlap another action on the clip.
105	- It would end past the clip's end and later than it ended before. An action a trim left past the clip's end can still be re-curved, moved earlier or shortened.
106	- On a speed action, it would make the clip read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
107	- On a speed action of a linked clip, it would change the clip's speed: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
108	- With none of the three arguments, the call answers "set_action needs start, duration or curve."
109	
110	## `set_action_end`
111	
112	Sets what an action animates to. It mirrors every inspector field you change while an action is selected. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) and [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
113	
114	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
115	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
116	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
117	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
118	| `patch` | object | Yes | The end state, with `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic` groups and a top-level `speed`. |
119	| `off` | array of strings | No | `"group.key"` paths to switch off at the end. See [Switching off at an end](#switching-off-at-an-end). |
120	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
121	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
122	
123	```json
124	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "video": { "opacity": 0 }, "audio": { "volume": 0.2 } } }
125	```
126	
127	The patch merges into the end state key by key, at every depth, so a one-key `shadow` keeps the rest of it. A key set to `null` is removed from the end state, so that property stops being animated, and a group set to `null` removes the whole group.
128	
129	The `video`, `audio` and `text` groups take the same keys as [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/), [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/) and [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/). A colour is four numbers here too, and it ramps in OKLab with straight alpha. So do the chroma key's three numbers.
130	
131	A bad key or value is refused by its path with the group in it, such as `video.filters[1].kind`. Values aren't range-checked, though: an animation can aim past what a stored property could hold.
132	
133	**Sound.** These `audio` keys animate: `pan`, `mono`, `channels`, `eq`, `hum`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `isolation`, beside `volume` and the fades.
134	
135	- Numbers ramp.
136	- A switch changes when the action ends: a group or an EQ slot turned on, `mono`, `channels`, an EQ slope, hum's frequency and harmonics, and the leveller's response.
137	- `isolation` ramps from 0 on a clip with none.
138	- `duck`, `keep_pitch`, the fade shapes and `voice` are stored but never animate.
139	
140	See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
141	
142	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. With `speed` in the patch it can add the keys listed under [Speed in an action](#speed-in-an-action).
143	
144	**When it refuses.** These keys are errors, a `null` included:
145	
146	| Key | Why, and what to do instead |
147	| --- | --- |
148	| `video.motion` | It's a preset tied to the clip's two ends. Set it with `set_video`. |
149	| `video.hide_silent` | It isn't an animation target. Set it with `set_video`. |
150	| `text.words` | Word times belong to speech. Set them with `set_text`. |
151	| `video.cutout.subject`, `video.cutout.quality` | They hold for the whole clip. Set them with `set_video`. A cutout's `edge`, `feather` and `background` do animate. |
152	| Any `shape` key | Shapes can't be animated, so `shape` isn't a group here. |
153	
154	### Animating graphic props
155	
156	A graphic clip's props are a fourth group: `graphic: {props: {<key>: <value>}}`, keyed by what its module declares. It mirrors the Graphic sub-tab's **Properties** with an action selected. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
157	
158	```json
159	{ "clip": 18, "action": 44, "patch": { "graphic": { "props": { "accent": "#ff5500", "count": 96 } } } }
160	```
161	
162	- A value is checked as `set_graphic` checks it, minimum and maximum included, against the module as the project's graphics folder holds it now.
163	- A number ramps along the curve and arrives with decimals, so 64 to 129 is 96.5 halfway. A module that needs a whole number rounds it.
164	- A colour blends in OKLab, with straight alpha.
165	- A string, a boolean and an enum switch to the end's value when the action ends.
166	- An image prop switches when the action ends. `""` names no image there.
167	- A prop the clip holds no value for starts from the module's current default, written into the clip in the same undo step.
168	- `graphic.props.<key>: null` removes that prop from the end, and `graphic: null` removes the whole group.
169	
170	`get_project` shows `kinds` beside `props`. Frame Job writes that and ignores any you send, so an end you read back can be sent again.
171	
172	**When it refuses.**
173	
174	- A prop its module marks `animate: false` is refused. Set it with `set_graphic`.
175	- `name`, `width`, `height`, `in` and `length` are refused: an action animates `graphic.props` only.
176	- While the module is missing or doesn't compile, a value is refused, and `get_graphic` says why. A `null` still removes.
177	- On a clip that isn't a graphic: "clip 7 is not a graphic clip".
178	
179	### Speed in an action
180	
181	`speed`, a number beside the groups, is a media clip's rate. The clip ramps to it along the curve, from the rate it's playing at when the action starts, and holds it after. It keeps its start and length, and plays more or less of its source. It mirrors the Speed section's **Rate** with an action selected. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).
182	
183	```json
184	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "speed": 3 } }
185	```
186	
187	The rate is clamped to ×0.1–×1000, and `speed: null` removes it.
188	
189	Above ×12 the clip's audio is left out, and the call that takes it there answers with `audio_left_out` (the clip ids) and `audio_note`. Captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are re-timed in the same step: `captions_retimed` lists them, and `captions_removed` lists those whose speech it no longer plays.
190	
191	**When it refuses.**
192	
193	- An end rate that would read past the end of the clip's media. The sentence names the largest end rate that fits, or, when none down to ×0.1 does, the latest clip end that fits at ×0.1.
194	- `speed: null` when the clip would then read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
195	- A value that isn't a number or `null`, or a clip that isn't a media clip.
196	- A rate on a linked clip: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
197	
198	### Switching off at an end
199	
200	`off` turns an optional property off at the end of the action. The path is stored as a `null` in the end state, where a `null` in `patch` removes the key instead. So `off` means "this shadow goes away by the end", and a `null` in `patch` means "stop animating the shadow".
201	
202	```json
203	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": {}, "off": ["video.shadow", "audio.eq.band_2"] }
204	```
205	
206	- A path is `"group.key"`, with a group of `video`, `audio` or `text` and one of its top-level keys, such as `video.shadow`, `text.width` or `audio.limiter`.
207	- One deeper path exists: `audio.eq.<slot>` switches that EQ slot off. The slots are `high_pass`, `low_shelf`, `band_1`, `band_2`, `band_3`, `high_shelf` and `low_pass`.
208	- Only optional keys can go off. A required key such as `video.opacity` is refused.
209	- A path can't also be named in `patch`.
210	- `graphic` paths are refused: name the value a prop ends at in `patch`.
211	- `video.cutout` is refused: `set_video` with `{cutout: null}` removes a cutout.
212	- `video.motion`, `video.hide_silent` and `text.words` are refused here too.
213	
214	## `remove_action`
215	
216	Removes an action. The clip keeps its base properties. It mirrors the action lane's trash button and <kbd>⌫</kbd> with an action selected. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
217	
218	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
219	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
220	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
221	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
222	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
223	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
224	
225	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. When the action named a speed, captions are re-timed in the same step, with `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed` as for `set_action`.
226	
227	**When it refuses.**
228	
229	- Removing a speed action when the clip would then read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
230	- Removing a speed action from a linked clip: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
231	- An action id the clip doesn't have is an error.

241	=================== mcp/tools-speed
242	---
243	title: "Tools: speed and time"
244	description: "The agent tools that change a clip's speed, ramp it, retime a stretch of the timeline, play a clip backwards and hold a frame, with their arguments, answers and limits."
245	---
246	
247	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
248	
249	These tools change how time passes in a clip: its rate, a ramp between rates, a whole stretch of the timeline played faster or slower, the direction it plays, and a held frame.
250	
251	<AtAGlance tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range', 'set_reversed', 'freeze_frame']} />
252	
253	## Pick a tool
254	
255	| You want to | Use |
256	| --- | --- |
257	| Play one clip at a rate, or fit it to a length | [`set_speed`](#set_speed) |
258	| Make a clip end at a time by changing its speed | [`rate_stretch`](#rate_stretch) |
259	| Ease a clip from one rate to another | [`add_speed_ramp`](#add_speed_ramp) |
260	| Play a stretch of the whole timeline faster or slower | [`retime_range`](#retime_range) |
261	| Play a clip backwards | [`set_reversed`](#set_reversed) |
262	| Hold one frame | [`freeze_frame`](#freeze_frame) |
263	
264	## What these tools share
265	
266	- **Times** are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
267	- **One call is one undo step.**
268	- **The answer** is `ok: true`, the ids of anything created, and a `project` summary. A call that changes nothing says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
269	- **Rates** run from ×0.1 to ×1000, where 1 is normal speed. See each tool for what it does with a rate outside that.
270	
271	### Above ×12 the sound is left out
272	
273	A clip playing above ×12 is silent in the preview and the export, with or without keep pitch. A person is asked first. A tool call never asks: the edit lands, and the answer gains two keys. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
274	
275	| Key | What it holds |
276	| --- | --- |
277	| `audio_left_out` | The ids of the clips this edit took past ×12. |
278	| `audio_note` | A sentence saying those clips are now silent. |
279	
280	Only a clip with its sound on, using a file that has sound, counts, and only when this edit took it over the line. A clip already above ×12 isn't reported again. On a ramped clip, the fastest rate in the ramp is the one that counts.
281	
282	### Captions move with the speech
283	
284	`set_speed`, `rate_stretch` and `add_speed_ramp` re-time captions on a Captions track that lie wholly inside a clip with sound, in the same undo step, whose name gains "and Re-time Captions". See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
285	
286	| Key | What it holds |
287	| --- | --- |
288	| `captions_retimed` | The caption clips that moved. |
289	| `captions_removed` | The caption clips whose speech the clip no longer plays. |
290	
291	### Linked clips
292	
293	A clip linked to its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) can't change speed or direction, because the other half would have to change with it. `set_speed`, `rate_stretch`, `add_speed_ramp`, `set_reversed` and `retime_range` all stop with "clip 12 is linked to clip 13: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction". Call [`attach_audio`](/mcp/tools-audio/#attach_audio) first.
294	
295	## `set_speed`
296	
297	Changes a clip's playback rate, or fits it to a length. The clip keeps its start and its length follows the rate, so a faster clip can leave a gap after it. Later clips don't move.
298	
299	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Speed…**. See [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/). With `duration` it mirrors **Fit to** in the Speed section. See [Fit a clip to a length](/speed/fit-to-duration/).
300	
301	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
302	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
303	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to change. |
304	| `rate` | number | One of `rate` or `duration` | 1 is normal, 2 twice as fast and half as long, 0.5 slow motion. From 0.1 to 1000. |
305	| `duration` | integer, ticks | One of `rate` or `duration` | The length to fit the clip to, instead of a rate. |
306	| `keep_pitch` | boolean | No | Keep the sound's pitch at the new speed. Left out, the clip's setting stays. |
307	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
308	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
309	
310	A rate outside ×0.1 to ×1000 is brought inside that range, not turned down. That goes for the rate a `duration` needs too, so a clip can end up a different length from the one you asked for. The new length lands on the frame grid and never runs past what the file holds at that rate. Actions keep their place, as fractions of the clip's length.
311	
312	On a clip with a speed ramp, every rate in the ramp scales together, so it keeps its shape. The scale stops where any of its rates would pass the limits, so the clip's rate can stop short of the one you asked for. See [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/).
313	
314	**Answers** the usual keys, with `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`, and `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed`, when they apply. The undo step is named Speed.
315	
316	**Won't run** when:
317	
318	- Both or neither of `rate` and `duration` are given, which is an error. So `keep_pitch` can't be sent alone.
319	- The clip isn't a video or audio file clip. Text, shapes, images, stills, graphics and nests are errors.
320	- `rate` or `duration` is zero or negative, which is an error. A `duration` that rounds to zero on the frame grid counts as zero.
321	- The clip is [linked](#linked-clips).
322	- A slowed clip would run into the next clip by more than the [overlap rule](/speed/change-speed/#a-slowed-clip-overlapping-the-next) allows. An overlap the rule allows gets a transition.
323	
324	## `rate_stretch`
325	
326	Makes a clip end at a new time by changing its speed instead of trimming it. Everything the clip shows still plays, faster or slower.
327	
328	It mirrors <kbd>⌥</kbd>-dragging a clip's end edge. See [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/).
329	
330	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
331	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
332	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to stretch. |
333	| `to_end` | integer, ticks | Yes | The clip's new end on the timeline. |
334	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
335	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
336	
337	Actions keep their place, as fractions of the clip's length. A speed ramp on the clip scales with it and keeps its shape.
338	
339	**Answers** the usual keys, with `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`, and `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed`, when they apply. The undo step is named Rate Stretch.
340	
341	**Changes nothing** when the new length would be under one frame, or the stretch would take any rate past ×0.1 or ×1000. Unlike a drag, it doesn't stop at the last length that worked.
342	
343	**Won't run** when:
344	
345	- The clip isn't a video or audio file clip. A text, shape, image or freeze clip has no source to stretch, which is an error.
346	- The clip is [linked](#linked-clips).
347	- The stretch would run into the next clip by more than the overlap rule allows.
348	
349	## `add_speed_ramp`
350	
351	Makes a speed ramp preset on a clip in one step, out of ordinary speed actions. The clip keeps its start and length, and plays more or less of its source.
352	
353	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**, but it isn't tied to the in and out range. See [Make a ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/).
354	
355	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
356	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
357	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to ramp. |
358	| `shape` | string | Yes | `ramp_up`, `ramp_down`, `speed_dip` or `speed_burst`. |
359	| `rate` | number | Yes | The rate to ramp to, from 0.1 to 1000. Outside that it's brought inside. Zero or less is an error. |
360	| `from` | integer, ticks | No | Where the span starts, measured from the clip's own start. Give it with `to`. |
361	| `to` | integer, ticks | No | Where the span ends, in clip time. Give it with `from`. With neither, the span is the whole clip. |
362	| `curve` | string | No | How each new action eases: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. Default `ease_in_out`. |
363	| `hold` | number | No | `speed_dip` and `speed_burst` only: how much of the span the hold at `rate` takes, from 0 to 0.9. Outside that it's brought inside. Default 0.5. 0 makes the two ramps meet. |
364	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
365	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
366	
367	The base rate is the rate the clip plays at `from` before the edit. After an earlier speed action, that's the action's end rate.
368	
369	| `shape` | What it makes | `rate` must be |
370	| --- | --- | --- |
371	| `ramp_up` | One action over the span, from the base rate to `rate`, which then holds. | Above the base rate |
372	| `ramp_down` | The same, slowing down. | Below the base rate |
373	| `speed_burst` | Two actions: up to `rate` at the start of the span and back to the base rate at its end, holding `rate` between them. | Above the base rate |
374	| `speed_dip` | The same two, slowing down and coming back. | Below the base rate |
375	
376	**Answers** `clip`, `new_actions` with the new actions' ids, and `audio_left_out`, `audio_note`, `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed` when they apply. The undo step is named for the shape, such as Speed Dip.
377	
378	**Errors** come first, and name the argument:
379	
380	- The clip isn't a video or audio file clip.
381	- Only one of `from` and `to` is given, `to` isn't after `from`, or `from` is negative.
382	- `hold` is given with `ramp_up` or `ramp_down`.
383	
384	**Won't run** in these cases, checked in this order. Each message says why:
385	
386	| What stops it | What to do |
387	| --- | --- |
388	| The span runs past the clip's end. | Shorten the span. |
389	| The span overlaps an action on the clip, including one that would sit inside a dip's or burst's hold. The message names it, and it's never replaced. | Pick a clear span, or move or remove the action. |
390	| A dip or burst span is under two frames. | Widen the span. |
391	| `rate` is on the wrong side of the base rate. The message gives the base rate. | Change `rate` or `shape`. |
392	| The clip is [linked](#linked-clips). | Call `attach_audio` first. |
393	| The clip would read past the end of its media. The message names the largest rate that fits, or says none does. | Use that rate, or shorten the span. |
394	
395	## `retime_range`
396	
397	Plays a stretch of the timeline faster or slower on every unlocked track, and moves everything after it up or back to stay in step.
398	
399	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Retime Range…**, but it takes its own times and doesn't read the in and out range. See [Retime a range](/speed/retime-range/).
400	
401	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
402	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
403	| `from` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range starts. |
404	| `to` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range ends. It must be after `from` once both are on the frame grid. |
405	| `rate` | number | Yes | 2 is twice as fast and the range half as long, 0.5 half speed. From 0.1 to 1000. |
406	| `keep_pitch` | boolean | No | Keep the sound's pitch at the new speed for every video and audio file clip in the range. Left out, each stays as it is. |
407	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
408	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
409	
410	Each clip across `from` or `to` is cut there, as [`split`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split) cuts it. Each video or audio file clip inside plays at its own rate times `rate`, and a speed ramp scales whole. Text, shapes, stills, images, graphics and adjustment clips inside are stretched or squeezed the same way. Actions keep their place. Markers inside move with the picture, markers after it move with the rest, and a linked partner of a moved clip moves with it.
411	
412	Inside a nest, the nest's own tracks are retimed and no marker moves. Unlike `set_speed`, `rate_stretch` and `add_speed_ramp`, it doesn't re-time captions on a Captions track, and it stops at a caption page with timed words. A `rate` of 1 changes nothing.
413	
414	**Answers** `new_clips`, the pieces the cuts made, and `audio_left_out` and `audio_note` when a clip crosses ×12. The undo step is named Retime Range.
415	
416	**Errors:** `to` isn't after `from`, or `rate` is missing, zero or negative.
417	
418	**Won't run** in these cases, and nothing changes. A clip only has to overlap the range to count.
419	
420	| What stops it | What to do |
421	| --- | --- |
422	| `rate` is outside ×0.1 to ×1000. This one isn't brought inside the range. | Pick a rate inside it. |
423	| The range is under two frames. | Widen the range. |
424	| A locked track has a clip that ends after `from`. | Unlock the track, or move `from` past that clip. |
425	| The range touches a nest clip. | Move the range off it, or retime inside the nest. |
426	| The range touches a caption page with timed words. | Move the range off it. |
427	| The range touches a [linked](#linked-clips) clip. | Call `attach_audio` first. |
428	| A transition touches the range. | Move the range off it, or remove the transition. |
429	| Two markers would land on one time. | Move one of them first. |
430	| A clip would play past ×0.1 or ×1000. The message names the clip and the rate. | Pick a gentler rate, or set the clip's own speed first. |
431	| A clip would last under one frame. The message names it. | Pick a gentler rate. |
432	
433	## `set_reversed`
434	
435	Plays a clip back to front, or forward again. It isn't a toggle: you say which way it plays.
436	
437	It mirrors the **Reverse** checkbox in the Clip tab's Timing section. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/).
438	
439	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
440	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
441	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to change. |
442	| `reversed` | boolean | Yes | True plays it backwards, false forwards again. |
443	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
444	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
445	
446	Nothing on the timeline moves. The clip keeps its start, its length and its in point, and the in point is measured in the direction the clip plays, so reversing a trimmed clip shows the other end of the file.
447	
448	:::caution
449	A clip plays backwards from a rendered copy of its file. In a project with a window, the Reversing sheet appears to make the copy the first time. Until the copy exists the clip shows a [slate](/speed/reverse/#the-slate), and an export writes the slate. A project open with no window shows no sheet and starts no render, so its reversed clips stay on the slate until the project is opened in a window.
450	:::
451	
452	**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`. The undo step is named Reverse. A clip already playing that way changes nothing.
453	
454	**Won't run** when the clip isn't a video or audio file clip, which is an error, or when it's [linked](#linked-clips).
455	
456	## `freeze_frame`
457	
458	Holds one frame. The clip is split at the moment, a gap opens across every unlocked track, and a still of that exact frame fills it, so the rest of the cut stays in step.
459	
460	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Freeze Frame** (<kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd>), but it can hold any moment of a clip without moving the playhead, for any length. See [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/).
461	
462	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
463	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
464	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to freeze. |
465	| `at` | integer, ticks | No | The moment to hold, on the timeline. Left out, the playhead. |
466	| `duration` | integer, ticks | No | How long to hold, at least one frame. Default 2 s, which is 1200000. |
467	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
468	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
469	
470	The still takes the clip's picture settings as they stand at that moment. It has no sound, no actions and no entrance or exit motion. Markers at or after `at` move with the gap. At a clip's very start or end there's nothing to split, and the still goes in without a cut. To change the frame a freeze holds afterwards, use [`slip`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#slip) on it.
471	
472	**Answers** `new_clips`, which holds the still, and the clip's second piece when there was a split. The undo step is named Freeze Frame.
473	
474	**Won't run** when:
475	
476	- The clip isn't a video file clip with a picture, which is an error. An audio-only clip, text, a shape, an image, a graphic, a nest or another still can't be frozen.
477	- The clip doesn't cover `at`, which is an error.
478	- `duration` comes to under one frame on the frame grid, which is an error.
479	- The still would break the overlap rule. This happens inside a [transition](/motion/transitions/) and on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/), whose clips can't move out of the still's way.

488	=================== mcp/tools-transitions
489	---
490	title: "Tools: transitions"
491	description: Make a transition at a hard cut from an agent, change its kind, length and easing, crossfade the sound, or remove it.
492	---
493	
494	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
495	
496	A [transition](/motion/transitions/) plays across the overlap between a clip and the clip before it on the same track, and it belongs to the later clip. Its length is that overlap. These tools make the overlap, choose the transition, and set how it eases and sounds.
497	
498	<AtAGlance
499	  tools={['add_transition', 'set_transition', 'set_transition_duration', 'set_transition_style']}
500	  menu="Clip ▸ Transition ▸"
501	  where="Clip tab ▸ Transition section"
502	/>
503	
504	Start with `add_transition` at a hard cut. Use `set_transition` and `set_transition_duration` on clips that already overlap.
505	
506	Every time here is in ticks, 600,000 to the second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). `ripple` and `audio` take `true` or `false`, or those words or `"1"` and `"0"` as strings.
507	
508	The kinds are `cross_dissolve`, `fade_black`, `fade_white`, `push_left`, `push_right`, `push_up`, `push_down`, `wipe`, `slide`, `zoom`, `wipe_left`, `wipe_up` and `wipe_down`. See [Transition styles](/motion/transition-styles/).
509	
510	An adjustment clip can't take a transition or overlap another clip, so these tools refuse one, and `set_transition` with `kind: null` is the only call that goes through. Fade it with opacity instead. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
511	
512	## `add_transition`
513	
514	Makes an overlap at the hard cut before a clip and puts a transition on it. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** on a clip that butts up against the one before it. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/).
515	
516	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
517	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
518	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The incoming clip's id. |
519	| `duration` | integer | Yes | The overlap you want. It can land shorter, but it's never refused for being too long. |
520	| `kind` | string | No | The transition. Left out, it's the clip's stored kind, else `cross_dissolve`. It can't be `null`: `set_transition` clears one. |
521	| `align` | string | No | Which side the overlap comes out of: `center`, the default, `before` or `after`. Ignored with `ripple`. |
522	| `ripple` | boolean or string | No | `true` makes the overlap by sliding the incoming clip and everything after it left, for two clips with no footage beyond the cut. The default is `false`. |
523	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
524	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
525	
526	```json
527	{ "clip": 15, "duration": 600000, "kind": "fade_black" }
528	```
529	
530	**How the overlap is made.** It's built from material the two clips already have: the source before the incoming clip's in point, and after the outgoing clip's out point. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and the pair's outer edges stay where they were.
531	
532	| `align` | Where the overlap comes from |
533	| --- | --- |
534	| `center` | Half from each side. An odd frame goes to the incoming clip, and a side with nothing to give passes its share to the other. |
535	| `before` | All from the incoming clip's head. |
536	| `after` | All from the outgoing clip's tail. |
537	
538	`duration` rounds to the nearest frame. It's then held to each side's spare material, to the neighbours on the track and to the [overlap rules](/motion/transitions/#the-overlap-rules), so a request too long for the media lands shorter. A nest clip has no spare head, and its tail ends at the nest's own length.
539	
540	A stored transition keeps its curve and crossfade. A new one eases at both ends and crossfades its sound. The incoming clip's actions move with its new first frame, so a zoom stays on the source frame it was drawn over.
541	
542	**With `ripple: true`.** This is the sheet's **Shift Clips Left** button, for when neither clip has footage beyond the cut. No material is read and `align` is ignored. The incoming clip and every clip at or after the cut, on every unlocked track, slide left by `duration`, so the timeline gets that much shorter and every clip keeps its in and out points.
543	
544	- The shift is capped at half the shorter of the two clips.
545	- It's also limited to the largest whole-frame shift that leaves every moved track within the overlap rules.
546	- A clip on another track pushed into its neighbour gets a `cross_dissolve`.
547	- Markers don't move.
548	
549	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
550	
551	**When it refuses.**
552	
553	- A `duration` that isn't positive once it's rounded to the frame grid is an error.
554	- A clip not at a hard cut is an error naming which of three: it's the first clip on its track, there's a gap before it, or it already overlaps a clip. For that last one, use `set_transition` or `set_transition_duration`.
555	- A cut with no room: nothing is left once the request is held to the two clips' spare material, their neighbours and the overlap rules. The sentence suggests `ripple: true`.
556	- A track that already breaks the overlap rules is refused before any shortening.
557	- With `ripple`: an incoming clip on a locked track, or clips with no room to overlap by shifting.
558	
559	## `set_transition`
560	
561	Sets the transition into a clip, or removes it. It mirrors the **Kind** pop-up in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
562	
563	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
564	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
565	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
566	| `kind` | string or null | Yes | The transition, or `null` to remove it. |
567	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
568	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
569	
570	The transition's length is the clip's overlap with the one before it, so a clip with no overlap ignores it until it has one. Make an overlap with `move_clip` or `set_transition_duration`. Changing the kind keeps the transition's curve and crossfade. A new one eases at both ends and crossfades its sound.
571	
572	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
573	
574	**When it refuses.** A missing `kind`, or a value that isn't one of the thirteen or `null`, is an error listing them.
575	
576	## `set_transition_duration`
577	
578	Makes a transition last `duration` by moving the clip, so its overlap with the clip before it equals that. It mirrors the **Duration** field in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
579	
580	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
581	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
582	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
583	| `duration` | integer | Yes | The overlap length, rounded to the frame grid. |
584	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
585	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
586	
587	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
588	
589	**When it refuses.**
590	
591	- On a track's first clip, which has nothing to overlap.
592	- Past half the shorter clip, snapped down. The sentence names that limit in ticks.
593	- A `duration` that isn't positive is an error. To clear a transition, use `set_transition` with `kind: null`.
594	
595	## `set_transition_style`
596	
597	Sets how a transition is eased, whether it crossfades the two clips' sound, and the crossfade's shape. It mirrors the **Curve** pop-up, the **Crossfade Audio** checkbox and the **Crossfade Shape** pop-up in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
598	
599	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
600	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
601	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
602	| `curve` | string | No | How the transition's progress is eased: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. |
603	| `audio` | boolean or string | No | Crossfades the two clips' sound across the overlap. |
604	| `audio_shape` | string | No | The crossfade's curve. See the table below. |
605	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
606	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
607	
608	| `audio_shape` | The curve, over the eased progress p |
609	| --- | --- |
610	| `plus_3db` | The default, constant power: sine in, cosine out. It holds the level across two unrelated takes, where a straight-line pair dips 3 dB. |
611	| `linear` | p in, 1 − p out. |
612	| `s_curve` | A slow start and a slow finish. |
613	| `minus_3db` | A slow start, rising fastest at the end. |
614	
615	The outgoing clip takes the shape of 1 − p.
616	
617	A key you leave out keeps what's there, so changing the curve never touches the crossfade, and the other way round.
618	
619	The tool writes onto any clip, with or without an overlap. A stored transition on a clip with no overlap isn't drawn until there is one. A clip with no transition at all gets a `cross_dissolve` with the style applied.
620	
621	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
622	
623	**When it refuses.** With none of the three keys, the call is an error naming them.
624

1	=================== speed/overview
2	---
3	title: "Speed at a glance"
4	description: "The ways to change a clip's time in Frame Job, which clips each one works on, and the rate and sound limits that apply."
5	---
6	
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Frame Job can play a video or audio clip faster or slower, change its speed over time, play it backwards and hold one of its frames. This page shows which tool fits the job and what limits apply to all of them.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…', 'Clip ▸ Retime Range…']}
13	  keys="⌥-drag"
14	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Speed section"
15	  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range']}
16	/>
17	
18	## Pick the right tool
19	
20	| You want to | Use | What happens on the timeline |
21	| --- | --- | --- |
22	| Play a clip at one new speed | [Clip ▸ Speed…](/speed/change-speed/) or **Rate** in the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/) | The clip's start stays and its length changes. Later clips don't move. |
23	| Make a clip last an exact length | [Fit to](/speed/fit-to-duration/) | The rate changes so the clip plays in the length you type. |
24	| Stretch a clip by eye | [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/), <kbd>⌥</kbd>-dragging its end edge | The clip gets longer or shorter and still plays the same source. |
25	| Speed up and slow down inside a clip | A [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) | The clip keeps its place and length, and plays more or less of its file. |
26	| Speed up or slow down a stretch of the whole timeline | [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | Every unlocked track changes together, and what follows moves up or back. |
27	| Speed up the typing in a screen recording | [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) | Only the stretches of typing change. |
28	| Play a clip backwards | [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) | Nothing on the timeline moves. |
29	| Hold one frame still | [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | A still clip fills a gap opened at the playhead. |
30	
31	A rate is a multiple of normal speed: ×1 is normal, ×2 is twice as fast and half as long, and ×0.5 is half speed.
32	
33	Sound follows the [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) setting, which is on for a new clip.
34	
35	## Which clips take speed
36	
37	Speed works on **media clips**, meaning clips of a video or audio file. Other clips have no source to speed up. Retime Range is the one exception.
38	
39	| Clip | Speed…, Fit to, rate stretch, Speed Ramp…, Reverse and Freeze Frame | Retime Range… |
40	| --- | --- | --- |
41	| A video or audio file | Yes | Yes |
42	| A still image, a freeze frame, text, a shape or an adjustment clip | No | Stretched or squeezed with the range |
43	| A graphic | No. Its timing comes from its module and its **Length**. | Stretched or squeezed, and it keeps its **Length** |
44	| A nest | No | Frame Job won't retime a range with a nest in it. Move the range off the nest, or retime inside it. |
45	| A caption page with timed words | No | Frame Job won't retime a range with one in it. Move the range off it. |
46	
47	When a selection mixes clip kinds, each command treats it differently:
48	
49	- **Clip ▸ Speed…** is available when the selection holds at least one media clip. It opens on those clips and skips the rest. With none selected it's dimmed.
50	- **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** is available only with exactly one media clip selected.
51	- The **Speed** section appears only when every selected clip is a media clip.
52	- With several clips selected, the **Timing** section, which holds **Reverse**, also appears only when every one is a media clip.
53	- <kbd>⌥</kbd>-dragging the end edge of any other clip is an ordinary trim.
54	
55	### Linked clips
56	
57	After [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/), a picture and its sound are linked. Frame Job won't change a linked clip's rate or direction, or give it a Speed action, until you attach it again. The foot of the inspector shows the reason, for example "clip 4 is linked to clip 7: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction". A rate stretch on a linked clip doesn't move and shows no reason.
58	
59	**Keep pitch** isn't a rate, so you can still change it on a linked clip.
60	
61	## Rate range
62	
63	A clip can play anywhere from ×0.1 to ×1000. What happens when you ask for more depends on where you ask.
64	
65	| Where | A rate past a limit |
66	| --- | --- |
67	| The **Speed**, **Speed Ramp** and **Retime Range** sheets | The field won't take it. Each sheet prints ×0.1 – ×1000 beside its buttons. |
68	| **Rate** in the Speed section | It's set to the nearest limit. |
69	| **Fit to** | The rate stops at the limit, so the clip ends up a different length from the one you typed. |
70	| A rate stretch | The clip stops following the drag at the last length inside the limits. |
71	
72	## Limits at a glance
73	
74	| Limit | Value |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| Slowest rate | ×0.1 |
77	| Fastest rate | ×1000 |
78	| Fastest rate that still has sound | ×12, with Keep pitch on or off |
79	| Freeze frame length when none is given | 2 s |
80	
81	What else to expect:
82	
83	- **Above ×12** the picture plays and the sound is left out of the preview and the export. Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip with sound past ×12. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
84	- **On a ramped clip**, one rate above ×12 anywhere in the ramp silences the whole clip.
85	- **A speed ramp** never changes the clip's start or length. Frame Job won't make an edit that would play the clip past the end of its file.
86	- **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** works on one clip at a time, and offers the **Ease In Out** and **Linear** curves and four hold values.
87	- **Rendered sound.** A ramp is silent in the preview until its sound has been rendered. So is a clip at any constant speed but ×1 with Keep pitch off. See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/#tape-pitch-is-rendered-in-the-background) and [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/).
88	- **After a steep slow-down** with Keep pitch on, a ramp's sound can lag the picture by up to about 24 ms.
89	- **A reversed clip** shows a slate until its backwards copy has been rendered.
90	- **Synchronize Audio** doesn't take clips that are reversed, ramped, or more than 0.2% away from ×1. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).
91	
92	## With an agent
93	
94	`set_speed`, `add_speed_ramp` and a speed in `set_action_end` bring a rate past a limit to that limit. `retime_range` is the exception: it won't take a rate outside ×0.1 to ×1000. `set_speed`, `add_speed_ramp` and `retime_range` don't accept a rate of zero or less.
95	
96	Asking for a speed on anything but a media clip is an error, "clip 12 is not a media clip", so the agent can correct the call.
97	
98	`add_speed_ramp` can also use any action curve and any hold from 0 to 0.9, which is more than the sheet offers. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
99	
100	## Related
101	
102	- [Limits](/reference/limits/)
103	- [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/)
104	- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
105	- [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/)

107	---
108	title: "Change a clip's speed"
109	description: "Use the Speed sheet to play selected clips faster or slower, see the new length before you apply it, and know what the change does to the clips around them."
110	---
111	
112	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
113	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
114	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
115	
116	The Speed sheet plays the selected clips at one new constant rate, and shows you the length that results before you apply it.
117	
118	<AtAGlance
119	  menu="Clip ▸ Speed…"
120	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Speed section"
121	  tools="set_speed"
122	/>
123	
124	## Set a new speed
125	
126	<Steps>
127	
128	1. Select one or more clips of a video or audio file.
129	
130	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed…**. The item has no keyboard shortcut.
131	
132	3. Type a **Rate**, or pick one from **Presets**.
133	
134	4. Read the [readout](#the-readout) under the controls. It updates when you pick a preset, change **Preserve pitch** or leave the **Rate** field.
135	
136	5. Choose **Apply**.
137	
138	</Steps>
139	
140	**Clip ▸ Speed…** is available when the selection holds at least one media clip, meaning a clip of a video or audio file. Clips of other kinds in the selection are skipped. See [Which clips take speed](/speed/overview/#which-clips-take-speed).
141	
142	To change one rate without opening a sheet, use **Rate** in the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/).
143	
144	## The Speed sheet
145	
146	<Shot
147	  name="13-speed-sheet.sheet"
148	  alt="The Speed sheet. A paragraph explains that faster clips can leave gaps and slower clips can overlap. Below it are a Rate field holding 1 with a Presets pull-down, a ticked Preserve pitch box, and the readout 1 clip, 00:00:05:07 to 00:00:05:07. The range ×0.1 – ×1000 sits beside Cancel and Apply."
149	/>
150	
151	| Control | What it does | Default |
152	| --- | --- | --- |
153	| **Rate:** | The playback rate as a number: 1 is normal, 2 is twice as fast, 0.5 is half speed. It takes up to three decimal places, and the field won't accept a value outside ×0.1 – ×1000, the range printed beside the sheet's buttons. | The rate the selected clips share, or ×1 if they differ |
154	| **Presets** | Fills in **Rate** with 0.25×, 0.50×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×, 10× or 100×. The same list appears on the [Speed Ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/) and [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) sheets. | |
155	| **Preserve pitch** | Keeps the sound at its own pitch at the new speed. Turn it off and the pitch rises and falls with the speed, like tape. See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/). | The first selected clip's setting, which is on for a new clip |
156	
157	## The readout
158	
159	Frame Job tries the change before you commit to it, so the readout shows what **Apply** will do:
160	
161	- The clip count and the total length before and after, for example `3 clips · 00:00:12:00 → 00:00:06:00`.
162	- One line for each clip whose transition starts playing, gets longer or gets shorter:
163	  - `clip 7 gains a 0.67 s cross dissolve`
164	  - `clip 7's cross dissolve grows to 1.50 s`
165	  - `clip 7's cross dissolve shrinks to 0.67 s`
166	- When a selected clip has a speed ramp, "Each speed ramp keeps its shape: the rates it names scale with the base rate."
167	
168	A clip that couldn't take the new rate counts at its old length, and the rest of the selection still counts.
169	
170	## Apply the change
171	
172	**Apply** sets the rate on every listed clip as one undo step, **Set Speed**. Captions the change re-times are part of the same step, which is then named **Set Speed and Re-time Captions**. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
173	
174	If nothing would change, **Apply** closes the sheet and adds no undo step.
175	
176	If the rate takes a clip with sound above ×12, an alert comes first, such as "“interview.mov” will be silent at ×20."
177	
178	- **Set Speed** closes the sheet and applies the change.
179	- **Cancel** leaves the sheet up with nothing applied.
180	
181	See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
182	
183	## What a speed change does
184	
185	- **The clip's start stays and its length changes.** A faster clip can leave a gap after it, and later clips don't move up to fill it. [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) closes it.
186	- **The new length snaps to a whole frame**, and never runs past the end of the file at the new rate. See [The new length](/speed/fit-to-duration/#the-new-length).
187	- **Actions keep their places** as fractions of the clip's length.
188	- **On a ramped clip** the sheet sets the clip's own rate, its base rate, and scales the whole ramp with it. See [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/).
189	
190	A speed ramp works the other way round: it leaves the clip where it is and changes how much of the source plays.
191	
192	## A slowed clip overlapping the next
193	
194	A slower clip gets longer, so it can run into the clip after it. Later clips stay where they are, so the two now overlap.
195	
196	- **If the overlap is allowed**, the later clip gets a transition across it, and the readout names that transition.
197	- **If it isn't allowed**, the slowed clip keeps its old speed. Any other selected clips still change.
198	
199	An overlap is allowed up to half the length of the shorter clip. It isn't allowed when one of the clips is an adjustment clip, or when the clip would reach a second neighbour on the same side. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
200	
201	## Good to know
202	
203	- **Clips at different rates.** The field opens on ×1, and **Apply** sets every listed clip to the rate in the field, even if you only changed **Preserve pitch**. Choose **Cancel** to leave them at their own rates.
204	- **Preserve pitch** applies to every listed clip, and changing it alone counts as a change.
205	- **Linked clips.** Frame Job won't change the speed of a clip linked to its detached sound until you attach it. See [Linked clips](/speed/overview/#linked-clips).
206	- **Inside a nest**, the sheet works on the clips you've selected in the open nest.
207	
208	## With an agent
209	
210	`set_speed` does the same job, one clip at a time. Give it `clip` and exactly one of `rate` or `duration`, the length that [Fit to](/speed/fit-to-duration/) takes. Both or neither is an error, and so is a rate of zero or less. Leave out `keep_pitch` and the clip's setting stays as it is.
211	
212	An agent isn't asked about ×12: the reply says which clips lost their sound. Its undo step is named **Speed**. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
213	
214	## Related
