217	- [The Speed section](/speed/speed-section/)
218	- [Fit a clip to a length](/speed/fit-to-duration/)
219	- [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/)
220	- [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/)
221	- [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/)
222	=================== speed/speed-section
223	---
224	title: "The Speed section"
225	description: "Set a clip's rate, pitch and length in the inspector, and set the rate an action ends on to build a speed ramp."
226	---
227	
228	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
229	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
230	
231	The **Speed** section is the inspector's home for a clip's rate. With no action selected it changes the whole clip, and with an action selected its **Rate** sets the rate that action ends on.
232	
233	<AtAGlance
234	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Speed section"
235	  tools={['set_speed', 'set_action_end', 'set_audio']}
236	/>
237	
238	## Open the section
239	
240	Select one or more clips of a video or audio file, then open the **Clip** sub-tab of the **Clip** tab. The section appears only when every selected clip is a media clip, meaning a clip of a video or audio file. See [Which clips take speed](/speed/overview/#which-clips-take-speed).
241	
242	It starts collapsed, and its header shows the rate, for example `2.00×`. Click the header to open it. It opens by itself when the selected action sets a rate.
243	
244	| Row | What it does |
245	| --- | --- |
246	| **Rate** | The rate, from ×0.1 to ×1000. See [Set the rate](#set-the-rate). |
247	| **Keep pitch** | Whether the sound keeps its pitch at the new speed. See [Keep pitch](#keep-pitch). |
248	| **Fit to** | Type a length, and the rate changes so the clip plays in it. See [Fit a clip to a length](/speed/fit-to-duration/). |
249	| Note | "Audio is silent above ×12" appears when a selected clip with sound is past the [audio limit](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/). |
250	
251	## Set the rate
252	
253	Type a rate in **Rate**. The field shows two decimal places, and a value outside ×0.1 – ×1000 is set to the nearest limit. The change applies to every selected media clip as one undo step, **Set Speed**.
254	
255	When the selected clips differ, the row carries a **mixed** tag and shows the first clip's rate.
256	
257	If the change takes a clip with sound past ×12, Frame Job asks first, with **Set Speed** and **Cancel**. **Cancel** puts the field back.
258	
259	### Quick picks
260	
261	The chevron at the end of the **Rate** field opens a menu of **0.50×**, **1.00×**, **2.00×** and **4.00×**, with a check beside the current rate. With an action selected, a pick sets the action's end rate.
262	
263	## Keep pitch
264	
265	**Keep pitch** is the same setting as **Preserve pitch** in the Speed sheet, applied to every selected media clip as one undo step, **Keep Pitch**. See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) for what it does to the sound.
266	
267	:::caution
268	The checkbox also sets every selected media clip to the first selected clip's rate. Changing it across clips at different rates brings them all to that rate, and that can bring up the ×12 question.
269	:::
270	
271	## Reset the rate
272	
273	**Reset** in the section header sets the rate back to ×1, as one undo step, **Set Speed**. It leaves **Keep pitch** as it is.
274	
275	It appears when no action is selected and the first selected clip's rate isn't ×1. No Reset shows while an action is selected. To end an action at ×1, type 1 in **Rate** or pick **1.00×** from its quick-pick menu.
276	
277	## Rate inside an action
278	
279	While an action is selected, **Rate** shows and sets the rate that action ends on. Setting it turns any action into a Speed action, which is how you [build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).
280	
281	<Shot
282	  name="10d-clip-speed-action.inspector"
283	  alt="The Clip sub-tab with action 1 selected. The Speed section's header reads ◆1, 2.00× and a Clear button. The Rate row has a ◆ in its gutter, a field reading 2.00× and a now 1.50× figure after it. Keep pitch and Fit to are marked ⊘."
284	/>
285	
286	- If the action sets no rate, **Rate** shows the rate the clip is playing at the end of that action. Typing a different rate or picking one from the quick-pick menu sets it. Entering the rate already showing changes nothing.
287	- The header shows ◆1 and the end rate, with **Clear** in place of **Reset**.
288	- The **Rate** row carries a ◆ in its gutter. After the field, a "now" figure gives the rate under the playhead, for example `now 1.50×`, when the playhead is inside the clip and that rate differs from the end rate.
289	- Crossing ×12 asks first, as it does for the clip's own rate.
290	- Frame Job won't accept an end rate that would run the clip past the end of its file. The foot of the inspector names the largest rate that fits, or, if nothing down to ×0.1 fits, the latest clip end that would fit at ×0.1.
291	
292	You can only select an action with one clip selected. With several clips selected, **Rate** always sets each clip's own rate.
293	
294	When no action is selected, or the selected one sets no rate, a row that another action changes shows ◇ with the tooltip "Changed by action N". Right-click the row's label and choose **Go to action N** to select it.
295	
296	## Clear a rate from an action
297	
298	Clearing takes the rate out of the action. The action itself stays. Any of these does it:
299	
300	| Do this | Undo step |
301	| --- | --- |
302	| Choose **Clear** in the section header. It shows when the action sets a rate. | **Clear** |
303	| Hover over the **Rate** row and click the × that replaces its ◆. | **Remove from Action** |
304	| Right-click the row's label and choose **Remove from action N**. | **Remove from Action** |
305	
306	Frame Job won't clear the rate when the clip would then run past the end of its file. The foot of the inspector names the latest clip end that fits.
307	
308	## Rows that stay the clip's
309	
310	**Keep pitch** and **Fit to** change the clip itself even with an action selected, so they're marked ⊘ and never animate.
311	
312	- **Keep pitch** still sets the clip's own setting, at the clip's own rate.
313	- **Fit to** still changes the whole clip's rate. See [When Fit to is unavailable](/speed/fit-to-duration/#when-fit-to-is-unavailable).
314	
315	## With an agent
316	
317	`set_speed` sets a clip's rate and `set_audio` its **Keep pitch**. To set the rate an action ends on, `set_action_end` takes `speed` at the top of its `patch`, beside the groups, and brings it inside ×0.1 – ×1000. `speed: null` clears it. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/) and [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
318	
319	## Related
320

326	=================== speed/rate-stretch
327	---
328	title: "Rate stretch"
329	description: "Hold ⌥ and drag a clip's end edge to change its length by changing its speed, so it still plays everything it showed."
330	---
331	
332	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
333	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
334	
335	A rate stretch changes a clip's length by changing its speed, not by trimming it. The clip still plays all of the source it showed, faster or slower, so it's the quick way to make a shot fit by eye.
336	
337	<AtAGlance
338	  keys="⌥-drag"
339	  where="Timeline: a media clip's end edge"
340	  tools="rate_stretch"
341	/>
342	
343	## Stretch a clip
344	
345	<Steps>
346	
347	1. Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd>.
348	
349	2. Press on the **end** edge of a clip of a video or audio file, and drag. The timeline shows the result as you drag.
350	
351	3. Let go.
352	
353	</Steps>
354	
355	The stretch lands as one undo step, **Rate Stretch**. The new rate is the length of source the clip shows divided by its new length, so a 10 s clip at ×1 dragged to 5 s plays at ×2.
356	
357	Frame Job reads <kbd>⌥</kbd> when you press, so hold it before the drag starts. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on an edge is a [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/), not a stretch.
358	
359	Actions keep their fraction of the clip. Captions over the clip are re-timed in the same step, which is then named **Rate Stretch and Re-time Captions**, and they jump when you let go. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
360	
361	## Snapping
362	
363	A rate stretch snaps like any other edge drag. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> as you press to turn snapping off for that drag. See [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/).
364	
365	## Which edges and clips stretch
366	
367	| You drag with ⌥ | What happens |
368	| --- | --- |
369	| A media clip's end edge | A rate stretch |
370	| A clip's start edge | An ordinary trim |
371	| The end edge of a still, text, shape, graphic or any other clip | An ordinary trim, with the undo step **Trim Clip** |
372	| An edge on a locked track | Nothing. The edge doesn't move. |
373	| The end edge of a clip linked to its detached sound | Nothing, until you [attach it](/audio/detach-and-attach/) |
374	
375	## Where a stretch stops
376	
377	The clip stops following the drag when the next step would break a limit, and it lands at the last length that worked:
378	
379	- **Rate limits.** The stretch can't need a rate outside ×0.1 – ×1000.
380	- **One frame.** The clip can't get shorter than one frame.
381	- **The next clip.** A stretch into the next clip follows the same [overlap rule](/speed/change-speed/#a-slowed-clip-overlapping-the-next) as any slowed clip, so the later clip gains a transition across an allowed overlap.
382	
383	Drag back inside the limit and the clip follows you again.
384	
385	## A ramped clip
386	
387	On a clip with a speed ramp, the whole ramp stretches with the clip and keeps its shape. The stretch stops where any of its rates would pass the limits. See [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/).
388	
389	## Stretching past ×12
390	
391	If a stretch takes a clip with sound past ×12, Frame Job puts the stretch back and asks first.
392	
393	- **Set Speed** applies the stretch you made.
394	- **Cancel** leaves the clip as it was.
395	
396	See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
397	
398	## With an agent
399	
400	`rate_stretch` takes `clip` and `to_end`, the clip's new end on the timeline, and both are required. A text, shape, image or freeze clip is an error. The reply's `captions_retimed` lists the captions that moved, and `captions_removed` those whose speech the clip no longer plays. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
401	
402	## Related
403	
404	- [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/)
405	- [Fit a clip to a length](/speed/fit-to-duration/)
406	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
407	- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
408	=================== speed/fit-to-duration
409	---
410	title: "Fit a clip to a length"
411	description: "Type the length you want and Frame Job works out the rate, so a clip plays in exactly that time."
412	---
413	
414	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
415	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
416	
417	**Fit to** makes a clip last the length you type, by changing its speed rather than trimming it. Use it to fill a gap or to land a clip on a beat, without working out the rate yourself.
418	
419	<AtAGlance
420	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Speed section ▸ Fit to"
421	  tools="set_speed"
422	/>
423	
424	## Fit a clip
425	
426	<Steps>
427	
428	1. Select one or more clips of a video or audio file.
429	
430	2. In the **Clip** tab's **Clip** sub-tab, open the **Speed** section.
431	
432	3. Type a length in **Fit to**, then press <kbd>Return</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>. The tooltip reads "Type a length: the rate changes so the clip plays in it".
433	
434	</Steps>
435	
436	The field takes a timecode such as `00:00:12:15` or `00:00:12.500`, a shorter form such as `01:30`, or a number of seconds such as `12.5`. Text that isn't a time beeps, and the field goes back to the clip's length.
437	
438	With several clips selected, each one is fitted to that length, as one undo step, **Fit to Duration**. Captions the change re-times are part of the same step, which is then named **Fit to Duration and Re-time Captions**.
439	
440	The field shows the first selected clip's length, with a **mixed** tag when the selected clips' lengths differ.
441	
442	Fit to lives only in the inspector. The Speed sheet has no Fit to control.
443	
444	## The new length
445	
446	The length you type snaps to the frame grid. A length that snaps to zero or less shows an error and changes nothing. Typing the clip's current length changes nothing.
447	
448	The same applies to any speed change: the clip's new length snaps to a whole frame, and never runs past the end of its file at the new rate.
449	
450	The rate is still held to ×0.1 – ×1000. A length that needs a rate past a limit stops at that limit, so the clip ends up a different length from the one you typed. For example, a 10 s clip at ×1 fitted to 200 s stops at ×0.1 and lasts 100 s.
451	
452	On a clip with a speed ramp, Fit to scales the whole ramp. It stops where any rate in the ramp would pass a limit, and the clip ends up a different length in the same way. See [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/).
453	
454	Everything else works as it does for any speed change:
455	
456	- The clip's start stays where it is, and later clips don't move.
457	- A fit that runs into the next clip follows the [overlap rule](/speed/change-speed/#a-slowed-clip-overlapping-the-next).
458	- A fit that takes a clip with sound past ×12 asks first, with **Set Speed** and **Cancel**. **Cancel** puts the field back. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
459	
460	## When Fit to is unavailable
461	
462	- **An action is selected.** Fit to belongs to the clip and can't be set inside an action, so its row is marked ⊘. Anything you type there changes the whole clip, not the action.
463	- **The selection holds another kind of clip.** The Speed section appears only when every selected clip is a media clip.
464	- **The clip is linked to its detached sound.** Frame Job won't change its speed until you attach it. See [Linked clips](/speed/overview/#linked-clips).
465	
466	## With an agent
467	
468	`set_speed` with `duration` in place of `rate` does the same job, one clip at a time. A duration of zero or less is an error. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
469	
470	## Related
471	
472	- [The Speed section](/speed/speed-section/)
473	- [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/)
474	- [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/)
475	=================== speed/retime-range
476	---
477	title: Retime Range
478	description: Play the stretch between In and Out faster or slower on every unlocked track at once, and keep everything after it in step.
479	---
480	
481	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
482	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
483	
484	Retime Range plays the stretch between In and Out faster or slower on every unlocked track at once, and moves everything after Out up or back to stay in step. Use it to speed up a slow part of a screen recording with its microphone and camera together.
485	
486	<AtAGlance
487	  menu="Clip ▸ Retime Range…"
488	  tools="retime_range"
489	  needs="An in/out range."
490	/>
491	
492	## Retime a range
493	
494	<Steps>
495	
496	1. Set [In and Out](/timeline/in-out-range/) around the stretch. The menu item is dimmed without them, and while another sheet is open.
497	
498	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Retime Range…**, right after **Close Gap**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
499	
500	3. Set the **Rate**, and tick or untick **Preserve pitch**.
501	
502	4. Choose **Apply**.
503	
504	</Steps>
505	
506	The whole edit is one undo step, **Retime Range**.
507	
508	## The sheet
509	
510	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
511	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
512	| **Rate:** | How much faster the range plays. ×2 makes it half as long, and ×0.5 twice as long. The **Presets** pull-down offers 0.25×, 0.50×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×, 10× and 100×. | ×2 | ×0.1 to ×1000 |
513	| **Preserve pitch** | Sets the pitch setting on every video or audio clip in the range, as [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) does on one clip. | As the first video or audio clip on an unlocked track in the range has it, or on when there is none | |
514	
515	**Apply** at ×1 closes the sheet and changes nothing. At any other rate it retimes the range.
516	
517	If the rate takes a clip with sound past ×12, Frame Job [asks first](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/), because above ×12 a clip's audio is left out. **Set Speed** closes the sheet and applies the edit. **Cancel** leaves the sheet open with nothing changed.
518	
519	## What happens in the range
520	
521	The range gets shorter or longer by the rate, and everything after Out moves to match. A 10 s range at ×2 lasts 5 s, and what follows it starts 5 s earlier.
522	
523	### Clips across an edge
524	
525	A clip that crosses In or Out is cut there first, as [Split](/editing/splitting/) cuts it. Only the piece inside the range changes speed.
526	
527	### Rates multiply
528	
529	Each video or audio clip inside plays at its own rate times the **Rate**, so a ×2 clip retimed by ×2 plays at ×4. A [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/#scale-a-whole-ramp) keeps its shape, and every rate in it scales.
530	
531	### Titles, shapes and stills
532	
533	Titles, shapes, stills, images, graphics and adjustment clips inside are stretched or squeezed by the same amount. A graphic with a length of its own keeps it.
534	
535	### Actions
536	
537	Actions keep their place in each clip, at the same fraction of its length. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).
538	
539	### Markers and detached sound
540	
541	Markers inside the range move with the picture, and markers after it move with everything else. A detached sound linked to a moved clip moves with it.
542	
543	## Inside a nest
544	
545	Retime Range works inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), where it retimes the nest's own tracks and uses the nest's own In and Out. A nest has no markers of its own, so none moves.
546	
547	## When a range can't be retimed
548	
549	Nothing changes, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. Frame Job stops at the first problem it finds, working roughly in this order, so fixing one can show the next:
550	
551	| What stops it | What to do |
552	| --- | --- |
553	| The rate is outside ×0.1 to ×1000. | This only comes up with an agent, because the sheet's field stays inside this range. |
554	| The range is under two frames. | Widen the range. |
555	| A locked track has a clip that ends after In. It would fall out of step. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/), or move In past that clip. |
556	| The range touches a nest clip. | Move the range off it, or retime inside the nest. |
557	| The range touches a caption page with timed words. | Move the range off it. |
558	| The range touches half of a detached pair. | Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
559	| A transition touches the range. | Move the range off it, or remove the transition. |
560	| Two markers would land on the same time. | Move one of them first. |
561	| A clip would play faster than ×1000 or slower than ×0.1. The message names the clip and the rate. | Pick a gentler rate, or set the clip's own speed first. |
562	| A clip would be squeezed under one frame. The message names it. | Pick a gentler rate. |
563	
564	A clip only has to overlap the range to count, so a nest or a detached clip that crosses In or Out stops the edit too.
565	
566	## With an agent
567	
568	`retime_range` makes the same edit, but it takes the range as times, `from` and `to`, so it needs no In and Out. It also needs a `rate`, and a rate of 1 changes nothing. `keep_pitch` is optional, and without it each clip keeps the setting it has.
569	
570	The result lists the pieces the cuts made in `new_clips`. It never asks about ×12: the clip's audio is left out, and the result carries `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/#retime_range).
571	
572	## Related

575	- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)
576	- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
577	- [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/)
578	=================== speed/freeze-frame
579	---
580	title: Freeze frame
581	description: Hold the frame under the playhead for 2 seconds, keep the rest of the cut in sync, and choose which frame the still holds.
582	---
583	
584	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
585	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
586	
587	Freeze Frame holds one moment of a clip on screen for 2 s, then lets the clip carry on. Use it to pause on a reaction, or to give a title or a voice-over time to land.
588	
589	<AtAGlance
590	  menu="Clip ▸ Freeze Frame"
591	  keys="⇧⌘F"
592	  tools={['freeze_frame', 'slip']}
593	/>
594	
595	## Freeze a frame
596	
597	<Steps>
598	
599	1. Select the clip.
600	
601	2. Move the playhead to the frame you want to hold.
602	
603	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Freeze Frame**, or press <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd>.
604	
605	</Steps>
606	
607	Frame Job splits the clip at the playhead, opens 2 s of empty time there, and fills the gap on the clip's track with a still of that source frame. The rest of the clip picks up after the still. All of this is one undo step, called **Freeze Frame**.
608	
609	The still has no sound, so the clip's own sound stops for the hold.
610	
611	If the playhead sits on the clip's first frame, there's nothing to cut. The still goes in and the whole clip moves after it.
612	
613	## When it is available
614	
615	Freeze Frame works on a selected clip under the playhead. With nothing selected there, it's dimmed. A playhead exactly at a clip's end isn't on that clip. With several selected clips under the playhead, it acts on the first.
616	
617	It needs a clip of a video file with its picture. An audio-only clip, text, a shape, a picture, a graphic, an adjustment clip, a nest or another still can't be frozen. The command stays available on those, and Frame Job shows an error saying the clip "is not a media clip" or "has no video properties". Nothing changes.
618	
619	## Everything stays in sync
620	
621	The 2 s opens across every unlocked track, so the cut stays together:
622	
623	- Clips that start at or after the playhead move 2 s later, on every unlocked track.
624	- Markers at or after the playhead move with them.
625	- A clip on another track that crosses the playhead is neither cut nor moved. It plays on through the hold, as a music bed would.
626	- Sound [linked](/audio/detach-and-attach/) to the frozen clip is cut at the playhead too, and its second half moves with the picture.
627	- Clips on locked tracks stay where they are.
628	
629	## The still keeps the clip's look
630	
631	The still keeps the clip's position, scale, crop and other picture settings as they were at that moment, including any action that was moving it. It lines up with the frame it froze, so the hold doesn't jump.
632	
633	The still has no actions of its own: its look at that moment is written into its own properties. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).
634	
635	A [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/) isn't carried over, so the still doesn't arrive or depart again. Freeze partway through an arrival and the still sits where the clip belongs, without the preset's movement, so the picture jumps there.
636	
637	## Change the frozen frame
638	
639	Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the still's body. The still stays where it is and holds an earlier frame of the source as you drag left, or a later one as you drag right. It stops at the first and last frames of the file. This is a [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/), one undo step called **Slip**.
640	
641	## Change how long it holds
642	
643	The hold is always 2 s from the menu. [Trim](/editing/trimming/) the still's end to change it. A trim moves only that edge, so shortening the still leaves a gap after it, which [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) removes.
644	
645	A still has no file end to stop it, so it can hold as long as you like, but the rest of the clip sits right behind it. To hold for longer, [open room](/editing/close-gaps/#open-room-by-hand) after the still first, then drag its end out. Pulled over the next clip instead, it makes an [overlap](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) with a Cross Dissolve.
646	
647	## On a ramped clip
648	
649	On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) or a changed speed, the still holds the frame actually playing at the playhead.
650	
651	A [reversed](/speed/reverse/) clip is different. The still counts forwards through the file, so it usually holds another frame from the one on screen. [Drag it](#change-the-frozen-frame) to the frame you want.
652	
653	## Good to know
654	
655	Frame Job won't freeze where the still would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule). It beeps, the foot of the inspector says why, and nothing changes. Two places do this:
656	
657	- Inside a [transition](/motion/transitions/), where the two clips already overlap.
658	- On a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/), because the rest of that track can't move out of the still's way.
659	
660	## With an agent
661	
662	`freeze_frame` takes the clip, an optional `at` (the playhead if left out) and an optional `duration` (2 s if left out), so it can hold any moment of a clip without moving the playhead, for any length of at least one frame. An `at` outside the clip or a shorter `duration` is an error. `slip` on a freeze frame moves the frame it holds. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
663	
664	## Related
665	
666	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
667	- [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
668	- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
669	- [Close gaps and insert time](/editing/close-gaps/)

671	=================== speed/reverse
672	---
673	title: Reverse a clip
674	description: Play a clip back to front, picture and sound, and deal with the backwards copy Frame Job renders to do it.
675	---
676	
677	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
678	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
679	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
680	
681	Reverse plays a clip back to front, picture and sound together. The Mac's playback can't run video backwards, so the first time you reverse a file, Frame Job renders a backwards copy of it and the clip plays from that.
682	
683	<AtAGlance
684	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Timing"
685	  tools="set_reversed"
686	/>
687	
688	<Shot
689	  name="10-clip-clip-tab.inspector"
690	  alt="The Clip tab on its Clip sub-tab, with the Timing section open: In, Out and Duration, then an unticked Reverse checkbox, Reversed frames reading a dash, and a dimmed Render Reverse button."
691	/>
692	
693	## Reverse a clip
694	
695	<Steps>
696	
697	1. Select the clip, or several clips.
698	
699	2. In the inspector, go to the **Clip** tab and its **Clip** sub-tab, and open **Timing** if it's closed.
700	
701	3. Tick **Reverse**.
702	
703	</Steps>
704	
705	If the file has no backwards copy yet, the [Reversing sheet](#the-reversing-sheet) appears while Frame Job makes one. When it closes, the clip plays backwards. If a copy already exists, the clip plays backwards straight away.
706	
707	Untick **Reverse** to play the clip forwards again. Each change is one undo step, called **Reverse**.
708	
709	## Where Reverse lives
710	
711	Reverse is for clips of a video or audio file. Text, shapes, graphics, adjustment clips, nests, pictures and freeze frames have no Reverse rows.
712	
713	With one clip selected, **Timing** shows [In, Out and Duration](/editing/timing-section/) above the Reverse rows. With several clips of video or audio files selected, it shows only the Reverse rows, and the section's summary is their total length.
714	
715	| Row | What it does |
716	| --- | --- |
717	| **Reverse** | Plays the clip back to front, or forwards again. |
718	| **Reversed frames** | Shows the state of the [backwards copy](#reversed-frames). |
719	| **Render Reverse** | Starts a stopped or failed render [again](#render-reverse). |
720	
721	With several clips selected, **Reverse** applies to all of them as one undo step. If they disagree, the row is tagged `mixed` and the box shows the first clip's state. Clicking it then sets every clip the same way.
722	
723	## Reversed frames
724	
725	This row tells you where the backwards copy has got to.
726	
727	| It reads | What it means |
728	| --- | --- |
729	| — | The clip isn't reversed. |
730	| Rendering… | The copy is being made, or is about to be. |
731	| Rendered | The copy exists and the clip plays from it. |
732	| Not rendered | The render was cancelled or failed. **Render Reverse** is available. |
733	| Media missing | The clip's file is missing or has no length. |
734	
735	Across several clips, the row shows the state that needs attention first: Not rendered, then Rendering…, Media missing, Rendered.
736	
737	## The Reversing sheet
738	
739	The sheet appears when a reversed clip needs a copy that doesn't exist, unless that file's render was cancelled or failed. Ticking **Reverse** is the usual reason. Opening a project whose package has lost its `cache` folder is another.
740	
741	It shows a progress bar, the line "Rendering a reversed copy of “name”…" or "Rendering reversed copies of 3 files…", and the name of the file being worked on. When it finishes, the sheet closes and the clip plays backwards.
742	
743	Editing commands are unavailable while the sheet is up. If an agent reverses another clip in the meantime, that clip's render starts when the sheet closes.
744	
745	### Cancel the render
746	
747	Choose **Cancel**. The sheet reads "Stopping…" until the render has stopped, then says:
748	
749	> Stopped. Clips that are still reversed show a slate until their frames are rendered — press Render Reverse in the Timing section of the Clip tab to try again.
750	
751	Choose **Close** to carry on. Files that had already finished are kept, and the clip stays reversed.
752	
753	### When a file can't be reversed
754	
755	The sheet says how many files failed, for example "2 files could not be reversed. Those clips show a slate rather than play forwards." Below that it names the first file and the reason. Choose **Close** to carry on. Files that rendered are kept.
756	
757	## The slate
758	
759	Until a clip's copy exists, it shows a slate instead of playing forwards: a dark plate with diagonal stripes, in the clip's place on the canvas. The clip plays no sound either. A clip with no picture stays silent and draws nothing.
760	
761	:::caution
762	An export made while a clip shows a slate writes the slate. Finish the render first.
763	:::
764	
765	## Render Reverse
766	
767	Nothing restarts a stopped render by itself. **Render Reverse** is how you try again, and it's available only when **Reversed frames** reads Not rendered.
768	
769	Each press renders one file, shared by every reversed clip of that file. If several files are waiting, press it once for each file until no selected clip reads Not rendered.
770	
771	Unticking **Reverse** on every clip of a file and ticking it again also starts a new render.
772	
773	## The clip stays in place
774	
775	Reversing never moves a clip. It keeps its start, its length and its in point.
776	
777	The in point is counted in the direction the clip plays, so reversing a trimmed clip shows the other end of the file. Take a 10 s file trimmed to its first 3 s. Reversed, the clip plays the file's last 3 s, from 10 s back to 7 s. To play a different part, [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/) the clip.
778	
779	## Reverse with speed and ramps
780	
781	Reverse works with [Speed](/speed/change-speed/), [Fit to](/speed/fit-to-duration/), the [⌥ rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) and [speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/). The in point and the ramp both count in the direction the clip plays, so a reversed ramped clip ramps through the file backwards.
782	
783	## The backwards copy
784	
785	Frame Job renders one copy per file. It's kept in the [project package](/reference/framejob-package/)'s `cache` folder with the other things Frame Job can rebuild, and every reversed clip of that file shares it. The same file can play forwards on one clip and backwards on another.
786	
787	The copy stays after you untick **Reverse**, so ticking it again doesn't render anything. [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) brings the copies its clips play along with it.
788	
789	The copy belongs to one version of the file, in one place. If the file changes or moves, or you [relink](/projects/relink-media/) the clip to another file, Frame Job renders a new copy and removes the old one.
790	
791	## Depth and colour
792	
793	The copy is rendered at 10 bits, at the source's exact size, with the colour information from the source file, so an HDR or log clip still looks right when reversed. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).
794	
795	It's written as HEVC Main 10. A source with an odd width or height takes ProRes 422 instead, which makes a file several times larger.
796	
797	:::caution
798	The copy doesn't keep an alpha channel. A reversed ProRes 4444 clip loses its transparency.
799	:::
800	
801	## Good to know
802	
803	### Still images
804	
805	A picture on the timeline looks the same backwards, so it has no Reverse rows and nothing to render. The same goes for a [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/).
806	
807	### Linked clips
808	
809	Frame Job won't reverse a clip linked to its detached sound. The foot of the inspector says which clips are linked. Choose **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** (<kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd>) first. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). With several clips selected, the others still reverse.
810	
811	### Commands that need a forward clip
812	
813	- [Generate Captions](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/) skips a reversed clip, because its words would come out backwards.
814	- [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), [Add Shortcut Overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) and [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) won't work on one.
815	
816	## With an agent
817	
818	`set_reversed` takes the clip and `reversed`, true or false, so it says which way to play and isn't a toggle. The Reversing sheet appears in the project's window, as it does when you tick **Reverse**, and the clip shows the [slate](#the-slate) until the copy exists. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
819

2	---
3	title: "Speed ramps"
4	description: "What a speed ramp is, how Speed actions build one, how to read it on the timeline, and why a ramp can't play past the end of its file."
5	---
6	
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A speed ramp changes a clip's rate over time. It can play at ×1, speed up to ×4 over half a second, hold there, and slow back down, all inside one clip. Use one to hurry through a slow stretch or linger on a moment, without cutting the clip or moving anything after it.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…', 'Clip ▸ Add Action']}
13	  keys="⌥⌘K"
14	  where={['The action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section']}
15	  tools={['add_speed_ramp', 'add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_action', 'remove_action']}
16	/>
17	
18	There are two ways to make one:
19	
20	- [Make a speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/) with **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**, which builds a whole ramp in one step.
21	- [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/), one change of speed at a time.
22	
23	Both give you the same thing, so you can start from the sheet and adjust the result by hand.
24	
25	## Speed actions
26	
27	A ramp is made of Speed actions. A Speed action is an ordinary [action](/motion/actions/) on the clip's action lane whose end sets a rate. Each one:
28	
29	- starts from the rate the clip is playing at when the action begins, which is the clip's own rate or the rate an earlier Speed action ended on
30	- moves to its own end rate along its curve
31	- keeps that end rate after it finishes, until the next Speed action
32	
33	So a ramp up and back down is two actions. The first ends at ×4, the clip stays at ×4 after it, and the second ends at ×1.
34	
35	An end rate can be anything from ×0.1 to ×1000. Only a video or audio clip can have one, because only those have a file to read at a rate.
36	
37	## A ramped clip keeps its place
38	
39	A ramp changes how much of the file plays, not where the clip sits. The clip's start, its end and every clip around it stay put.
40	
41	Speeding part of a clip up makes it play further into its file. Slowing part of it down makes it play less of the file.
42	
43	For example, take a 10-second clip at ×1 with a Linear ramp up to ×4 from 2 s to 2.5 s, and back to ×1 from 4 s to 4.5 s. It still takes 10 seconds on the timeline, but it now plays 16 seconds of its file.
44	
45	This is the difference from [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/), where the clip gets longer or shorter.
46	
47	## Never past the end of the file
48	
49	Because a ramp can play further into the file, it can run out of file. A ramp may never play past the end of the clip's media, so an edit that would do that isn't made, and the reason says what would fit.
50	
51	| What you tried | What the reason tells you |
52	| --- | --- |
53	| Setting an end rate too high | The largest end rate that fits, to 0.001. If no rate down to ×0.1 fits, it names the latest clip end that would fit at ×0.1. |
54	| Moving, resizing or removing a Speed action, or clearing its rate | The latest clip end that fits |
55	| Applying **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** | The largest rate that fits, or that no rate fits |
56	
57	Nothing changes when this happens. Frame Job beeps and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, starting "Refused:". It stays there until you click it or the project changes. In the Speed Ramp sheet the reason appears in the [readout](/speed/make-a-ramp/#the-readout) and **Apply** is unavailable. Dragging a band doesn't show a reason. The band stays at the last place that fits.
58	
59	A clip end in a reason is a position on the timeline, given in ticks, Frame Job's own unit of time. Divide by 600,000 to get seconds. Trim the clip's end to that time and the ramp has enough file to play.
60	
61	## The rate line
62	
63	A white line across the action lane draws the clip's rate over its length, higher where it plays faster and lower where it plays slower.
64	
65	The line is scaled from the clip's own slowest rate to its fastest, so a gentle ramp draws as tall as a steep one. Use it to see the ramp's shape. For the figures, see the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/).
66	
67	The line shows at the **Medium** and **Large** track heights and in the Clip tab's lane. A clip whose rate never changes draws no line. While the line is drawn, a selected Speed band leaves out the curve it would otherwise show.
68	
69	The clip's filmstrip and waveform follow the ramp too.
70	
71	## The band label
72	
73	At the **Large** track height, a Speed action's band on the timeline is labelled `speed`. A band's label lists everything its action changes, so one that also changes the clip's scale reads `scale, speed`. At **Medium** it shows only its number, and at **Small** it's a plain bar.
74	
75	## Good to know
76	
77	- A clip linked to its detached sound can't change its speed. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
78	- Going above ×12 anywhere in a ramp silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/#ramps-and-the-12-rule).
79	- Sound on a ramped clip is rendered in the background, so a clip can be briefly silent after you edit it. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/).
80	- Captions over a ramped clip follow the ramp. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
81

89	=================== speed/make-a-ramp
90	---
91	title: "Make a speed ramp"
92	description: "Use Clip ▸ Speed Ramp… to speed up or slow down part of a clip in one step, with a choice of four shapes."
93	---
94	
95	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
96	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
97	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
98	
99	**Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** makes a whole [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) in one step. Pick a shape and a rate, and the sheet adds the Speed actions for you. The clip keeps its start and its length, and plays more or less of its file.
100	
101	<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…" tools="add_speed_ramp" />
102	
103	## Make a ramp
104	
105	<Steps>
106	
107	1. Select one clip. **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** is available only when exactly one video or audio clip is selected. It has no keyboard shortcut.
108	
109	2. To ramp part of the clip, set an [in and out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) inside it first. See [The span](#the-span).
110	
111	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**.
112	
113	4. Choose a **Shape** and a **Rate**. For **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**, choose a **Hold** too.
114	
115	5. Read the [readout](#the-readout), then choose **Apply**.
116	
117	</Steps>
118	
119	<Shot
120	  name="13b-speed-ramp-sheet.sheet"
121	  alt="The Speed Ramp sheet, with Shape set to Speed Dip, Rate 0.5 beside a Presets menu, Curve set to Ease In Out and Hold set to 50%. The readout below says Speed Dip, the whole clip, from 00:00:00:00 to 00:00:05:07, then ×1 to ×0.5, held 2.63 s, back to ×1. Cancel and Apply sit at the foot, with the range ×0.1 to ×1000 to their left."
122	/>
123	
124	**Apply** adds the actions as one undo step named after the shape, such as **Speed Dip**. When captions move with it, the step's name adds "and Re-time Captions".
125	
126	The result is ordinary Speed actions, one for **Ramp Up** and **Ramp Down** and two for **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**. They show as bands on the action lane and you can [edit them by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/) like any other action.
127	
128	## The span
129	
130	The ramp covers the timeline's in and out range if that range lies entirely inside the clip. Otherwise it covers the whole clip, and an in and out range that runs past either edge of the clip is ignored.
131	
132	The [readout](#the-readout) says which one you've got.
133	
134	## The shapes
135	
136	| Shape | What it makes | Rate must be | Default rate |
137	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
138	| **Ramp Up** | One action over the span, rising from the current rate to your rate and holding it after. | Above the rate where the span starts | ×2 |
139	| **Ramp Down** | One action over the span, falling to your rate and holding it after. | Below the rate where the span starts | ×0.5 |
140	| **Speed Dip** | Two actions: a ramp down to your rate at the start of the span, a hold, and a ramp back to the starting rate at its end. | Below the rate where the span starts | ×0.5 |
141	| **Speed Burst** | Two actions: a ramp up to your rate at the start of the span, a hold, and a ramp back to the starting rate at its end. | Above the rate where the span starts | ×2 |
142	
143	"Up" and "down" describe the rate where the span starts, not time. That rate is the clip's own rate, or the rate an earlier Speed action ended on, so a ramp can't start slow and rise to the clip's own rate. For that, set the clip to the slow rate first, then use **Ramp Up**.
144	
145	**Speed Dip** is the default because it plays less of the file, so it fits a clip that already uses its whole file. Anything that rises past the starting rate needs footage beyond the clip's current end. If a clip has none spare, trim its end first.
146	
147	## The controls
148	
149	| Control | What it does | Default |
150	| --- | --- | --- |
151	| **Shape** | One of the four shapes above. Choosing a shape resets **Rate** to that shape's default. | Speed Dip |
152	| **Rate** | The rate the ramp reaches, from ×0.1 to ×1000. **Presets** offers 0.25×, 0.50×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×, 10× and 100×, the same as the Speed sheet. | Set by **Shape**: ×0.5 for Speed Dip |
153	| **Curve** | How each new action eases: **Ease In Out** or **Linear**. | Ease In Out |
154	| **Hold** | For **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**, how much of the span stays at your rate: **None**, **25%**, **50%** or **75%**. Dimmed for **Ramp Up** and **Ramp Down**, which hold nothing. | 50% |
155	
156	The sheet opens on these defaults every time.
157	
158	With **Hold**, the rest of the span is split evenly between the two ramps, each rounded down to whole frames and at least one frame long. On a 6-second span at 50%, each ramp takes 1.5 s and the rate holds for 3 s. At **None** the two ramps meet.
159	
160	## The readout
161	
162	The sheet tries the ramp on every change, including each keystroke in **Rate**, and shows what it would make.
163	
164	The first line gives the shape and the span in timecode, such as `Speed Dip · the whole clip 00:00:02:00 – 00:00:08:00`. It says `the range` instead when the ramp covers the in and out range.
165	
166	The second line gives the rates, such as `×1 → ×0.5, held 3.00 s, → ×1`. If the ramp can't be made, the second line gives the reason instead and **Apply** is unavailable.
167	
168	## When Apply is unavailable
169	
170	Nothing changes in any of these cases. The readout gives the reason. It can quote clip and action ids, which aren't the numbers on the bands, and times in ticks, Frame Job's own unit of time, where 600,000 ticks make a second. The checks run in this order, so fixing one can show the next.
171	
172	| The problem | What to do |
173	| --- | --- |
174	| The span overlaps an action already on the clip. This counts any action, including one that would sit inside a dip's or burst's hold. The reason names it, and it's never replaced. | Set an in and out range clear of the action, or [move or remove](/speed/build-a-ramp/#move-and-resize-an-action) it. |
175	| A **Speed Dip** or **Speed Burst** span is shorter than two frames. | Widen the in and out range. |
176	| The rate is on the wrong side of the starting rate, such as a **Ramp Up** to a rate that isn't faster. | Change **Rate** or **Shape**. The reason gives the starting rate. |
177	| The clip is linked to its detached sound. | Choose [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
178	| The ramp would [play past the end of the file](/speed/speed-ramps/#never-past-the-end-of-the-file). | Use the largest rate that fits, which the reason names, or trim the clip's end. |
179	
180	## Good to know
181	
182	- Taking a clip with sound past ×12 asks once first, on the sheet. **Set Speed** closes the sheet and applies the ramp, and **Cancel** leaves the sheet open. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
183	- Captions on a Captions track are re-timed in the same step. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
184	
185	## With an agent
186	
187	`add_speed_ramp` takes `clip`, `rate` and a `shape`: `ramp_up`, `ramp_down`, `speed_dip` or `speed_burst`. It isn't tied to the in and out range. Give `from` and `to` together, measured from the clip's start, to set the span, or neither for the whole clip. A span running past the clip's end isn't accepted, which can't happen from the sheet.
188	
189	It can also use any action curve and any `hold` from 0 to 0.9, and a larger hold comes down to 0.9. A `hold` on `ramp_up` or `ramp_down` is an error. So is a rate of zero or less, and any other rate outside ×0.1 to ×1000 is brought inside that range.
190	
191	The result gives the new actions' ids in `new_actions`, adds `audio_left_out` and `audio_note` when a clip goes past ×12, and adds `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed` when captions moved. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
192	
193	## Related
194

196	- [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/)
197	- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)

199	=================== speed/build-a-ramp
200	---
201	title: "Build a ramp by hand"
202	description: "Add Speed actions yourself, set each one's rate and curve, and move, resize, split or remove them."
203	---
204	
205	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
206	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
207	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
208	
209	Building a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) by hand gives you full control of each change of speed, where it starts, how long it takes and how it eases. Use it when the four shapes in [Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) don't fit.
210	
211	<AtAGlance
212	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
213	  keys="⌥⌘K"
214	  where={['The action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section ▸ Rate']}
215	  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_action', 'remove_action']}
216	/>
217	
218	## Build a ramp
219	
220	<Steps>
221	
222	1. Select the clip and put the playhead where the change of speed should start.
223	
224	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>), or the **+** in the action lane's header. The new action is 1 s long, uses the **Linear** curve, and is selected.
225	
226	3. [Move or resize](#move-and-resize-an-action) its band so it covers the change, and [set its curve](#set-the-curve).
227	
228	4. In the Clip tab's **Speed** section, [set **Rate**](#set-the-rate) to the rate this action should end on.
229	
230	5. Repeat for each change of speed. Each action starts from the rate the last one ended on.
231	
232	</Steps>
233	
234	<Shot
235	  name="10d-clip-speed-action.inspector"
236	  alt="The Clip tab with an action selected. The action lane reads Actions 1, editing 1, with one green band, a white rate line rising across it, and a row below for the action's start, its length of 1.00 s, its curve set to Linear and a trash button. Further down, the Speed section shows Rate at 2.00× with now 1.50× in coral beside it, and a Clear button in its header."
237	/>
238	
239	**Add Action** is available when a selected clip is under the playhead. An action needs a full second free, so Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector if it would run past the clip's end or overlap another action. Move the playhead earlier, or clear the way.
240	
241	## Set the rate
242	
243	While an action is selected, the **Speed** section edits that action rather than the clip. **Rate** shows the rate the action ends on. Type a rate from ×0.1 to ×1000, or pick 0.50×, 1.00×, 2.00× or 4.00× from its menu. Doing this turns any action into a Speed action.
244	
245	If the action doesn't set a rate yet, **Rate** shows the rate the clip is playing at the end of that action. The coral **now** beside the field shows the rate at the playhead, when that differs. There's no **Reset** while an action is selected, so to end the action at ×1, enter 1.
246	
247	To take the rate out of an action and keep the action, choose **Clear** in the section header. This is one undo step, and it can't be done if the clip would then [play past the end of its file](/speed/speed-ramps/#never-past-the-end-of-the-file). See [Clear a rate from an action](/speed/speed-section/#clear-a-rate-from-an-action) for the other ways to do it.
248	
249	**Keep pitch** and **Fit to** still belong to the clip, so their rows are marked ⊘. A length typed in **Fit to** changes the clip, not the action. See [Rows that stay the clip's](/speed/speed-section/#rows-that-stay-the-clips).
250	
251	A rate too high for the file isn't accepted, and the reason at the foot of the inspector names the largest that fits. Setting a rate above ×12 on a clip with sound [asks first](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
252	
253	## Set the curve
254	
255	The curve is how an action eases from its starting rate to its end rate. Select the action and choose from the curve pop-up in the detail row under the Clip tab's action lane. It has no label of its own, and shows the curve's name:
256	
257	| Curve | How the rate moves |
258	| --- | --- |
259	| **Linear** | Steadily, from start to end. This is what a new action uses. |
260	| **In** | Slowly at first. |
261	| **Out** | Slowly at the end. |
262	| **In Out** | Slowly at both ends. |
263	
264	Changing a curve changes how much of the file the ramp plays, so a change won't go through if the ramp would then play past the end of the file. The undo step is **Action Curve**.
265	
266	## Move and resize an action
267	
268	Drag the middle of a band on the action lane to move it. Drag either end to resize it. The grips are the outer 5 pt of a band, and they show when you hover over a band wider than 15 pt.
269	
270	Bands drag the same way on the timeline and in the Clip tab's lane. A drag snaps to whole frames and stops at the next action and at the clip's end. An action can't be shorter than one frame.
271	
272	You can also type in the detail row: the first field is where the action starts, measured from the clip's start, and the second is its length.
273	
274	The undo steps are **Move Action** and **Resize Action**. Captions over the clip move in the same step, which adds "and Re-time Captions" to the name. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
275	
276	Moving or resizing a Speed action changes how much of the file the clip plays. If a drag would take the clip past the end of its file, the band stays at the last place that fits. If a typed value would, nothing changes and the reason names the latest clip end that fits.
277	
278	## The playhead selects the action
279	
280	With one clip selected, playing or scrubbing into an action selects it. The Speed section then edits that action. Clicking a band also selects it, and parks the playhead at the action's end so the preview shows the rate you're setting.
281	
282	An action stays selected when the playhead moves out of it, until the playhead enters another action or you go back to the clip. So check the lane's header before you change **Rate**. It reads "editing" and the action's number while an action is selected.
283	
284	## Back to editing the clip
285	
286	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or choose the **Clip** chip at the left of the Clip tab's action lane. The Speed section edits the clip itself again.
287	
288	The playhead can stay inside the action, and it won't be selected again until the playhead leaves and comes back.
289	
290	## Remove an action
291	
292	Select the action and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, or choose the trash button in the detail row. With an action selected, <kbd>⌫</kbd> removes the action and not the clip. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
293	
294	A Speed action can't be removed if the clip would then play past the end of its file, which happens when the action was slowing the clip down. The reason at the foot of the inspector names the latest clip end that fits.
295	
296	The undo step is **Remove Action**, or **Remove Action and Re-time Captions** when captions move.
297	
298	## Split inside an action
299	
300	To [split a clip](/editing/splitting/) partway through a Speed action, put the playhead inside the action and split as usual. The split keeps the picture continuous at the cut, with no repeated or skipped frame. Each half gets its own Speed action, and the second half starts at the rate the clip had reached.
301	
302	Two things can change, depending on the curve:
303	
304	- With **Out** or **In Out**, the rate can jump at the cut.
305	- With **In** or **In Out**, the second half can end on a different frame of the file.
306	
307	See [Split inside a Speed action](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/#split-inside-a-speed-action) for how the rates are worked out.
308	
309	## Good to know
310	
311	A clip linked to its detached sound can't have its Speed actions changed until you choose [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
312	
313	## With an agent
314	
315	`add_action` adds the action, and `set_action_end` with `speed` in its `patch`, such as `{ "speed": 3 }`, sets the rate it ends on. `speed: null` takes the rate out again. `set_action` moves or resizes an action and sets its curve, and `remove_action` removes it. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
316

324	=================== speed/edit-a-ramped-clip
325	---
326	title: Edit a ramped clip
327	description: What a speed change, trim, split or freeze frame does to a clip with a speed ramp, and why Frame Job sometimes won't make the edit.
328	---
329	
330	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
331	
332	Once a clip has a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), your ordinary edits still work on it. This page says what each one does to the ramp, and what stops an edit that would break it.
333	
334	<AtAGlance
335	  menu="Clip ▸ Speed…"
336	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', '⌥-drag a clip\'s end edge', 'The action lane']}
337	  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'set_action']}
338	/>
339	
340	## Scale a whole ramp
341	
342	These all change a ramped clip's speed by scaling the whole ramp by one factor:
343	
344	- **Clip ▸ Speed…**
345	- **Rate** in the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/), with no action selected
346	- **Fit to** in the Speed section
347	- The ⌥ [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) on the clip's end edge
348	- [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/), for the part of the clip inside the range
349	
350	The clip's own rate, every end rate and the length of every Speed action scale together, so the ramp keeps its shape and the clip still plays the same stretch of its file. The clip itself gets shorter or longer. A ramp from ×1 to ×2 scaled by ×2 becomes a ramp from ×2 to ×4, in half the time. With a ramped clip selected, the Speed sheet's readout ends "Each speed ramp keeps its shape: the rates it names scale with the base rate."
351	
352	No rate in a clip can go below ×0.1 or above ×1000, and what happens at those limits depends on how you made the change:
353	
354	| You used | At a limit |
355	| --- | --- |
356	| **Speed…**, **Rate** or **Fit to** | Scaling stops at the limit, so the clip's rate can end up short of the rate you asked for. |
357	| The ⌥ rate stretch | Nothing happens. |
358	| Retime Range | Frame Job won't make the edit, and the reason names the clip and the rate. |
359	
360	To change one rate inside the ramp instead, select its action. **Rate** then sets that action's end rate. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).
361	
362	## Edits follow the ramp
363	
364	Trims, slips, rolls, splits, freeze frames and transitions all read the ramp, so each cut or held frame is the frame the ramp actually plays at that moment.
365	
366	| Edit | What it does on a ramped clip |
367	| --- | --- |
368	| [Trim](/editing/trimming/) the start | The frame under the edge stays put. The Speed actions stay the same distance from the clip's start, so what plays after the new start can change. The edge stops where the clip would otherwise play past the end of its file. |
369	| Trim the end | The Speed actions don't move. How far you can pull the end out depends on the rate the clip reaches, not on its own rate. |
370	| [Roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) | The later clip's start behaves as a start trim, and the earlier clip's end as an end trim. |
371	| [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/) | The source moves at the clip's own rate, and the Speed actions stay where they are. It stops so the clip never plays past the end of its file. |
372	| [Split](#split-inside-a-speed-action) | The two halves meet at the frame the ramp plays at the cut, and the second half starts at the rate playing there. |
373	| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | The still holds the frame the ramp plays at that moment. |
374	| [Transition](/motion/add-a-transition/) | The overlap follows the ramp. The earlier clip carries on past its old end, and the extra footage before the later clip's start plays at that clip's own rate. The later clip still ends on the same frame of its file. |
375	| [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | The separate audio clip gets the same ramp. |
376	
377	[**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**](/editing/paste-attributes/) never copies a speed or a ramp.
378	
379	Transcribing a ramped clip places each word where the ramp plays it. Captions already on the timeline [follow a later change to the ramp](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
380	
381	## Split inside a Speed action
382	
383	Splitting partway through a Speed action keeps the picture continuous at the cut, with no repeated or skipped frame. The action becomes two, one on each half. The first ends at whatever rate makes the picture meet at the cut, and the second keeps the original end rate.
384	
385	The action's curve matters here:
386	
387	- With **Ease Out** or **Ease In Out**, the rate can jump at the cut.
388	- With **Ease In** or **Ease In Out**, the second half can end on a different frame of the file than the unsplit clip did. If it would then play past the end of the file, its end rate is lowered to the largest that fits.
389	
390	## Filmstrip and waveform
391	
392	A ramped clip's filmstrip and waveform follow the ramp, so what you see at a point on the timeline is what plays there. A stretch at a high rate shows more of the file in the same space.
393	
394	## An action past the clip's end
395	
396	After a trim, or after a ramp is scaled, a Speed action can lie partly or wholly past the clip's end. It stays on the clip, and you can still change its curve, move it earlier or shorten it. Being past the end stops only a change that takes it further past.
397	
398	Its end rate still counts for the [×12 rule](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/), even though that part never plays. If a clip is silent though it never seems to pass ×12, look for an action like this.
399	
400	## When a ramp edit can't be made
401	
402	A ramped clip keeps its place and its length on the timeline, so a ramp can't play past the end of the clip's file. Frame Job won't make an edit that would, and the reason says what would fit: the largest rate, or the latest clip end. [Never past the end of the file](/speed/speed-ramps/#never-past-the-end-of-the-file) lists what each edit names.
403	
404	**Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** has a few more conditions, such as a span that overlaps another action. See [When Apply is unavailable](/speed/make-a-ramp/#when-apply-is-unavailable).
405	
406	A clip with [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) is linked to its audio, so no speed or ramp edit will change it. The reason says to use Attach Audio first.
407	
408	Whatever stops the edit, nothing changes. Frame Job beeps, makes no undo step, and shows the reason:
409	
410	- **At the foot of the inspector**, after the word "Refused:". It stays until the project changes or you click it. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
411	- **In the Speed Ramp sheet's readout**, as you adjust the sheet, so nothing has been applied and there's no beep. **Apply** is dimmed until the preset fits.
412	
413	Dragging an action's band is different. There's no beep and no reason, and the band stays at the last place that worked.
414	
415	A reason can give a time in ticks, the unit Frame Job counts time in. There are 600,000 ticks in a second, so 1,200,000 ticks is 2 seconds.
416

425	=================== speed/ramp-audio
426	---
427	title: Sound on a ramp
428	description: How Frame Job renders the sound of a ramped clip in the background, why the clip goes silent for a moment, and what an export does about it.
429	---
430	
431	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
432	
433	A clip whose speed changes as it plays can't play its sound straight from the file, so Frame Job renders that sound in the background. While it renders, the clip is silent in the preview. An export always waits for it.
434	
435	<AtAGlance
436	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section ▸ Keep pitch"
437	  tools={['set_speed', 'export']}
438	/>
439	
440	## Rendered audio
441	
442	Two kinds of clip have their sound rendered into a separate file:
443	
444	- a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), with **Keep pitch** on or off
445	- a clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with **Keep pitch** off
446	
447	A clip at a constant speed with **Keep pitch** on isn't rendered, and neither is a clip above ×12, because [it has no sound](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
448	
449	There's nothing to start. A new render begins after each edit that changes the clip's timing, such as a ramp, its rate, a trim or a split, and after you change **Keep pitch**. During a drag, it waits until you let go.
450	
451	Each render covers the whole clip's sound, so how long it takes grows with the clip's length and rate. Renders run one at a time, in the background, so you can keep editing. An edit that makes a render out of date drops it, so a run of quick edits doesn't queue up work.
452	
453	The files are saved inside the project package, in `cache/ramp-audio/`, and Frame Job can rebuild them. Until a new project is saved, they're in a temporary folder. [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) doesn't copy them, so the new project renders its own.
454	
455	## Keep pitch off
456	
457	The sound glides smoothly up and down in pitch with the rate, like tape, and stays in step with the picture. At a constant speed it plays at that speed's tape pitch.
458	
459	## Keep pitch on
460	
461	The sound keeps its own pitch as the speed changes. After a deep slow-down, such as ×2 to ×0.5, it can run up to about 24 ms behind the picture.
462	
463	See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) for the control itself.
464	
465	## Silent while it renders
466	
467	While a clip's sound is rendering, that clip plays silent in the preview. Everything else on the timeline plays as usual, and the clip's sound comes back on its own when the render finishes.
468	
469	## Undo and redo render again
470	
471	Undo and redo usually start a render too, because Frame Job drops the file from before the edit once a newer render lands. The clip is briefly silent then as well.
472	
473	## Exports wait for it
474	
475	An export waits for every render it needs and never writes that sound silent. The Exporting sheet reads "Preparing “*name*”…" during the wait, and a queued export's row reads `Writing · 0 %`. You can cancel either one there. This covers speed ramps and clips at a constant speed other than ×1 with **Keep pitch** off.
476	
477	An animated GIF or APNG has no sound, so it doesn't wait. An export an agent starts with `export` waits the same way.
478	
479	## A failed render
480	
481	If a render fails, an export that needs it stops with this message, naming the clip:
482	
483	> Clip N's retimed audio could not be rendered: …
484	
485	Frame Job doesn't try a failed render again while it stays open. The clip stays silent, and exports that need it keep failing, until you change the clip's timing, which starts a new render, or quit and reopen Frame Job.
486

494	=================== speed/keep-pitch
495	---
496	title: "Keep pitch"
497	description: "Choose whether a clip's sound keeps its own pitch at a new speed or follows the speed like tape, and know when that sound is silent while it renders."
498	---
499	
500	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
501	
502	When a clip plays faster or slower, its sound can do one of two things. Keep pitch decides which.
503	
504	<AtAGlance
505	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed… ▸ Preserve pitch', 'Clip ▸ Retime Range… ▸ Preserve pitch']}
506	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Speed section ▸ Keep pitch"
507	  tools={['set_speed', 'retime_range', 'set_audio']}
508	/>
509	
510	## What it does
511	
512	| Setting | The sound |
513	| --- | --- |
514	| On | The voice or music keeps its own pitch at the new speed. |
515	| Off | The pitch follows the speed, higher when faster and lower when slower, like tape or a record. |
516	
517	The setting belongs to the clip and is on for a new clip. Above ×12 a clip has no sound either way. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
518	
519	It also controls how a speed ramp sounds. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/).
520	
521	## Keep pitch in the inspector
522	
523	Tick or untick **Keep pitch** in the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/#keep-pitch). It applies to every selected media clip as one undo step, **Keep Pitch**.
524	
525	## Preserve pitch in the Speed sheet
526	
527	The [Speed sheet](/speed/change-speed/) calls the same setting **Preserve pitch**. It opens on the first selected clip's setting, and **Apply** sets it on every listed clip. Changing it alone counts as a change for **Apply**.
528	
529	The [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) sheet has a **Preserve pitch** box too, for the clips in the range.
530	
531	## Tape pitch is rendered in the background
532	
533	With Keep pitch off, at any rate but ×1 and up to ×12, Frame Job renders the clip's sound in the background before it plays. The clip is silent in the preview until that finishes. When it's ready, the sound plays at that speed's tape pitch.
534	
535	- Renders run one at a time, and the wait grows with the clip's length and, above ×1, its rate.
536	- A change to the clip's timing, such as a new rate, a trim or a split, starts a new render.
537	- Undo and redo render again too, because the file from before the edit isn't kept. The clip is briefly silent after an undo as well.
538	- In a saved project, the rendered sound is kept in the project package.
539	
540	An export waits for every render it needs, so that sound is never silent in the file. The **Exporting** sheet reads "Preparing" and the file's name during the wait, for example "Preparing “movie.mp4”…".
541	
542	If a render fails, the export stops with "Clip N's retimed audio could not be rendered: …". Frame Job doesn't try that render again while it stays open, so the clip stays silent in the preview. Change the clip's timing to start a new render, or quit and reopen Frame Job.
543	
544	With Keep pitch on, a constant speed needs no render and plays straight away.
545	
546	## Good to know
547	
548	- **It always applies to the whole clip**, even with an action selected, and it can't be animated. In an action, its row is marked ⊘.
549	- **Across clips at different rates**, the inspector's checkbox also brings them all to the first clip's rate. See [Keep pitch in the Speed section](/speed/speed-section/#keep-pitch).
550	- **Linked clips.** Keep pitch isn't a rate, so you can change it on a clip that's linked to its detached sound.
551	- **Very small speed changes.** With Keep pitch on, a rate within 0.1% of ×1 plays as plain varispeed, which moves the pitch by under 1.74 cents, too little to hear. From ×0.98 to ×1.02, outside that band, Frame Job uses a stretch suited to small changes.
552	- **Synchronize Audio** turns Keep pitch off on a clip it corrects for drift. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).
553	
554	## With an agent
555	
556	`set_speed`, `retime_range` and `set_audio` all take `keep_pitch`. Leave it out and the setting stays as it is. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
557

564	=================== speed/sound-at-high-speed
565	---
566	title: "Sound at high speed"
567	description: "Why a clip goes silent above ×12, what the alert asks before it happens, and how ramps count towards the limit."
568	---
569	
570	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
571	
572	A clip that plays faster than ×12 loses its sound in the preview and in the export, while its picture keeps playing. Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip there.
573	
574	<AtAGlance
575	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…', 'Clip ▸ Retime Range…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…']}
576	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', 'The ⌥ rate stretch on the timeline']}
577	  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'set_action_end', 'retime_range']}
578	/>
579	
580	## Sound is left out above ×12
581	
582	The limit is the same with [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) on or off. At exactly ×12 the sound still plays, and at anything faster it doesn't. The picture carries on to the top of the speed range, ×1000.
583	
584	The limit is fixed, and no setting changes it. It sits a margin below the speeds at which an export with sound can stall.
585	
586	Nothing is deleted. Bring the clip back to ×12 or below and its sound returns.
587	
588	## The alert
589	
590	Before an edit takes a clip with sound from ×12 or below to above ×12, an alert asks first. For one clip it reads:
591	
592	> “Interview” will be silent at ×16.
593	>
594	> Frame Job leaves a clip’s audio out above ×12. The picture still plays.
595	
596	For several clips it counts them. It reads “3 clips will be silent at ×16.”, or “3 clips will be silent at their new speeds.” when their rates differ, and then “Frame Job leaves a clip’s audio out above ×12. The pictures still play.”
597	
598	The alert is a question, not a block. You can always go ahead.
599	
600	| Button | What it does |
601	| --- | --- |
602	| **Set Speed** | Makes the edit exactly as you asked. It's the default button, and it keeps this name when the edit is a ramp or a stretch. |
603	| **Cancel** | Changes nothing and adds no undo step. |
604	
605	You're asked once. A clip that's already above ×12 isn't asked about again, even if you make it faster still. A clip whose sound is switched off, or whose file has no sound, isn't asked about at all.
606	
607	## Where the alert appears
608	
609	| You're using | If you choose **Cancel** |
610	| --- | --- |
611	| **Clip ▸ Speed…** | The sheet stays open. |
612	| **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** | The sheet stays open. |
613	| **Clip ▸ Retime Range…** | The sheet stays open. |
614	| **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | The sheet stays open. |
615	| The [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/): **Rate**, its quick picks, **Keep pitch**, **Reset** or **Fit to** | The fields go back to what they showed. |
616	| The [⌥ rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) | The clip stays as it was before the drag. |
617	
618	A stretch is put back when you let go, so nothing has changed while the question is up. **Set Speed** then applies it again.
619	
620	Moving, resizing or removing an action can't raise a clip's fastest rate, so those edits never ask.
621	
622	## Ramps and the ×12 rule
623	
624	On a [ramped clip](/speed/speed-ramps/), Frame Job looks at the fastest rate set anywhere on the clip. If any rate in the ramp is above ×12, the whole clip is silent, not only the fast part.
625	
626	The alert counts the ramp's peak rate in the same way. A clip at ×1 with one Speed action ending at ×16 is asked about at ×16.
627	
628	An end rate on an action lying past the clip's end still counts, even though that part never plays. If a trimmed clip has gone silent for no clear reason, check the count in the header of its [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) in the Clip tab. An action wholly past the clip's end has no band you can reach, but it's still counted.
629	
630	## The silent audio note
631	
632	The Speed section shows **Audio is silent above ×12** while a selected clip is past the limit. It needs a clip whose file has sound and whose sound is on. It appears in either pitch mode, and a ramp counts by its fastest rate.
633	
634	## Good to know
635	
636	- A clip that only has sound follows the same rule, and is silent above ×12.
637	- Clips inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) count too.
638	- Turning a clip's sound back on while it's above ×12 doesn't bring up the alert, because the speed didn't change. The silent audio note shows instead.
639	- When Speed Up Typing runs by itself after a [recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/), Frame Job can't stop to ask. A speed-up that would silence a clip isn't made, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector.
640	
641	## With an agent
642	
643	An agent is never asked. Its edit goes through, and the result lists the ids of the clips that went silent in `audio_left_out`, with a sentence saying so in `audio_note`. Neither appears if no clip crossed the limit. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
644

652	=================== speed/captions-and-speed
653	---
654	title: Captions follow a speed change
655	description: How captions stay on the speech when a clip's speed or ramp changes, which ones move, and which ones Frame Job removes.
656	---
657	
658	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
659	
660	When you change the speed of a clip with sound, the captions over it move with its speech, so they stay on the words you hear. There's nothing to turn on.
661	
662	<AtAGlance
663	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…']}
664	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', 'The action lane', '⌥-drag a clip\'s end edge']}
665	  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
666	/>
667	
668	## What moves them
669	
670	Captions move when you:
671	
672	- change the clip's speed, with **Clip ▸ Speed…**, the Speed section or the ⌥ rate stretch
673	- add a ramp with **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**
674	- add, move, resize, edit or remove a Speed action on the clip
675	
676	The captions move in the same undo step as the edit, so one undo puts them back too. The step is named after the edit with "and Re-time Captions" added, such as **Set Speed and Re-time Captions**. A drag moves them when you let go of the mouse.
677	
678	The clip has to be one captions could have been made from: it plays media with sound, its audio is on, and it isn't reversed.
679	
680	## Which captions move
681	
682	A caption moves when all of these are true:
683	
684	- It's a text clip on a track named **Captions** or **Captions N**, such as **Captions 2**.
685	- That track holds only text clips and isn't locked.
686	- It lies wholly inside the clip you edited.
687	
688	A caption that runs past either edge of the clip stays where it is, and so does anything on another track.
689	
690	## Speech the clip no longer plays
691	
692	A ramp that slows a clip down makes it play less of its file, so it can stop reaching speech it played before.
693	
694	A caption whose speech the clip no longer reaches is removed. A word caption page that's only partly reached keeps the words that still play, and its text is cut to match.
695	
696	## Newly revealed speech
697	
698	When a ramp makes the clip play further into its file, the new part gets no captions. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) again to caption it.
699	
700	## Neighbouring captions
701	
702	A moved caption is cut back where it would run into a caption that didn't move. One that would start inside such a caption, or end up shorter than a frame, is removed.
703	
704	## Good to know
705	
706	- Only speed and ramp edits re-time captions. A trim, slip or split leaves them where they are.
707	- [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) works differently. It stretches or squeezes a text clip in the range along with everything else, and Frame Job won't retime a range that touches a caption page with timed words.
708	- Frame Job checks every caption's new place before it makes the edit. If they don't all work out, the speed edit goes through on its own and the captions stay where they were.
709	
710	## With an agent
711	
712	`set_speed`, `rate_stretch`, `add_speed_ramp`, `set_action`, `remove_action` and `set_action_end` re-time captions the same way, in the same undo step. `set_action_end` does so only when it changes the speed.
713	
714	The result lists the caption clips that moved in `captions_retimed` and the ones removed in `captions_removed`. Each key appears only when it has something in it. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/) and [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
715
