2	---
3	title: Actions
4	description: What an action is, how it takes a clip to an end state over a span of time, and how numbers, colours and switches change along the way.
5	---
6	
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	An action makes a clip change over time: a zoom into a screen recording, a fade of the volume, a title that slides and changes colour. You say where the clip ends up, and the action's span and curve say how it gets there.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
14	  keys="⌥⌘K"
15	  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', "A band on the clip in the timeline"]}
16	  tools={['add_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
17	/>
18	
19	<Shot
20	  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.window"
21	  alt="The editor with a lower third selected. On the timeline the graphic clip holds a numbered action band, the Clip tab's action lane reads 1, editing 1, and the inspector shows the values the clip reaches at the action's end."
22	/>
23	
24	## What an action is
25	
26	An action is a span of time on one clip. Over that span, the clip's properties move from whatever they were when the span began to the action's **end state**, along the action's curve.
27	
28	Actions take the place of keyframes. You don't set a value at each moment. You set what the clip ends at, and the span and the curve do the rest.
29	
30	Actions on one clip can't overlap, and you can't make one that runs past the clip's end. A later trim can leave an action running past the end, and only the part inside the clip plays. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).
31	
32	To make one, see [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/), then [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
33	
34	## The end state is held
35	
36	When the span is over, the clip keeps the end state until a later action changes it. An action that takes the scale to 200% leaves the clip at 200% for the rest of its length. The clip doesn't drift back on its own.
37	
38	To go back, add a second action whose end state names the old value. [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/) does this for a zoom.
39	
40	## Clip time
41	
42	An action's times are measured from the clip's own start, not from the start of the timeline. An action that starts at 2 seconds starts 2 seconds into the clip, wherever the clip sits. Move the clip and its actions go with it.
43	
44	The start field in the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) shows this time.
45	
46	## Several actions on a clip
47	
48	A clip can have as many actions as fit end to end. They run in time order, and each one starts from the state the earlier ones left behind.
49	
50	An action only changes what its end state names. If action 1 takes the scale to 200% and action 2 names only the opacity, the scale stays at 200% through action 2 while the opacity moves.
51	
52	## Action numbers
53	
54	Actions are numbered in time order, and an action has the same number on the timeline and in the Clip tab. The number is a position, not a name, so adding an action before an existing one moves the later ones up by one. If two actions ever share a start, the older one comes first.
55	
56	## Easing curves
57	
58	A curve sets how a value moves across the span. The same four curves serve actions, zooms, speed ramps and transitions.
59	
60	| Curve | In the action lane | How it moves | Halfway through the span, the value is |
61	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
62	| Linear | Linear | At a constant speed | 50% of the way there |
63	| Ease In | In | Starts slowly, ends fast | 25% of the way there |
64	| Ease Out | Out | Starts fast, ends slowly | 75% of the way there |
65	| Ease In Out | In Out | Slow at both ends | 50% of the way there |
66	
67	The action lane's curve pop-up shows the short names, with a small drawing of the curve beside it. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/). A transition's **Curve** pop-up shows the full names. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
68	
69	### Default curves
70	
71	A new action from **Add Action** is **Linear**. A zoom action, from Zoom to Region or Zoom Back, is **Ease In Out**.
72	
73	## How values change over an action
74	
75	What happens to a property depends on what kind of value it is. [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/) goes through them section by section.
76	
77	### Numbers
78	
79	Numbers ramp along the action's curve. That covers position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, volume, a filter's amount, a grade's sliders and a graphic's number properties.
80	
81	An agent can aim a number past what the property can hold. Frame Job keeps the value in the action as written and brings it into range as the clip is drawn, so an opacity aimed at 200% reaches 100% before the action ends and stays there.
82	
83	### Colours
84	
85	Colours ramp too, through OKLab, which keeps the blend's midpoints even. See [Colours blend in OKLab](/motion/what-can-animate/#colours-blend-in-oklab).
86	
87	### Switches, pop-ups and text
88	
89	An on/off box, a filter's kind, a font and a graphic's string, boolean or image property have nothing in between. They hold their value for the whole span, then switch to the end value when the action ends. Once the action changes one, its row in the Clip tab is tagged "at end".
90	
91	The same goes for a section you turn on inside an action, such as a shadow or an outline. Its numbers have nothing to ramp from, so it appears whole when the action ends.
92	
93	:::tip
94	To fade a shadow in, turn it on for the clip with **Opacity** at 0%, then add an action that raises **Opacity**. The opacity ramps, because both ends of it exist.
95	:::
96	
97	### Lists
98	
99	Filters and obscure regions are lists, and they ramp entry by entry while both ends have the same number of entries.
100	
101	| If | Then |
102	| --- | --- |
103	| Both ends have the same number of entries | Each entry's numbers ramp to the entry in the same place at the other end |
104	| One entry changes kind, or a region changes shape | Only that entry switches at the end, and the others still ramp |
105	| The list's length changes | The whole list switches at the end |
106	
107	### Colour curves
108	
109	Curves in the **Color** sub-tab always animate. Two curves with the same number of points ramp point by point, and a neutral curve lines up with the other curve's points. Two curves with different numbers of points blend their values over the action.
110	
111	## With an agent
112	
113	`add_action`, `set_action`, `set_action_end` and `remove_action` do everything the Clip tab does with an action. An agent names the curves `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` and `ease_in_out`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

146	
147	## Bands on the timeline
148	
149	A clip that has an action shows a lane directly under its name strip, with one band per action. Each band spans the action's time on the clip, and is at least 2 pt wide however short the action is.
150	
151	Actions are numbered in time order, so a band's number is its place on the clip, and moving an action past another changes both numbers. The number is the same on the timeline and in the Clip tab.
152	
153	Click a band to select the clip and that action. The playhead moves to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing. Drag a band's body to move the action, or a grip to resize it. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/) and [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
154	
155	The selected action's band is solid. A wash runs down the clip under its span, and the span is shaded on the ruler.
156	
157	A band on a locked track doesn't respond. It doesn't highlight, and clicking it selects the clip, not the action.
158	
159	### Band detail by track height
160	
161	How much a band shows depends on [**View ▸ Timeline Track Height**](/timeline/track-height/).
162	
163	| Track height | Lane height | A band shows |
164	| --- | --- | --- |
165	| Small | 5 pt | A plain bar. |
166	| Medium | 12 pt | Its number, a zoom glyph for a zoom action, and the curve on the selected band. |
167	| Large | 18 pt | All of that, plus the properties it changes, such as `scale, x, y` or `speed`. A graphic's animated properties are listed with the clip's other properties. |
168	
169	The zoom glyph is a small magnifier. It appears on any action that changes exactly scale, x and y, however the action was made.
170	
171	From Medium, a clip whose rate moves also draws its rate line over the bands. While the line is there, a selected Speed band doesn't draw its curve. See [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/).
172	
173	### Band hover
174	
175	Point at a band, on the timeline or in the Clip tab's lane, and it brightens and shows a 5 pt grip at each end. The pointer is an open hand over the body and a resize arrow over a grip.
176	
177	A band 15 pt wide or narrower has no grips, so you can only move it. On the timeline, zoom in to make it wider.
178	
179	## The action lane in the Clip tab
180	
181	The action lane is a small timeline of the selected clip. It's pinned at the top of the Clip tab, between the clip's name and the sub-tabs, so it stays put while you scroll the sections below. The whole clip always fits the lane's width, however long it is.
182	
183	### Header row
184	
185	The header reads **ACTIONS**, then the number of actions or "none". While action N is selected, it adds "· editing N". The three buttons at its right end are:
186	
187	| Button | Tooltip | What it does |
188	| --- | --- | --- |
189	| Zoom-in magnifier | Zoom to Region (Z) | Lets you draw a rectangle on the canvas to zoom to. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/). |
190	| Zoom-out magnifier | Zoom Back | Adds an action that returns the clip to its own scale and position. See [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/#zoom-back). |
191	| Plus | Add Action (⌥⌘K) | Adds an action at the playhead. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/). |
192	
193	While you drag a band in the lane, a readout takes the place of the header's text, with times counted from the clip's start. The buttons stay.
194	
195	### Lane row
196	
197	The **Clip** chip sits at the left. It's highlighted while no action is selected, and clicking it deselects the action, so the Clip tab goes back to editing the clip itself.
198	
199	To its right is the whole clip, with its actions as numbered bands and the playhead as a thin line. Click or drag a band here as you would on the timeline. These bands show their number, the zoom glyph and the selected band's curve whatever the track height, and never list properties. A clip whose rate moves draws its rate line here too.
200	
201	A clip with no actions shows "no actions · ⌥⌘K adds one".
202	
203	### What else the lane shows
204	
205	Under the bands, the lane draws the same marks the timeline draws for the clip, so you can place an action around them:
206	
207	| Mark | Where | Shown when |
208	| --- | --- | --- |
209	| Hatching | At the clip's start, as long as the overlap | The clip has a [transition](/motion/transitions/) and overlaps the clip before it. |
210	| Fades | Triangles along the bottom, at either end | The clip has sound and a fade in or out. |
211	| Motion wedges | Triangles hanging from the top, at either end | The clip has an active In or Out [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/). |
212	
213	### Detail row
214	
215	This row appears only while an action is selected. Its fields have no labels, so read them from left to right as they're listed here. Each change is one undo step.
216	
217	| Control | What it does | Range |
218	| --- | --- | --- |
219	| Start | Where the action starts, as a timecode measured from the clip's own start. | |
220	| Length | How long the action takes, in seconds, snapped to whole frames. | 0.01 to 36,000 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2. A longer value is held to the clip's length. |
221	| Curve | How the action eases from its start to its end state, with a glyph of the curve beside it. | Linear, In, Out, In Out |
222	| Trash button | Removes the action. <kbd>⌫</kbd> does the same. | |
223	
224	If Frame Job can't take a typed Start or Length, for example because the action would overlap another or run past the clip's end, it beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused:". The line stays until the project next changes or you click it.
225	
226	### Several clips selected
227	
228	With several clips selected the lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions.", and there's no count, Clip chip, bands or detail row.
229	
230	The three buttons stay. Add Action still works, and puts the action on the first selected clip under the playhead without selecting it. Zoom to Region and Zoom Back need a single clip, so they beep.
231	
232	## The gutter mark
233	
234	While an action is selected, each row of the Clip tab it animates has a ◆ in its left gutter. Hover over the ◆ and it turns into ×, with the tooltip "Remove from action N". Click it to take that row out of the action, as one undo step, Remove from Action. The row's right-click menu has the same command.
235	
236	See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for all the marks and what they mean.

252	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
253	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
254	
255	Add Action puts a new [action](/motion/actions/) on the selected clip at the playhead, ready for you to say what it animates to.
256	
257	<AtAGlance
258	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
259	  keys="⌥⌘K"
260	  where="Clip tab ▸ action lane ▸ + (Add Action)"
261	  tools="add_action"

263	
264	## Add Action
265	
266	<Steps>
267	
268	1. Select a clip and put the playhead over it.
269	
270	2. Press <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>. **Clip ▸ Add Action** and the **+** button in the Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) do the same.
271	
272	3. In the Clip tab, change what you want the clip to reach by the end of the action. To fade the clip out over that second, for example, set **Opacity** in the **Picture** sub-tab to 0%.
273	
274	</Steps>
275	
276	The new action starts at the playhead, lasts 1 second and uses the **Linear** curve. It's one undo step.
277	
278	## A new action starts empty
279	
280	A new action's end state is empty, so it changes nothing until you edit it. The band appears, and the clip looks and sounds the same as before.
281	
282	The action is selected as it's added, so the Clip tab is ready for its end state. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/). The playhead stays where it is, at the action's start, so the preview shows the change only once you move through the action or play it.
283	
284	## When Add Action is available
285	
286	Add Action needs the playhead over a selected clip. Otherwise **Clip ▸ Add Action** is greyed out, and the action lane's **+** button beeps.
287	
288	## Several clips selected
289	
290	With several clips selected, the action goes on the first selected clip under the playhead and isn't selected, because only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Select that clip alone to edit the new action.
291	
292	## When there's no room for an action
293	
294	The new action needs a clear second after the playhead. Frame Job beeps and adds nothing when the action would:
295	
296	- overlap another action on the clip, or
297	- run past the clip's end.
298	
299	The reason appears at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused:". See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
300	
301	Near the end of a clip, move the playhead back first, or [shorten an existing action](/motion/change-an-action/). A clip shorter than 1 second has no room for an action from Add Action.
302	
303	## Other commands that make actions
304	
305	These commands write ordinary actions. They show as bands and edit like any other.
306	
307	| Command | What it adds |
308	| --- | --- |
309	| [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) | One 1-second **Ease In Out** action that zooms to a rectangle you draw |
310	| [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/) | One 1-second **Ease In Out** action back to the clip's own size and place |
311	| [Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) | One action for Ramp Up and Ramp Down, two for Speed Dip and Speed Burst |
312	| [Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…](/recording/auto-zoom/) | Zoom actions planned from a recording's cursor file |
313	| [Clip ▸ Follow Subject…](/framing/follow-subject/) | Moves that keep a subject in frame |
314	| [Clip ▸ Camera Layout](/framing/camera-layouts/) | Moves from one layout to the next |
315	| [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) | An action for each point you add with <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click |
316	
317	Only Add Action, Zoom to Region and Zoom Back select the action they make.
318	
319	## With an agent
320	
321	`add_action` takes the clip, a start in clip time and an optional length, 1 second if left out, so an agent can place an action shorter than 1 second where Add Action has no room. The new action's id comes back in `new_actions`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

350	
351	## Click a band
352	
353	Click an action's band on the timeline or in the Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). The action is selected, and the Clip tab then edits its end values.
354	
355	The playhead moves to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing. When the action ends with the clip, the playhead stops one frame short, because the clip's very end has no picture.
356	
357	Clicking a band on a clip that's part of a multi-clip selection selects only that clip and its action.
358	
359	On the timeline the action is selected when you press. In the Clip tab's lane it's selected when you let go, so a drag in the lane selects the band when you drop it. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
360	
361	## Adding selects the action
362	
363	An action made with [Add Action](/motion/add-an-action/), [Zoom to Region or Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/) is selected as it's added. The playhead doesn't move for this.
364	
365	## Play or scrub into a span
366	
367	While a clip is the only one selected, moving the playhead into one of its actions selects that action. Playing, scrubbing and stepping all count.
368	
369	Selecting a clip counts too. If the playhead is already inside one of its actions, that action is selected along with the clip.
370	
371	The playhead has to enter the span. An edit that puts a span under a still playhead selects nothing, and neither does an undo or a redo.
372	
373	## How a selected action looks
374	
375	On the timeline:
376	
377	- The action's band is solid.
378	- A wash runs down the clip under the action's span.
379	- The span is shaded on the ruler.
380	
381	In the Clip tab:
382	
383	- The action lane is tinted, and its header adds "· editing N" after the count.
384	- The band is solid, and the **Clip** chip is no longer highlighted.
385	- A detail row appears with the action's start, length, curve and trash button.
386	
387	## The Clip chip
388	
389	The **Clip** chip sits at the start of the action lane. It's highlighted while no action is selected, which tells you the fields edit the clip. Click it while an action is selected to leave the action.
390	
391	## Leave an action
392	
393	Do any of these, and the Clip tab shows the clip's own values again:
394	
395	- Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>.
396	- Click the **Clip** chip.
397	- Select a different clip.
398	
399	Moving the playhead out of the span doesn't leave the action. It stays selected, and the fields keep editing its end state.
400	
401	After <kbd>Esc</kbd> or the **Clip** chip, the playhead can stay inside the span without selecting the action again. It's selected the next time the playhead leaves and comes back.
402	
403	With no action selected, <kbd>Esc</kbd> does whatever it would do otherwise.
404	
405	## Selection is not an edit
406	
407	Selecting an action isn't an undo step, and it isn't saved with the project. A project always opens with no action selected.
408	
409	## Good to know
410	
411	- Only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Select a second clip and the action is deselected. The action lane then reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."
412	- Where two bands sit under the pointer, the one painted on top wins, which is the later one.
413	- Clicking a band that touches the next action puts the playhead on the first frame of that next action, but the one you clicked stays selected.
414	- Removing the selected action deselects it.

444	
445	## Move an action
446	
447	Drag the body of a band, on the timeline or in the Clip tab's action lane, to move the action within its clip. The pointer is an open hand over the body, and a dashed outline marks where the band started.
448	
449	When you let go, the action is selected and the playhead sits at its new end, or one frame short of it when the action ends with the clip. The whole drag is one undo step, **Move Action**.
450	
451	## Resize an action
452	
453	Drag either end of a band to move that end of the action. Each end's grip is its outer 5 pt. The grips appear when you hover over the band, and the pointer becomes a left-right arrow over them.
454	
455	The action stays selected and the playhead goes to its new end, as with a move. The whole drag is one undo step, **Resize Action**.
456	
457	A band 15 pt wide or narrower has no grips and only moves. [Zoom the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) in, or type a [length](#type-a-start-length-or-curve).
458	
459	## Where a drag stops
460	
461	A band drag snaps to whole frames and keeps the action at least one frame long. It stops at the neighbouring actions and at the clip's ends. It doesn't snap to the playhead or to other edits.
462	
463	If Frame Job wouldn't allow a position, the band stops there and shows no message. A Speed action stops where the clip would run out of media, for example.
464	
465	An action that a trim left running past the clip's end can move earlier or get shorter, but can't end any later than it already does.
466	
467	On the timeline, a band on a locked track doesn't drag, and clicking it selects the clip, not the action. Select the action in the Clip tab's lane instead.
468	
469	## The drag readout
470	
471	While you drag, a small readout gives the band's new place.
472	
473	| You're dragging | The readout shows | Example |
474	| --- | --- | --- |
475	| The body, or the start grip | The new start, the new end, and how far the start has moved in seconds and frames | `00:00:01:00 → 00:00:03:00  +0:12` |
476	| The end grip | How much the length has changed, in frames | `len −6f` |
477	
478	On the timeline the readout floats above the clip and gives timeline times. In the Clip tab's lane it replaces the header text and gives times from the clip's own start, to match the Start field.
479	
480	## Drag in the Clip tab's lane
481	
482	The lane moves and resizes bands as the timeline does, with the same limits. It differs in three ways:
483	
484	- It selects the action when you let go, where the timeline selects when you press. A click and a drop both select, and both move the playhead to the action's end.
485	- A locked track doesn't stop a click or a drag here.
486	- It shows a zero-length action, which the timeline doesn't draw.
487	
488	## Type a start, length or curve
489	
490	The action lane's detail row shows while an action is selected.
491	
492	| Control | What it does | Limits |
493	| --- | --- | --- |
494	| Start | Where the action starts, as a timecode from the clip's own start, not the timeline's. | Capped at the clip's length and snapped to a frame. |
495	| Length | How long the action takes, in seconds, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2. | 0.01 to 36000 s, then capped at the clip's length and snapped to a frame. |
496	| Curve | How the action eases from its start to its end state. A small glyph of the curve sits beside the pop-up. | **Linear**, **In**, **Out** or **In Out**. |
497	| Trash button | [Removes the action](#remove-an-action). | |
498	
499	**Linear** runs at a constant speed. **In** starts slowly and ends fast, **Out** starts fast and ends slowly, and **In Out** is slow at both ends.
500	
501	Each change is one undo step: **Move Action**, **Resize Action** or **Action Curve**.
502	
503	A Start that isn't a timecode beeps and goes back to the old value. A Length under half a frame rounds to nothing, and Frame Job shows an error alert instead.
504	
505	Length is capped at the whole clip, not at the room left after the action's start, so a long enough value can still run past the clip's end, and Frame Job won't take that. The next section has the reasons it gives.
506	
507	## When an edit is refused
508	
509	If Frame Job won't take a typed Start or Length, or an [end value](/motion/edit-an-action/), it beeps and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused: ". The message stays until the project next changes or you click it. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/) for how to read it.
510	
511	| Frame Job won't do this when | What to do |
512	| --- | --- |
513	| The action would end past the clip's end, and later than it did before | Shorten it or move it earlier. |
514	| The action would overlap another action on the clip | Move or shorten one of them. |
515	| A Speed action would make the clip run out of media | Use the latest clip end the message names. |
516	| The edit would change a Speed action on a clip that's linked to another | Choose **Attach Audio** first, as the message says. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). |
517	
518	A band drag never shows this message. The band stops instead.
519	
520	## Remove an action
521	
522	Select the action, then press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, choose **Edit ▸ Delete**, or click the trash button in the action lane. Only the action goes, as one undo step, **Remove Action**.
523	
524	The clip keeps its own properties and loses what the action did to them.
525	
526	A Speed action can't be removed if the clip would then run out of media. The message names the latest clip end that fits. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/). On a clip that's linked to another, choose **Attach Audio** before you remove a Speed action.
527	
528	## Ripple Delete still deletes the clip
529	
530	:::caution
531	<kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> (**Ripple Delete**) deletes the whole selected clip and closes the gap, even while an action is selected. Only <kbd>⌫</kbd> removes the action.
532	:::
533	
534	## Good to know
535	
536	- Moving, resizing or removing a Speed action re-times the captions on a Captions track that sit wholly inside a clip with sound, in the same undo step. The step's name gains "and Re-time Captions". A caption whose speech the clip no longer plays is removed. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
537	- With words selected in the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> removes those words, not the action.
538	- In the Clip tab's lane, a zero-length action draws as a band 2 pt wide. You can click it to select it, but it doesn't drag. The timeline doesn't draw it at all.
539	- Clicking a band on a clip in a multi-clip selection selects that clip alone.
540	
541	## With an agent
542	
543	`set_action` moves an action, changes its length or changes its curve in one step, and `remove_action` removes it. Both need the clip and the action. Give `set_action` any of `start`, `duration` and `curve`, and what you leave out keeps its value. The curves are `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` and `ease_in_out`.
544	
545	Where a band stops, an agent's edit that goes too far fails, with the same reason a typed value gets. When a Speed action changes or goes, the answer lists the captions it re-timed in `captions_retimed` and those it took out in `captions_removed`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
546

557	title: Set what an action animates to
558	description: With an action selected, use the Clip tab or the canvas to set where a clip ends up, read the marks that show what the action changes, and take a property back out.
559	---
560	
561	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
562	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
563	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
564	
565	An [action](/motion/actions/) moves a clip towards its end state: the values the clip reaches when the action finishes. An action made with **Add Action** has an empty end state, so it changes nothing until you say what it animates to.
566	
567	<AtAGlance
568	  where={[
569	    'Clip tab, with an action selected',
570	    'The canvas, with an action selected',
571	    'Right-click a row in the Clip tab',
572	  ]}
573	  tools="set_action_end"
574	/>
575	
576	<Shot
577	  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.inspector"
578	  alt="The Clip tab with action 1 selected on a graphic clip. The Actions header reads editing 1. The Graphic sub-tab shows a count of 3, and so does the Properties section, which has a Clear button. The accent, size and boxed rows each have a diamond in their left gutter. The size slider has a coloured fill and a coral tick, its field has a coloured border, and boxed says at end. The Size and Timeline sections show the ⊘ mark."

580	
581	## Edit the end state
582	
583	<Steps>
584	
585	1. [Select the action](/motion/select-an-action/). Clicking its band also moves the playhead to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing.
586	
587	2. Change any row in the Clip tab. Type a value, drag a slider, pick from a pop-up or choose a colour.
588	
589	3. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to see the clip travel to what you set.
590	
591	</Steps>
592	
593	While an action is selected, every field shows the value the clip reaches at the action's end, and every edit writes that value. Changing a row adds it to the action, and the row gets a ◆.
594	
595	Your edits follow the selected action, not the playhead. If the playhead wanders out of the action's span, the action stays selected and the fields keep showing its end. If it moves into another action's span on the clip, that action becomes the selected one.
596	
597	To edit the clip itself again, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or click the [**Clip** chip](/motion/select-an-action/#the-clip-chip) at the start of the action lane.
598	
599	What happens along the way depends on the kind of value. Numbers and most colours ramp along the action's curve, and switches, pop-ups and text hold and then change at the end. See [How values change over an action](/motion/actions/#how-values-change-over-an-action).
600	
601	## Edit on the canvas
602	
603	With an action selected, the canvas writes the end state too. Moving, scaling, rotating or cropping the clip, nudging it with the arrow keys, dragging a text clip's wrap width and dragging an obscure region all change that action's end, not the clip.
604	
605	The box on screen still shows the frame at the playhead, while a drag starts from the end state and changes it by the distance you drag. With the playhead partway through the action, the box moves only part of the way. Work with the playhead at the action's end, which is where clicking the band puts it, and the box lands where you let go.
606	
607	Two things on the canvas always edit the clip itself:
608	
609	- A drag on a multi-clip selection. Only a single selected clip can have a selected action.
610	- Resizing a shape's box, or dragging a line's or arrow's end points. A shape's own properties can't animate. Moving a shape still writes the action's end.
611	
612	## Switch a property off
613	
614	Untick a switch inside an action and that property turns off when the action ends. **Drop shadow**, a text clip's **Outline** and **Backdrop**, and sound switches such as **Limit peaks** all work this way, and so does a single band of the EQ.
615	
616	The property stays on through the action, then goes off as it ends. The row shows ◆ and "at end".
617	
618	This is different from [taking the row out of the action](#take-a-property-out-of-the-action), which stops the action changing the property at all.
619	
620	## Read the row marks
621	
622	Each row in the Clip tab has a narrow gutter to the left of its label. The mark there says how the row relates to the selected action.
623	
624	| Mark | What it means | How else you can tell |
625	| --- | --- | --- |
626	| ◆ | This action animates the row. | The label turns strong, and a field or pop-up gets a border in the action colour. |
627	| ◇ | Another action on the clip animates the row. | Its tooltip reads "Changed by action N". |
628	| ○ | The row follows a value this action animates. **Gain** follows **Volume**, for example. | |
629	| ⊘ | Actions don't animate this row, so an edit here changes the clip. | The label turns faint. |
630	
631	With an action selected, a blank gutter usually means the row can animate and nothing is animating it yet. It isn't a promise: a few controls carry no mark and still change the clip, such as **In**, **Out** and **Reverse** in the Timing section.
632	
633	◇ also shows when no action is selected, on every row an action on the clip animates. It's a quick way to see what's moving before you pick an action.
634	
635	The **Normalize** button changes the clip whatever is selected. While an action is selected a small boxed **clip** tag follows it, and the tag's tooltip reads "Actions don't animate this. It changes the clip."
636	
637	### The "at end" tag
638	
639	A control that can't blend says "at end" beside it once the action animates it. It holds its old value until the action ends, then switches.
640	
641	Pop-ups, checkboxes, segmented controls and text fields all work this way. Most colours ramp, but a few can't blend, such as a cursor's ripple colour, and those say "at end" too.
642	
643	## See the value change as it plays
644	
645	With an action selected, the field reads the value at the action's end. The rest of the row shows how it gets there.
646	
647	**On a slider**, the rail fills in the action colour from the value at the action's start to the knob. A coral tick marks the value at the playhead. The tick shows whenever the playhead is inside the clip and that value differs from the knob, even with no action selected.
648	
649	**On a row with no slider**, a coral tag gives that value in words, such as "now 1.50×". It shows while the playhead is inside the clip and the value there differs from the field.
650	
651	## Read the sections and sub-tabs
652	
653	Section headers carry the same marks as their rows:
654	
655	- **◆N** counts what the selected action animates in that section.
656	- **◇** means another action animates a row in the section.
657	- **⊘** means every row in the section is ⊘, and the section also says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip."
658	
659	The summary at the right of a header turns the action colour when the action animates the section.
660	
661	### Sub-tab counts
662	
663	Each sub-tab's label shows **◆N** when the selected action animates N things on it, so you can see what an action does without opening every tab.
664	
665	| Sub-tab | What counts |
666	| --- | --- |
667	| Picture | Each property. A zoom action reads ◆3, for its scale and its two position values. |
668	| Color | Light and Color together count as one. Look, Wheels, Curves and Qualifier count as one each, however many values inside them change. On an adjustment clip, Strength counts as one too. |
669	| Sound | Each property. |
670	| Text | Each property. |
671	| Graphic | Each property the action animates. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/). |
672	| Clip | A speed change, as ◆1. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/). |
673	| Shape | Nothing, ever. A shape's own properties can't animate. |
674	
675	### Sections open by themselves
676	
677	Selecting an action opens the sections it animates on the sub-tab you're looking at, and they stay open for as long as that action is selected. A sub-tab you switch to later opens its own animated sections the first time it shows.
678	
679	Close one by hand and it stays closed while that action is selected. Opening by itself doesn't change your own layout: leave the action and the sections it opened go back to how you had them.
680	
681	## Take a property out of the action
682	
683	Taking a property out stops the action changing it. The row falls back to what the clip held before the action, and the action itself stays.
684	
685	| To take out | Do this | Undo step |
686	| --- | --- | --- |
687	| One row | Hover over its ◆ and click the × that replaces it. The tooltip reads "Remove from action N". | Remove from Action |
688	| One row | Right-click it and choose **Remove from action N**. | Remove from Action |
689	| A whole section | Click **Clear** in the section's header. Its tooltip reads "Remove this section from action N". | Clear |
690	| Everything | [Remove the action](/motion/change-an-action/#remove-an-action). | Remove Action |
691	
692	### Clear and Reset
693	
694	**Clear** and **Reset** share one place in a section's header, and at most one of them shows.
695	
696	- While an action is selected, a section with rows that can animate shows **Clear** if the action animates anything in it, and neither button if it doesn't.
697	- A section of ⊘ rows keeps **Reset**, because its edits go to the clip.
698	- There, and in any section with no action selected, **Reset** shows only while the section differs from its defaults.
699	
700	## Right-click a row
701	
702	Right-click a row's label, slider, checkbox or the space beside them. Each item shows only where it applies, and a row with nothing to offer has no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own right-click menu.
703	
704	| Item | When it shows | What it does |
705	| --- | --- | --- |
706	| **Remove from action N** | The selected action animates the row | Takes the row out of the action. |
707	| **Go to action M** | The row shows ◇ | Selects the action that animates the row, and moves the playhead to that action's end. |
708	| **Set end value to default** | An action is selected, and the row has a default and can animate | Sets the value at the action's end to the row's default. |
709	| **Reset to default** | Any other row with a default | Puts the row back to its default. |
710	
711	The two default items are greyed while the row already holds its default.
712	
713	**Set end value to default** and **Remove from action N** aren't the same. The first makes the clip animate to the default. The second stops the action touching the row.
714	
715	## Good to know
716	
717	- Typing the number a field already shows isn't an edit, so it doesn't add the row to the action.
718	- Some rows always change the clip, whatever is selected, and they're marked ⊘. [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/) lists them.
719	- Adding or removing a filter or an obscure region changes the clip even inside an action, though dialling a value inside one animates. If the action already animates that list, the whole list then switches at the action's end rather than ramping.
720	- With several clips selected, the fields edit the clips themselves. The action lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."
721	- An end value Frame Job won't take shows the reason at the foot of the inspector. See [When an edit is refused](/motion/change-an-action/#when-an-edit-is-refused).
722	- Selecting an action isn't an undo step, but each change to its end state is.
723	
724	## With an agent
725	
726	`set_action_end` does what the fields do. It needs the clip, the action and the values to end at, grouped as `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic`, with `speed` beside them. What you send merges into what the action already holds. A key set to `null` takes that property out of the action, and a path listed in `off` switches the property off at the action's end.
727	
728	It can also do one thing the fields can't: send a value past a row's usual range, which is only held to that range as the clip is drawn. There are two exceptions: a graphic's properties are checked when they're set, and a Speed action's rate is held to ×0.1–×1000 when it's set.
729	
730	A few things can't be an action's target, because they belong to the clip: its motion preset (`video.motion`), Hide While Silent (`video.hide_silent`), a text clip's word timing (`text.words`), and a cutout's subject and quality (`video.cutout.subject`, `video.cutout.quality`). Set those with `set_video` or `set_text`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

740	=================== motion/how-edits-move-actions
741	---
742	title: "How edits move actions"
743	description: "See what trimming, splitting, slipping, retiming, copying or freezing a clip does to its actions and its motion presets."
744	---
745	
746	An action's times are measured from the clip's own start, not from the start of the timeline. So moving a clip takes its actions with it, but an edit that changes where the clip starts, how long it is or what it plays can change what an action lands on. This page goes through those edits one at a time, so you know what to expect, and where to look when a zoom no longer lands where you put it.
747	
748	## Trim
749	
750	**Trimming the start** keeps each action's time on the clip. An action 2 s into the clip is still 2 s into the clip afterwards, so it stays put relative to the new start and now plays over different footage.
751	
752	**Trimming the end** leaves actions where they are, so one can end up running past the clip's new end. A start trim shortens the clip too, so it can do the same.
753	
754	Only the part of an action inside the clip plays, so a zoom cut off halfway stops partway in. You can still move that action earlier, shorten it or change its curve, but you can't make it end any later.
755	
756	See [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/).
757	
758	## Slip and roll
759	
760	**Slip** and **Roll** leave actions at the same times on the clip. A slip slides the footage under them. A roll moves the cut between two clips, and the actions on both stay put, as they do for a trim.
761	
762	See [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/).
763	
764	## Speed changes
765	
766	Changing the speed with **Clip ▸ Speed…**, or rate-stretching with an <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag of the end edge, keeps each action at its place as a fraction of the clip. An action a quarter of the way through a clip is still a quarter of the way through, and it gets longer or shorter with the clip. **Clip ▸ Retime Range…** does the same in each clip it changes.
767	
768	The times snap to whole frames, and an action is kept at least one frame long and inside the clip.
769	
770	See [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/), [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) and [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/). A clip with a speed ramp has its own rules, in [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/).
771	
772	## Split
773	
774	**Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>) shares the actions out between the two halves:
775	
776	- An action that ends at or before the cut stays on the first half.
777	- An action that starts at or after the cut goes to the second half, with its times now counted from that half's start.
778	- An action that spans the cut is divided in two. The first piece ends at the values the action had reached at the cut, and the second carries on to the original end state.
779	
780	Both pieces of a divided action keep its curve. The values match at the join, but an eased action can change pace there.
781	
782	## Adding a transition
783	
784	Adding a transition at a hard cut can give the incoming clip a new, earlier first frame, when it has spare footage before the cut. Its actions move with that frame, so a zoom stays on the frame it was drawn over.
785	
786	When there's no spare footage and the incoming clip slides left to make the overlap instead, the clip moves whole and its actions go with it. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/).
787	
788	## Duplicate, copy and paste
789	
790	**Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>), an <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag, and **Edit ▸ Copy** then **Paste** all give copies that keep their actions, and the clip's name travels with them. Each copy's actions are its own, so changing one doesn't touch the other.
791	
792	Pasting into a project with a different frame rate snaps the actions' times to that project's frames.
793	
794	See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/) and [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/).
795	
796	## Nest
797	
798	Clips you [nest](/editing/nests/) keep their actions inside the nest. Open the nest to see and edit them.
799	
800	## Detach Audio
801	
802	**Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (<kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>) gives the new sound clip a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working. An action that only changes the picture does nothing on the sound clip.
803	
804	## Freeze Frame
805	
806	The still that **Clip ▸ Freeze Frame** (<kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd>) makes has no actions. Instead, the look at the frozen frame is baked into the still's own properties: its position, scale, crop and any other picture setting an action had changed by that moment. So it lines up with the frame it froze, and holds there. See [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/).
807	
808	## Add Blurred Background
809	
810	The backdrop copy that **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** makes has no actions, so a zoom on the foreground doesn't zoom the backdrop.
811	
812	## Paste Attributes
813	
814	**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) doesn't copy actions. The clips you paste onto keep the actions they had. See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
815	
816	## What keeps or drops motion
817	
818	[Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/) aren't actions, and they follow their own rules.
819	
820	| Edit | What happens to the presets |
821	| --- | --- |
822	| Duplicate, Paste, Detach Audio | Kept. |
823	| Paste Attributes | Copied, with the rest of the clip's picture settings. |
824	| Freeze Frame | The still has none. It sits where the clip sits with no preset applied, so a freeze taken during an entrance can jump. |
825	| Add Blurred Background | The backdrop has none. The foreground keeps its own. |
826	| Split | The first half gives up its Out and the second half its In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. During stays on both halves and restarts at the cut. |
827	| Change the speed | Kept, and not rescaled. |
828	
829	Because During restarts at each cut, [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.
830	
831	## When a graphic's module changes
832	
833	Editing a graphic's [module](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#modules) can leave an action animating a property the module no longer has, or no longer lets you animate. With that action selected, the property shows as a dimmed row at the end of **Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties**, with its value and a **⌫** button. The tooltip says which of the two happened.
834	
835	Click **⌫** to take the property out of the action. It's one undo step, Remove from Action. An agent does this with `set_action_end`: `graphic.props.<key>: null` takes out one property, and `graphic: null` all of them. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
836	
837	See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
838

846	=================== motion/what-can-animate
847	---
848	title: What an action can animate
849	description: Which properties ramp across an action, which switch at its end, and which can't animate at all, sub-tab by sub-tab.
850	---
851	
852	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
853	
854	An [action](/motion/actions/) can animate most of what's in the Clip tab. This page goes through the tab by sub-tab, so you can see what ramps smoothly, what switches when the action ends, and what can't animate.
855	
856	<AtAGlance
857	  where="Clip tab, with an action selected"
858	  tools="set_action_end"
859	/>
860	
861	With an action selected, the Clip tab marks each row. A row that switches shows "at end" once the action changes it, and most rows that can't animate show ⊘. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for all the marks.
862	
863	One rule applies everywhere. A section you turn on inside an action has no numbers to ramp from, so it appears whole when the action ends. For a gradual start, turn the section on for the clip first and animate its numbers. Turning a section off inside an action turns it off when the action ends.
864	
865	## Picture
866	
867	An action can animate every value in the **Picture** sub-tab, apart from the few under [What never animates](#what-never-animates).
868	
869	| Section | Ramps | Switches at the end |
870	| --- | --- | --- |
871	| [Transform](/canvas/transform/) | **Scale**, **Position X**, **Position Y**, **Rotation**, **Opacity**, [**Motion Blur**](/motion/motion-blur/) | **Blend** |
872	| [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) | | **Behind subject** |
873	| [Crop](/canvas/crop/) | **Left**, **Top**, **Right**, **Bottom** | |
874	| Corner Radius | **Radius** | |
875	| [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/) | **Key Color**, **Tolerance**, **Softness**, **Spill** | **Key out a color** |
876	| [Background](/effects/remove-background/) | **Edge**, **Feather** | **Background** |
877	| [Cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) | **Size**, **Ripple size** | **Show cursor**, **Style**, **Clicks**, **Ripple color** |
878	| [Shadow](/effects/shadow/) | **Color**, **Opacity**, **Blur**, **Angle**, **Distance** | **Drop shadow** |
879	| [Filters](/effects/filters/) | Each filter's **Amount** | A filter's kind |
880	| [Reflection](/effects/reflection/) | **Opacity**, **Height**, **Gap**, **Falloff** | **Mirror the layer below itself** |
881	| [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/) | **Center X**, **Center Y**, **Width**, **Height**, **Feather**, **Dim**, **Zoom** | **Spotlight a region**, **Shape** |
882	| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) | Each region's position, size, **Amount** and **Feather** | A region's kind and **Shape** |
883	
884	Filters and obscure regions follow the [list rule](/motion/actions/#lists). Changing a value inside an existing entry animates, but adding or removing an entry [changes the clip](#what-never-animates).
885	
886	The **Layout** section's **Switch at Playhead** makes actions of its own. See [Camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/).
887	
888	## Color
889	
890	An action can animate the whole grade in the **Color** sub-tab.
891	
892	| Section | What animates |
893	| --- | --- |
894	| Light | Every slider |
895	| Color | Every slider |
896	| [Wheels](/color/wheels/) | Each wheel and its master strip |
897	| [Curves](/color/curves/) | Every channel, whatever the number of points |
898	| [Look](/color/looks/) | **Amount** |
899	| [Adjustment](/color/adjustment-clips/), on an adjustment clip | **Strength** |
900	| [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/), on an adjustment clip | Each range's numbers. **Invert** and turning a range on or off switch at the end |
901	
902	Choosing a look or a LUT, changing it or removing it changes the clip itself, even with an action selected. Only **Amount** animates. If an agent gives an action a different look, it switches at the end. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
903	
904	## Sound
905	
906	An action can animate the **Sound** sub-tab's **Volume** and **Fades** sections, and every other audio setting apart from the few listed under [What never animates](#what-never-animates). <kbd>⌥</kbd>-clicking the [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) adds volume actions too.
907	
908	Numbers ramp. Switches change when the action ends: **Mute**, **Mix to mono**, **Channels**, the EQ's slots and slopes, Hum's mains and harmonics, the Leveller's **Response**, and turning a section on or off. Voice Isolation is the exception: **Isolate voice** and **Amount** both ramp from 0 on a clip with none.
909	
910	**Normalize** sets the clip's own level whatever is selected, and its row shows a small "clip" tag while an action is selected.
911	
912	See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
913	
914	## Text
915	
916	An action can animate the **Text** sub-tab's style, size and colours.
917	
918	| Section | Ramps | Switches at the end |
919	| --- | --- | --- |
920	| Content | | The words |
921	| Font | **Size** | **Family**, **Style** |
922	| Style | **Color**, **Line spacing**, **Tracking** | **Align**, **Vertical**, **UPPERCASE** |
923	| Outline | **Width**, **Color** | **Outline** |
924	| Backdrop | **Fill**, **Padding**, **Radius** | **Backdrop** |
925	| Box | **Width** | **Mode** |
926	| Reveal | **In**, **Out** | **Reveal** |
927	
928	Choosing one of the **Presets** with an action selected sets the action's end state, and each value then ramps or switches as above.
929	
930	A word caption page's timing can't animate, because it belongs to the speech. There's no inspector section for its word colours and pop scale, so only an agent can put those in an action. They ramp when it does. See [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
931	
932	For the rows themselves, see [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/).
933	
934	## Graphics
935	
936	An action can animate a graphic clip's properties in the **Properties** section of the **Graphic** sub-tab. Numbers and colours ramp, while strings, booleans, choices and images switch at the end. A property the graphic marks as not animatable shows ⊘, and so do the **Size** and **Timeline** sections.
937	
938	See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
939	
940	## Speed
941	
942	An action can change a media clip's playback rate, which makes a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/). With an action selected, **Rate** in the **Clip** sub-tab's **Speed** section sets the rate the action ends at, and the clip holds that rate afterwards.
943	
944	- The rate goes from ×0.1 to ×1000.
945	- The clip keeps its start and length, and plays more or less of its source.
946	- Frame Job won't set a rate that would read past the end of the media, and it names the largest rate that fits.
947	- Above ×12 the clip's sound is left out, and Frame Job asks first. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
948	
949	**Keep pitch** and **Fit to** always change the clip.
950	
951	## What never animates
952	
953	These change the clip itself whatever is selected. Unless the list says otherwise, their rows are marked ⊘ in the Clip tab while an action is selected, and a section where every row is ⊘ says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip."
954	
955	- **Clip sub-tab:** the [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/) section, and **Keep pitch** and **Fit to** in the Speed section. The Timing and Transition sections change the clip too, and their rows carry no mark.
956	- **Sound sub-tab:** Ducking, the fade shapes (**In shape** and **Out shape**), the Voice Effect, and a nest clip's **Mix to mono**.
957	- **Picture sub-tab:** the [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) section, **Remove background**, **Subject** and the header's **Reset** (which carries no mark) in the Background section, and **Smoothing**, **Hide when idle** and **Polish** in the Cursor section.
958	- **Filters and Obscure:** adding or removing a filter or a region. These buttons carry no mark. Changing a value inside an existing entry still animates.
959	- **Shape sub-tab:** a [shape's](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) kind, size, corner radius, stroke, fill, gradient and arrows. These rows carry no mark. Its position, scale and opacity animate like any clip's, through the **Picture** sub-tab. Dragging a shape's handles on the canvas to resize it changes the shape itself.
960	- **Graphic sub-tab:** the **Size** and **Timeline** sections, and any property the graphic marks as not animatable.
961	
962	A track's own volume, pan, compressor and limiter aren't part of a clip, so an action can't reach them.
963	
964	## Colours blend in OKLab
965	
966	Every colour an action animates blends through the OKLab colour space. It keeps the midpoints even and avoids the muddy middle of a straight RGB blend. Pure red to pure blue passes through `#8c53a2` halfway, for example, where a straight RGB blend would give the darker `#800080`.
967	
968	This covers the shadow, chroma key, text, outline, backdrop, word caption and graphic colours. Opacity moves separately from the colour. A colour whose two ends are equal stays exact all the way through, and there's no setting for any of this.
969	
970	Shape colours can't animate at all.
971	
972	## With an agent
973	
974	`set_action_end` writes an action's end state. It takes the same keys as `set_video`, `set_audio` and `set_text`, grouped under `video`, `audio` and `text`, with a graphic's properties under `graphic`. A rate goes in `speed`, beside those groups, and `speed: null` takes it back out.
975	
976	Frame Job won't accept the keys that belong to the clip: `video.motion`, `text.words`, `video.cutout.subject` and `video.cutout.quality`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
977

1	=================== motion/motion-presets
2	---
3	title: Motion presets
4	description: Give a clip a ready-made entrance, exit or continuous movement that's tied to its two ends and stays with it through a trim.
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	
10	A motion preset says what a clip does rather than where it is: how it arrives, how it leaves and what it does in between. It's tied to the clip's two ends, so it goes with the clip through a trim and there's nothing to reposition afterwards.
11	
12	Each clip has three slots, and all three can run on the same clip:
13	
14	- **In** is an entrance at the clip's start: Fade, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Slide Left, Slide Right, Slide Up, Slide Down, Spin or Pop. See [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/).
15	- **Out** is an exit at the clip's end, from the same nine kinds.
16	- **During** is a movement for the clip's whole length: Pulse, Shake, Spin, Bounce or Drift. See [During presets](/motion/during-presets/).
17	
18	Presets work on any clip that draws a picture: video, still images, text, shapes, graphics and nests.
19	
20	<AtAGlance
21	  menu={['Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Out', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview']}
22	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Motion presets"
23	  tools="set_video"
24	/>
25	
26	## Give a clip a preset
27	
28	<Steps>
29	
30	1. Select the clip.
31	
32	2. In the Clip tab, pick the **Clip** sub-tab and open **Motion presets**, the last section. It's closed by default.
33	
34	3. Choose a kind from **In**, **Out** or **During**.
35	
36	4. Set **In Duration** or **Out Duration**, or for a During movement, **Amount** and **Period**.
37	
38	5. Choose **Preview** to watch it loop.
39	
40	</Steps>
41	
42	If the defaults suit you, [the Motion menu](#use-the-motion-menu) is quicker.
43	
44	## The Motion presets section
45	
46	| Row | What it does | Range | Default |
47	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
48	| **In** | How the clip enters. | None and nine kinds | None |
49	| **In Duration** | How long the entrance takes. Dimmed while **In** is None. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 | 0.5 s |
50	| **Out** | How the clip leaves. | None and nine kinds | None |
51	| **Out Duration** | How long the exit takes. Dimmed while **Out** is None. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 | 0.5 s |
52	| **During** | What the clip does for its whole length. | None and five kinds | None |
53	| **Amount** | How strong the During movement is. Dimmed while **During** is None. | 0 to 100%, with quick picks of 25, 50, 75 and 100 | 50% |
54	| **Period** | How long one cycle of the During movement takes. Dimmed while **During** is None, and for Drift, which has no cycle. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 | 1 s |
55	| **Preview** | Loops the clip so you can [watch its motion](#preview-a-preset). | | |
56	
57	The two durations and **Period** snap to the project's frame grid. The In is measured from the clip's first frame and the Out back from its last.
58	
59	The section's header sums up the first selected clip's presets, for example "in fade · out slide left · pulse". With no presets it reads "off".
60	
61	## Use the Motion menu
62	
63	**Clip ▸ Motion** has three submenus, **In**, **Out** and **During**, then [**Preview**](#preview-a-preset). Each submenu lists its kinds, then **None** to clear the slot. They work on every selected clip that has a picture, and they're dimmed when no selected clip has one. None of them has a keyboard shortcut.
64	
65	A checkmark shows the kind every selected clip shares. If the clips disagree, nothing is checked. If none of them has a preset in that slot, **None** is checked. A kind can also carry an [(inactive)](#inactive-presets) label.
66	
67	## Change or clear a preset
68	
69	Choosing a different kind keeps the settings the slot already had: an In or Out keeps its duration, and a During keeps its amount and period. A slot that's empty, including one you've set to **None**, starts at the defaults: 0.5 s for an In or Out, and 50% with a 1 s period for a During.
70	
71	To clear one slot, choose **None**. To clear all three, choose **Reset** in the section's header. **Reset** shows only when the first selected clip has a preset, and it clears every selected clip.
72	
73	Each change is one undo step, however many clips are selected.
74	
75	## Set presets on several clips
76	
77	With several clips selected, a change to one slot leaves each clip's other slots as they were. Choosing a new In kind doesn't touch anyone's Out, and each clip keeps its own In duration.
78	
79	The section shows the first selected clip's values, with **mixed** beside a row where the clips differ. That has two effects to watch for:
80	
81	- **In Duration**, **Out Duration**, **Amount** and **Period** only change the clips that have a preset in that slot. The others are left alone.
82	- Those rows are dimmed by the first clip alone. If the first selected clip has no In, **In Duration** is dimmed even when other selected clips have one.
83	
84	## Preview a preset
85	
86	Choose **Preview** in the section, or **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview**. Frame Job sets the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) to the clip, turns [Loop](/timeline/loop/) on, moves the playhead to the clip's start and plays.
87	
88	With several clips selected, it loops the first selected clip that has a picture.
89	
90	The range and Loop stay until you clear them. Choose **Mark ▸ Clear Range** (<kbd>⌥X</kbd>) and click the **Loop** button in the toolbar. A range you'd already set is replaced.
91	
92	## Read presets on the timeline
93	
94	Small marks on a clip's name strip show its presets:
95	
96	- **A wedge at each end** along the bottom of the strip stands for an In or an Out. It's as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom, at least 2 points wide so a short preset still shows, and never wider than the clip. The Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) shows the same two wedges.
97	- **A wave symbol** at the right end of the strip stands for a During movement. On a clip too narrow to fit it, the symbol is left out.
98	
99	See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/) for everything else a clip draws.
100	
101	## Motion sits on top of placement
102	
103	A preset works relative to the clip. Frame Job takes the clip's own placement and any [actions](/motion/actions/) first, then applies the preset on top:
104	
105	- Its scale and opacity multiply the clip's own. A clip at 50% opacity fades in to 50%, not 100%.
106	- Its rotation and offset add to the clip's own.
107	- Anything that changes the clip's size or turns it does so about the clip's visible centre, after any crop.
108	- The drawn size stays within the 1% to 1,000% that **Scale** allows.
109	
110	The three slots add up the same way, so a clip can slide in while it pulses.
111	
112	### The inspector shows un-moved values
113	
114	The fields in the Clip tab show the clip's own numbers, even while the preview and the export show it moving. Halfway through a Zoom In, **Scale** still reads what you typed. That's why editing a clip's position or size works the same with a preset on it.
115	
116	### Dragging during motion
117	
118	A drag on the canvas changes the clip's own position, starting from where it sits without the preset. If you drag partway through a preset, the distance you drag is added to that un-moved position, and the preset keeps playing on top of it. To place a clip by eye, park the playhead where its In has finished and its Out hasn't started.
119	
120	## Overlong presets shorten
121	
122	An In and an Out can together last longer than the clip. Frame Job keeps both and shortens them in proportion to their lengths, so the entrance ends on the frame where the exit begins. A 2 s In and a 1 s Out on a 1.5 s clip play as 1 s and 0.5 s. An In or Out alone that's longer than the clip plays over the clip's whole length.
123	
124	On the timeline the wedges aren't shortened, so they overlap. That's how to spot it. **In Duration** and **Out Duration** keep what you set too, so if you lengthen the clip later, the presets get their full time back.
125	
126	## Inactive presets
127	
128	An In or Out with a zero duration can come from an agent. Frame Job keeps it but it does nothing, and it draws no wedge. It's marked so you can fix it:
129	
130	- The section's summary reads, for example, "in fade (inactive)".
131	- The **Clip ▸ Motion** submenus read **Fade (inactive)**, or **Fade (some inactive)** when only some of the selected clips with that kind have a zero duration.
132	- A note at the top of the section reads "Selection includes inactive In motion (zero duration). Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear." It names **In**, **Out** or **In and Out**, and it counts every selected clip.
133	
134	Changing the kind doesn't fix it, because a new kind keeps the old duration. Raise **In Duration** or **Out Duration**, or choose **None**.
135	
136	## Presets and actions
137	
138	An [action](/motion/actions/) animates a property to a value you set, over a span you place on the clip. A preset is anchored to the clip's ends and says what the clip does. Use a preset for an entrance, an exit or a repeating movement, and an action when a value has to reach a particular number at a particular moment.
139	
140	A preset is never part of an action, and no action can animate one. While an action is selected, the section's rows are marked ⊘ and the section reads "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip." Your edits there write the clip, as they do with no action selected, and **Reset** is still available.
141	
142	## How edits treat a preset
143	
144	| Edit | What happens to the presets |
145	| --- | --- |
146	| Trim | Each preset moves with its edge and keeps its length. |
147	| [Split](/editing/splitting/) | The first half keeps the In and gives up the Out, and the second half keeps the Out and gives up the In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. Both halves keep the During. |
148	| [Change the speed](/speed/change-speed/) | The presets aren't rescaled. A 0.5 s In stays 0.5 s, and a clip that gets much shorter can make its presets [shorten](#overlong-presets-shorten). |
149	| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | The still has no preset, and it sits at the clip's un-moved position, so a freeze taken mid-motion can jump. |
150	| [Add Blurred Background](/canvas/backgrounds/#blurred-background) | The backdrop copy doesn't move. The clip in front keeps its presets. |
151	| [Duplicate](/editing/duplicate-clips/), [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) and [Paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | The presets are kept. |
152	| [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) | Presets are copied with the rest of the picture settings. |
153	
154	A During movement restarts at each cut, because each piece is a clip of its own. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.
155	
156	## Good to know
157	
158	- A preset moves the picture only. A Fade leaves the sound as it is, so use [audio fades](/audio/fades/) for that.
159	- A preset on a [nest](/editing/nests/) moves everything inside the nest together.
160	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) have the section and draw the marks, but there's no picture to move. Only a preset's fade has an effect, and it fades the clip's strength.
161	- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) blurs a preset's movement like any other.
162	- [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) works out its zoom without a During movement, and tells you so with "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it".
163	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) works on an upright picture, so it won't take a clip with Spin in any slot.
164	- Changing the project's frame rate moves the durations and the period onto the new frame grid.
165	
166	## With an agent
167	
168	An agent sets and clears presets with the `motion` key of `set_video`, which is `null` or `{in, out, during}`. `in` and `out` each take a `kind` and a `duration`. `during` takes a `kind`, an `amount` from 0 to 1 and a `period`, and Drift ignores its period. Durations and periods are written in [an agent's time units](/mcp/units-and-ids/#times-in-ticks).
169	
170	A slot left out keeps what it had, a slot set to `null` is cleared, and `{motion: null}` clears all three.
171	
172	An agent isn't held to the section's ranges. Any duration of zero or more is accepted, which is how an [inactive preset](#inactive-presets) comes about, and a period can be outside 0.1 to 10 s as long as it's above zero. Frame Job won't accept an amount outside 0 to 1, which is 0 to 100%. Durations and periods snap to the frame grid, so the value read back can differ a little from the one sent.
173	
174	`get_project` reports the clip's un-moved values, so use `render_frame` to see a preset's effect. `set_action_end` won't take a preset, not even to clear one. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/) for the full list of keys, and [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/#with-an-agent) for the values of `kind`.
175

185	=================== motion/during-presets
186	---
187	title: During presets
188	description: Give a clip a movement that runs all the way through it, such as a pulse, a shake or a slow push-in, and set how strong and how fast it is.
189	---
190	
191	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
192	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
193	
194	A During preset is a movement that runs for a clip's whole length: a gentle pulse, a shake, a spin, a hop or a slow push-in. It's one of a clip's three [motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/), beside [In and Out](/motion/entrances-and-exits/), and it works on any clip that draws a picture: video, stills, text, shapes, graphics and nests.
195	
196	<AtAGlance
197	  menu="Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During"
198	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Motion presets"
199	  tools="set_video"
200	/>
201	
202	## Add a During movement
203	
204	<Steps>
205	
206	1. Select one or more clips.
207	
208	2. On the Clip tab's **Clip** sub-tab, open the **Motion presets** section.
209	
210	3. Choose a kind from **During**: Pulse, Shake, Spin, Bounce or Drift. It starts at half strength with a one-second cycle.
211	
212	4. Set [Amount](#amount) and [Period](#period).
213	
214	5. Choose **Preview** to watch it loop. Preview sets the in and out range to the clip, turns Loop on and plays, and both stay until you clear them.
215	
216	</Steps>
217	
218	**Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During** sets the kind too. A checkmark shows the kind every selected clip shares, and there's no checkmark when they differ. The menu is dimmed with nothing selected, or when every selected clip comes from a sound-only file.
219	
220	To take the movement off, choose **None** in the row or in the menu. Switching straight from one kind to another keeps the Amount and Period you set, but going through **None** clears them, so the next kind starts at 50% and 1 s.
221	
222	A clip with a During movement shows a small wave symbol at the right end of its name strip, when the strip has room.
223	
224	With several clips selected, a new kind goes to every clip that draws a picture, and each clip keeps its own In and Out. **Amount** and **Period** change only the selected clips that already have a During movement. Each change is one undo step, however many clips it touches.
225	
226	## The movements
227	
228	Every kind is described at 100% and at the default 50%. [Amount](#amount) scales between them, and 0% is no movement.
229	
230	### Pulse
231	
232	The clip gently grows and shrinks, once per Period. It starts at its own size, is largest halfway through the cycle, and is back at its own size at the end. At 100% it grows to 20% larger, and at 50% to 10% larger.
233	
234	### Shake
235	
236	The clip jitters in every direction, in a pattern that never visibly repeats. At 100% it moves up to 4% of the canvas's shorter edge on each axis, and at 50% up to 2%. A shorter Period shakes faster.
237	
238	### Spin
239	
240	The clip turns clockwise without stopping. At 50% it makes one full turn per Period, at 100% two turns, and at 25% half a turn.
241	
242	### Bounce
243	
244	The clip hops upward once per Period and lands back where it started. At 100% each hop is up to 8% of the canvas height, and at 50% up to 4%.
245	
246	### Drift
247	
248	A slow push-in across the whole clip. The clip grows steadily from its own size and ends 24% larger at 100%, or 12% larger at 50%.
249	
250	Drift ignores Period. Its speed comes from the clip's length, so a longer clip reaches the same size more slowly.
251	
252	## Amount
253	
254	How strong the movement is, from 0 to 100%, with quick picks at 25, 50, 75 and 100. The default is 50%. A number outside the range is brought back to the nearest end.
255	
256	At 0% the clip stays still but keeps its During kind. **Amount** is greyed while **During** is **None**.
257	
258	## Period
259	
260	How long one cycle takes, from 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks at 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2. The default is 1 s, and what you type lands on the nearest frame.
261	
262	**Period** is greyed while **During** is **None**, and for Drift. Drift keeps the value, so it's still there if you switch to another kind.
263	
264	## How During starts
265	
266	Every During movement starts from the clip's own placement on its first frame. The clip begins exactly where you put it, whatever it goes on to do.
267	
268	The movement sits on top of that placement and of any [actions](/motion/actions/). Its size multiplies the clip's own scale, and its turn and offset add to the clip's own rotation and position. Pulse, Spin and Drift work around the clip's visible centre, after any crop.
269	
270	The inspector still shows the clip's own values, not the moved ones, even though the preview and the export show it moving.
271	
272	## During with In and Out
273	
274	A During movement runs under the In and Out, so a clip can slide in while it pulses. Their sizes multiply, and their turns and offsets add, so a Spin entrance and a During Spin turn together.
275	
276	A During movement never changes a clip's opacity. Only In and Out fade a clip.
277	
278	## During restarts at a cut
279	
280	A During movement counts from each clip's own first frame, so cutting a clip restarts it. After a [split](/editing/splitting/), both halves keep the movement and the second half starts over.
281	
282	That can show as a jump at the cut. A Pulse goes back to the start of its cycle, and a Drift drops back to the clip's own size and drifts again across the shorter piece. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at every cut.
283	
284	To keep one movement going across cuts, [nest](/editing/nests/) the pieces and give the nest clip the During movement.
285	
286	## Good to know
287	
288	- A preset is not part of any [action](/motion/what-can-animate/). With an action selected, the **Motion presets** rows are marked ⊘ and still edit the clip, so **Amount** can't ramp.
289	- Changing a clip's speed doesn't change its During movement. **Period** stays the same length on the timeline, and a Drift spreads over the clip's new length.
290	- Inside a nest, Shake and Bounce measure against the nest's canvas, not the project's.
291	- A Pulse or Drift can't draw a clip past 1,000%, the largest scale a clip can have.
292	- Freeze Frame and Add Blurred Background leave the movement behind. Duplicate, Detach Audio and Paste keep it.
293	- A drag on the canvas that starts while the clip is moving starts from the clip's own position, not the moved one.
294	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) won't frame a clip with a Spin, whether it's the In, the Out or the During, because it needs an upright picture.
295	- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) counts a During movement as motion.
296	
297	## With an agent
298	
299	An agent sets During through `set_video`, with a `kind` of `pulse`, `shake`, `spin`, `bounce` or `drift`, an `amount` from 0 to 1, and a `period`.
300	
301	An agent isn't held to the row's range for Period. A period shorter than one frame becomes one frame. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#motion).
302
