325	---
326	title: Edit a ramped clip
327	description: What a speed change, trim, split or freeze frame does to a clip with a speed ramp, and why Frame Job sometimes won't make the edit.
328	---
329	
330	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
331	
332	Once a clip has a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), your ordinary edits still work on it. This page says what each one does to the ramp, and what stops an edit that would break it.
333	
334	<AtAGlance
335	  menu="Clip ▸ Speed…"
336	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', '⌥-drag a clip\'s end edge', 'The action lane']}
337	  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'set_action']}
338	/>
339	
340	## Scale a whole ramp
341	
342	These all change a ramped clip's speed by scaling the whole ramp by one factor:
343	
344	- **Clip ▸ Speed…**
345	- **Rate** in the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/), with no action selected
346	- **Fit to** in the Speed section
347	- The ⌥ [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) on the clip's end edge
348	- [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/), for the part of the clip inside the range
349	
350	The clip's own rate, every end rate and the length of every Speed action scale together, so the ramp keeps its shape and the clip still plays the same stretch of its file. The clip itself gets shorter or longer. A ramp from ×1 to ×2 scaled by ×2 becomes a ramp from ×2 to ×4, in half the time. With a ramped clip selected, the Speed sheet's readout ends "Each speed ramp keeps its shape: the rates it names scale with the base rate."
351	
352	No rate in a clip can go below ×0.1 or above ×1000, and what happens at those limits depends on how you made the change:
353	
354	| You used | At a limit |
355	| --- | --- |
356	| **Speed…**, **Rate** or **Fit to** | Scaling stops at the limit, so the clip's rate can end up short of the rate you asked for. |
357	| The ⌥ rate stretch | Nothing happens. |
358	| Retime Range | Frame Job won't make the edit, and the reason names the clip and the rate. |
359	
360	To change one rate inside the ramp instead, select its action. **Rate** then sets that action's end rate. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).
361	
362	## Edits follow the ramp
363	
364	Trims, slips, rolls, splits, freeze frames and transitions all read the ramp, so each cut or held frame is the frame the ramp actually plays at that moment.
365	
366	| Edit | What it does on a ramped clip |
367	| --- | --- |
368	| [Trim](/editing/trimming/) the start | The frame under the edge stays put. The Speed actions stay the same distance from the clip's start, so what plays after the new start can change. The edge stops where the clip would otherwise play past the end of its file. |
369	| Trim the end | The Speed actions don't move. How far you can pull the end out depends on the rate the clip reaches, not on its own rate. |
370	| [Roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) | The later clip's start behaves as a start trim, and the earlier clip's end as an end trim. |
371	| [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/) | The source moves at the clip's own rate, and the Speed actions stay where they are. It stops so the clip never plays past the end of its file. |
372	| [Split](#split-inside-a-speed-action) | The two halves meet at the frame the ramp plays at the cut, and the second half starts at the rate playing there. |
373	| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | The still holds the frame the ramp plays at that moment. |
374	| [Transition](/motion/add-a-transition/) | The overlap follows the ramp. The earlier clip carries on past its old end, and the extra footage before the later clip's start plays at that clip's own rate. The later clip still ends on the same frame of its file. |
375	| [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | The separate audio clip gets the same ramp. |
376	
377	[**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**](/editing/paste-attributes/) never copies a speed or a ramp.
378	
379	Transcribing a ramped clip places each word where the ramp plays it. Captions already on the timeline [follow a later change to the ramp](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
380	
381	## Split inside a Speed action
382	
383	Splitting partway through a Speed action keeps the picture continuous at the cut, with no repeated or skipped frame. The action becomes two, one on each half. The first ends at whatever rate makes the picture meet at the cut, and the second keeps the original end rate.
384	
385	The action's curve matters here:
386	
387	- With **Ease Out** or **Ease In Out**, the rate can jump at the cut.
388	- With **Ease In** or **Ease In Out**, the second half can end on a different frame of the file than the unsplit clip did. If it would then play past the end of the file, its end rate is lowered to the largest that fits.
389	
390	## Filmstrip and waveform
391	
392	A ramped clip's filmstrip and waveform follow the ramp, so what you see at a point on the timeline is what plays there. A stretch at a high rate shows more of the file in the same space.
393	
394	## An action past the clip's end
395	
396	After a trim, or after a ramp is scaled, a Speed action can lie partly or wholly past the clip's end. It stays on the clip, and you can still change its curve, move it earlier or shorten it. Being past the end stops only a change that takes it further past.
397	
398	Its end rate still counts for the [×12 rule](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/), even though that part never plays. If a clip is silent though it never seems to pass ×12, look for an action like this.
399	
400	## When a ramp edit can't be made
401	
402	A ramped clip keeps its place and its length on the timeline, so a ramp can't play past the end of the clip's file. Frame Job won't make an edit that would, and the reason says what would fit: the largest rate, or the latest clip end. [Never past the end of the file](/speed/speed-ramps/#never-past-the-end-of-the-file) lists what each edit names.
403	
404	**Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** has a few more conditions, such as a span that overlaps another action. See [When Apply is unavailable](/speed/make-a-ramp/#when-apply-is-unavailable).
405	
406	A clip with [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) is linked to its audio, so no speed or ramp edit will change it. The reason says to use Attach Audio first.
407	
408	Whatever stops the edit, nothing changes. Frame Job beeps, makes no undo step, and shows the reason:
409	
410	- **At the foot of the inspector**, after the word "Refused:". It stays until the project changes or you click it. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
411	- **In the Speed Ramp sheet's readout**, as you adjust the sheet, so nothing has been applied and there's no beep. **Apply** is dimmed until the preset fits.
412	
413	Dragging an action's band is different. There's no beep and no reason, and the band stays at the last place that worked.
414	
415	A reason can give a time in ticks, the unit Frame Job counts time in. There are 600,000 ticks in a second, so 1,200,000 ticks is 2 seconds.
416

425	=================== speed/ramp-audio
426	---
427	title: Sound on a ramp
428	description: How Frame Job renders the sound of a ramped clip in the background, why the clip goes silent for a moment, and what an export does about it.
429	---
430	
431	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
432	
433	A clip whose speed changes as it plays can't play its sound straight from the file, so Frame Job renders that sound in the background. While it renders, the clip is silent in the preview. An export always waits for it.
434	
435	<AtAGlance
436	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section ▸ Keep pitch"
437	  tools={['set_speed', 'export']}
438	/>
439	
440	## Rendered audio
441	
442	Two kinds of clip have their sound rendered into a separate file:
443	
444	- a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), with **Keep pitch** on or off
445	- a clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with **Keep pitch** off
446	
447	A clip at a constant speed with **Keep pitch** on isn't rendered, and neither is a clip above ×12, because [it has no sound](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
448	
449	There's nothing to start. A new render begins after each edit that changes the clip's timing, such as a ramp, its rate, a trim or a split, and after you change **Keep pitch**. During a drag, it waits until you let go.
450	
451	Each render covers the whole clip's sound, so how long it takes grows with the clip's length and rate. Renders run one at a time, in the background, so you can keep editing. An edit that makes a render out of date drops it, so a run of quick edits doesn't queue up work.
452	
453	The files are saved inside the project package, in `cache/ramp-audio/`, and Frame Job can rebuild them. Until a new project is saved, they're in a temporary folder. [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) doesn't copy them, so the new project renders its own.
454	
455	## Keep pitch off
456	
457	The sound glides smoothly up and down in pitch with the rate, like tape, and stays in step with the picture. At a constant speed it plays at that speed's tape pitch.
458	
459	## Keep pitch on
460	
461	The sound keeps its own pitch as the speed changes. After a deep slow-down, such as ×2 to ×0.5, it can run up to about 24 ms behind the picture.
462	
463	See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) for the control itself.
464	
465	## Silent while it renders
466	
467	While a clip's sound is rendering, that clip plays silent in the preview. Everything else on the timeline plays as usual, and the clip's sound comes back on its own when the render finishes.
468	
469	## Undo and redo render again
470	
471	Undo and redo usually start a render too, because Frame Job drops the file from before the edit once a newer render lands. The clip is briefly silent then as well.
472	
473	## Exports wait for it
474	
475	An export waits for every render it needs and never writes that sound silent. The Exporting sheet reads "Preparing “*name*”…" during the wait, and a queued export's row reads `Writing · 0 %`. You can cancel either one there. This covers speed ramps and clips at a constant speed other than ×1 with **Keep pitch** off.
476	
477	An animated GIF or APNG has no sound, so it doesn't wait. An export an agent starts with `export` waits the same way.
478	
479	## A failed render
480	
481	If a render fails, an export that needs it stops with this message, naming the clip:
482	
483	> Clip N's retimed audio could not be rendered: …
484	
485	Frame Job doesn't try a failed render again while it stays open. The clip stays silent, and exports that need it keep failing, until you change the clip's timing, which starts a new render, or quit and reopen Frame Job.
486

494	=================== speed/keep-pitch
495	---
496	title: "Keep pitch"
497	description: "Choose whether a clip's sound keeps its own pitch at a new speed or follows the speed like tape, and know when that sound is silent while it renders."
498	---
499	
500	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
501	
502	When a clip plays faster or slower, its sound can do one of two things. Keep pitch decides which.
503	
504	<AtAGlance
505	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed… ▸ Preserve pitch', 'Clip ▸ Retime Range… ▸ Preserve pitch']}
506	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Speed section ▸ Keep pitch"
507	  tools={['set_speed', 'retime_range', 'set_audio']}
508	/>
509	
510	## What it does
511	
512	| Setting | The sound |
513	| --- | --- |
514	| On | The voice or music keeps its own pitch at the new speed. |
515	| Off | The pitch follows the speed, higher when faster and lower when slower, like tape or a record. |
516	
517	The setting belongs to the clip and is on for a new clip. Above ×12 a clip has no sound either way. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
518	
519	It also controls how a speed ramp sounds. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/).
520	
521	## Keep pitch in the inspector
522	
523	Tick or untick **Keep pitch** in the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/#keep-pitch). It applies to every selected media clip as one undo step, **Keep Pitch**.
524	
525	## Preserve pitch in the Speed sheet
526	
527	The [Speed sheet](/speed/change-speed/) calls the same setting **Preserve pitch**. It opens on the first selected clip's setting, and **Apply** sets it on every listed clip. Changing it alone counts as a change for **Apply**.
528	
529	The [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) sheet has a **Preserve pitch** box too, for the clips in the range.
530	
531	## Tape pitch is rendered in the background
532	
533	With Keep pitch off, at any rate but ×1 and up to ×12, Frame Job renders the clip's sound in the background before it plays. The clip is silent in the preview until that finishes. When it's ready, the sound plays at that speed's tape pitch.
534	
535	- Renders run one at a time, and the wait grows with the clip's length and, above ×1, its rate.
536	- A change to the clip's timing, such as a new rate, a trim or a split, starts a new render.
537	- Undo and redo render again too, because the file from before the edit isn't kept. The clip is briefly silent after an undo as well.
538	- In a saved project, the rendered sound is kept in the project package.
539	
540	An export waits for every render it needs, so that sound is never silent in the file. The **Exporting** sheet reads "Preparing" and the file's name during the wait, for example "Preparing “movie.mp4”…".
541	
542	If a render fails, the export stops with "Clip N's retimed audio could not be rendered: …". Frame Job doesn't try that render again while it stays open, so the clip stays silent in the preview. Change the clip's timing to start a new render, or quit and reopen Frame Job.
543	
544	With Keep pitch on, a constant speed needs no render and plays straight away.
545	
546	## Good to know
547	
548	- **It always applies to the whole clip**, even with an action selected, and it can't be animated. In an action, its row is marked ⊘.
549	- **Across clips at different rates**, the inspector's checkbox also brings them all to the first clip's rate. See [Keep pitch in the Speed section](/speed/speed-section/#keep-pitch).
550	- **Linked clips.** Keep pitch isn't a rate, so you can change it on a clip that's linked to its detached sound.
551	- **Very small speed changes.** With Keep pitch on, a rate within 0.1% of ×1 plays as plain varispeed, which moves the pitch by under 1.74 cents, too little to hear. From ×0.98 to ×1.02, outside that band, Frame Job uses a stretch suited to small changes.
552	- **Synchronize Audio** turns Keep pitch off on a clip it corrects for drift. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).
553	
554	## With an agent
555	
556	`set_speed`, `retime_range` and `set_audio` all take `keep_pitch`. Leave it out and the setting stays as it is. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
557

566	title: "Sound at high speed"
567	description: "Why a clip goes silent above ×12, what the alert asks before it happens, and how ramps count towards the limit."
568	---
569	
570	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
571	
572	A clip that plays faster than ×12 loses its sound in the preview and in the export, while its picture keeps playing. Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip there.
573	
574	<AtAGlance
575	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…', 'Clip ▸ Retime Range…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…']}
576	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', 'The ⌥ rate stretch on the timeline']}
577	  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'set_action_end', 'retime_range']}
578	/>
579	
580	## Sound is left out above ×12
581	
582	The limit is the same with [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) on or off. At exactly ×12 the sound still plays, and at anything faster it doesn't. The picture carries on to the top of the speed range, ×1000.
583	
584	The limit is fixed, and no setting changes it. It sits a margin below the speeds at which an export with sound can stall.
585	
586	Nothing is deleted. Bring the clip back to ×12 or below and its sound returns.
587	
588	## The alert
589	
590	Before an edit takes a clip with sound from ×12 or below to above ×12, an alert asks first. For one clip it reads:
591	
592	> “Interview” will be silent at ×16.
593	>
594	> Frame Job leaves a clip’s audio out above ×12. The picture still plays.
595	
596	For several clips it counts them. It reads “3 clips will be silent at ×16.”, or “3 clips will be silent at their new speeds.” when their rates differ, and then “Frame Job leaves a clip’s audio out above ×12. The pictures still play.”
597	
598	The alert is a question, not a block. You can always go ahead.
599	
600	| Button | What it does |
601	| --- | --- |
602	| **Set Speed** | Makes the edit exactly as you asked. It's the default button, and it keeps this name when the edit is a ramp or a stretch. |
603	| **Cancel** | Changes nothing and adds no undo step. |
604	
605	You're asked once. A clip that's already above ×12 isn't asked about again, even if you make it faster still. A clip whose sound is switched off, or whose file has no sound, isn't asked about at all.
606	
607	## Where the alert appears
608	
609	| You're using | If you choose **Cancel** |
610	| --- | --- |
611	| **Clip ▸ Speed…** | The sheet stays open. |
612	| **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** | The sheet stays open. |
613	| **Clip ▸ Retime Range…** | The sheet stays open. |
614	| **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | The sheet stays open. |
615	| The [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/): **Rate**, its quick picks, **Keep pitch**, **Reset** or **Fit to** | The fields go back to what they showed. |
616	| The [⌥ rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) | The clip stays as it was before the drag. |
617	
618	A stretch is put back when you let go, so nothing has changed while the question is up. **Set Speed** then applies it again.
619	
620	Moving, resizing or removing an action can't raise a clip's fastest rate, so those edits never ask.
621	
622	## Ramps and the ×12 rule
623	
624	On a [ramped clip](/speed/speed-ramps/), Frame Job looks at the fastest rate set anywhere on the clip. If any rate in the ramp is above ×12, the whole clip is silent, not only the fast part.
625	
626	The alert counts the ramp's peak rate in the same way. A clip at ×1 with one Speed action ending at ×16 is asked about at ×16.
627	
628	An end rate on an action lying past the clip's end still counts, even though that part never plays. If a trimmed clip has gone silent for no clear reason, check the count in the header of its [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) in the Clip tab. An action wholly past the clip's end has no band you can reach, but it's still counted.
629	
630	## The silent audio note
631	
632	The Speed section shows **Audio is silent above ×12** while a selected clip is past the limit. It needs a clip whose file has sound and whose sound is on. It appears in either pitch mode, and a ramp counts by its fastest rate.
633	
634	## Good to know
635	
636	- A clip that only has sound follows the same rule, and is silent above ×12.
637	- Clips inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) count too.
638	- Turning a clip's sound back on while it's above ×12 doesn't bring up the alert, because the speed didn't change. The silent audio note shows instead.
639	- When Speed Up Typing runs by itself after a [recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/), Frame Job can't stop to ask. A speed-up that would silence a clip isn't made, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector.
640	
641	## With an agent
642	
643	An agent is never asked. Its edit goes through, and the result lists the ids of the clips that went silent in `audio_left_out`, with a sentence saying so in `audio_note`. Neither appears if no clip crossed the limit. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
644	
645	## Related
646	
647	- [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/)
648	- [The Speed section](/speed/speed-section/)
649	- [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/)
650	- [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/)
651	- [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/)
652	=================== speed/captions-and-speed
653	---
654	title: Captions follow a speed change
655	description: How captions stay on the speech when a clip's speed or ramp changes, which ones move, and which ones Frame Job removes.
656	---
657	
658	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
659	
660	When you change the speed of a clip with sound, the captions over it move with its speech, so they stay on the words you hear. There's nothing to turn on.
661	
662	<AtAGlance
663	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…']}
664	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', 'The action lane', '⌥-drag a clip\'s end edge']}
665	  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
666	/>
667	
668	## What moves them
669	
670	Captions move when you:
671	
672	- change the clip's speed, with **Clip ▸ Speed…**, the Speed section or the ⌥ rate stretch
673	- add a ramp with **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**
674	- add, move, resize, edit or remove a Speed action on the clip
675	
676	The captions move in the same undo step as the edit, so one undo puts them back too. The step is named after the edit with "and Re-time Captions" added, such as **Set Speed and Re-time Captions**. A drag moves them when you let go of the mouse.
677	
678	The clip has to be one captions could have been made from: it plays media with sound, its audio is on, and it isn't reversed.
679	
680	## Which captions move
681	
682	A caption moves when all of these are true:
683	
684	- It's a text clip on a track named **Captions** or **Captions N**, such as **Captions 2**.
685	- That track holds only text clips and isn't locked.
686	- It lies wholly inside the clip you edited.
687	
688	A caption that runs past either edge of the clip stays where it is, and so does anything on another track.
689	
690	## Speech the clip no longer plays
691	
692	A ramp that slows a clip down makes it play less of its file, so it can stop reaching speech it played before.
693	
694	A caption whose speech the clip no longer reaches is removed. A word caption page that's only partly reached keeps the words that still play, and its text is cut to match.
695	
696	## Newly revealed speech
697	
698	When a ramp makes the clip play further into its file, the new part gets no captions. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) again to caption it.
699	
700	## Neighbouring captions
701	
702	A moved caption is cut back where it would run into a caption that didn't move. One that would start inside such a caption, or end up shorter than a frame, is removed.
703	
704	## Good to know
705	
706	- Only speed and ramp edits re-time captions. A trim, slip or split leaves them where they are.
707	- [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) works differently. It stretches or squeezes a text clip in the range along with everything else, and Frame Job won't retime a range that touches a caption page with timed words.
708	- Frame Job checks every caption's new place before it makes the edit. If they don't all work out, the speed edit goes through on its own and the captions stay where they were.
709	
710	## With an agent
711	
712	`set_speed`, `rate_stretch`, `add_speed_ramp`, `set_action`, `remove_action` and `set_action_end` re-time captions the same way, in the same undo step. `set_action_end` does so only when it changes the speed.
713	
714	The result lists the caption clips that moved in `captions_retimed` and the ones removed in `captions_removed`. Each key appears only when it has something in it. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/) and [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
715	
716	## Related

3:description: Frame Job's own words in plain terms, from action and canvas to nest, ramp, stem and tick, each linked to its page.
10:- **Action.** An animation on a clip: a span on its action lane with an end state its properties ease to. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).
16:- **Frame grid.** The frames of the project's rate. Every time you set lands on one. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
26:- **Selected action.** The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing. While it's chosen, the fields show and write its end state. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/).
45:- **Ramp.** A speed change over time, a Speed action on the action lane. See [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/).
49:- **Transition.** The change from one clip to the next across their overlap on one track. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
---LIMITS

60:| Slowest rate | ×0.1 |
61:| Fastest rate | ×1000 |
62:| Fastest rate with sound | ×12, with Keep pitch on or off |
63:| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) length, when none is given | 2 s |
64:| [Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) **Hold** | None, 25%, 50% or 75%, 50% by default. An agent can use any hold from 0 to 0.9. |
66:Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip with sound past ×12. On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
68:With Keep pitch on, a ramp's sound can lag the picture by up to about 24 ms after a steep slow-down. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/), and [Speed at a glance](/speed/overview/) for how the rates fit together.

Frame Job won't add one that would overlap another action or run past the clip's end. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/). | A selected clip is under the playhead |

102:| **Retime Range…** | | Plays the in/out range faster or slower on every unlocked track and moves what follows to stay in step, in one undo step, "Retime Range". See [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/). | An in/out range is set. It works inside a nest |
118:## Transition

122:**Transition ▸** sets the transition into the clip. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/).
124:The rows are **Cross Dissolve**, **Fade Through Black**, **Fade Through White**, **Push Left**, **Push Right**, **Push Up**, **Push Down**, **Wipe**, **Slide**, **Zoom**, **Wipe Left**, **Wipe Up** and **Wipe Down**, then **None**. A checkmark shows the selected clip's transition.

129:| **None** | Something is selected, so a transition the timeline doesn't show can always be cleared. |
131:At a hard cut it aims for a transition 0.5 s long, snapped to frames, and makes a shorter one when the clips have less footage to spare. Where neither side of the cut has a frame to spare, a sheet says so and offers **Shift Clips Left**, which slides the second clip and everything after it on unlocked tracks left by half a second.
133:## Motion
137:**Motion ▸** sets how the clip enters, leaves and moves, and previews the result. Every item is available when a selected clip is anything but sound alone. See [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).

170:It's available when a selected clip plays a video file, is a freeze frame of one, or is a picture.
202:A row is available when exactly one clip is selected, its track isn't locked, it isn't linked to a detached sound, and that row's track still covers it with video clips. It works inside a nest.
214:| **Add Blurred Background** | Adds a blurred copy of the picture with the same start, duration and speed, playing the same part of its media. The copy is muted, and has none of the clip's transition, actions or label. | Exactly one clip is selected and it's a video, image, still, shape or graphic clip. # app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c));
  `PlanSegment.path` (the clip alone when absent) and `origin` (nil) read a nested audio
  segment's instance (spec §11 TX-10); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and
  `gates` a gated clip's hide-while-silent gate (format 43, spec §11 CO-93). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and
  `RecipeCursor` (the recipe layer's `cursor`, `media` and `at` required).
  `CutoutProps.swift` (format 39, road map creator-jobs CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21;
  `foreground` and the image arm format 41, CO10a, CO-100, CO-101) holds `CutoutSubject`
  (`person`, `foreground`), `CutoutQuality`, `CutoutBackground`, `CutoutProps` (`VideoProps.cutout` and
  `VideoPatch.cutout`; its `dictionary` writes all five keys), `CutoutPatch` (the sparse
  write `VideoPatch.cutoutPart` carries — written under `cutout` only when `cutout` is nil,
  never decoded — so a Background, Edge or Feather row writes its own key alone, CO3),
  `RecipeCutoutMaskKind` (`media`, and `image`, drawn since CO10b from the
  picture's one mask, CO-107),
  `RecipeCutoutMask` (`kind` and `media` required; `subject` lenient,
  `person` when absent, CO-101) and `RecipeCutout` (the recipe layer's
  `cutout`, `mask` required; `subjectCopy`, CO-51); `RecipeLayer.videoProps` passes no cutout — the recipe's is a draw
  instruction, not the clip's props. `VideoProps.swift` (`VideoProps`),
  `ClipSnapshot.swift` (`ClipSource` with its nested `CodingKeys`, `ClipSnapshot`,
  `TransitionSnapshot`) and `TrackSnapshot.swift` (`TrackSnapshot`) are pure moves out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T11–T13). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name
  (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an action's `curve`,
  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the
  APP's writer saying all three slots, not a replace rule, and it is the only
  edge that writes a whole motion. `MotionEdge` also supplies nonpersisted
  zero-duration activity and inactive display/menu titles (E2-27).
  `TextProps.swift` is the text group and `RecipeReveal` (with format version
  9's `textCase` / `words` / `wordStyle`, the recipe's `word` / `wordPop` and,
  since format version 12, `wordGlide` / `wordFill` / `wordDim`), a pure move
  out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift` because a stored property cannot be added
  from an extension. `RecipeReveal` reads and writes its OWN keys — siblings of
  `hash` and `text` in the `text` source — through `init(siblingsOf:)` and
  `encodeSiblings(to:)`, so a new recipe key costs `FrameRecipe.swift`
  nothing; a key spelled other than the snake-case converter spells it
  decodes silently to that key's default (the amount to 1, the rest to nil).
  `ProjectSnapshot+Graphic.swift` mirrors
  `model_graphic.rs`'s `GraphicProps` as `GraphicSnapshot` (`in` is
  `sourceIn`) and `GraphicPropValue` (string, number, bool; anything else
  `.null`), decoded into `ClipSnapshot.graphic`; `props` keys keep the
  module's own spelling (snake-case conversion does not reach a dictionary's
  keys). `WordProps.swift` mirrors `model_words.rs`
  (`TextCase`, `TextWord`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill`, `WordStyle`)
  — `WordStyle.dictionary` writes ALL eight keys (`active_fill` and `pause_dim` since format version 12; `ActivePill.dictionary` writes `glide`), `NSNull` for a nil slot,
  `MotionProps.dictionary`'s rule, because the core deep-merges
  `word_style` — and holds
  what the renderer and the inspector share: `laidContent` (`case` applied —
  every layout and string index is in ITS UTF-16 space, never `content`'s),
  `tokenCount`, `isUntimedPage`, `TextPatch.contentEdit` and
  `InspectorBinding.contentOps` / `ops(textContent:)` — the Content write,
  decided PER CLIP: `words: []` beside the content in one `set_text` only for
  base clips whose count changed, and never `words` in an action end (W-2,
  W-6). It lives there, not in `InspectorPane.swift`, for the size rule.

**The document.**
- `ProjectDocument.swift` (+`DisplayStem`, +`Recording`, +`SelectedAction`, +`Import`, +`Graphics`, +`GraphicFiles`, +`UndoGroup`, +`CacheSaves`, +`Alerts`, +`Reverse`, +`Derived`)
  — NSDocument, `.framejob` package read/write, and the single mutation
  point (see Undo); `applyEdit`'s `.refused` arm beeps and then posts
  `projectDocumentDidRefuse` with the `ReelRefusal` (spec §11 CI-10), which
  the editor forwards to the inspector's refusal strip. Holds the SIX pieces of view state nothing persists —
  playhead, clip selection, in/out range, `selectedMedia`, `nestPath` and
  `selectedAction` — re-clamped by `clampViewState` in that order with the
  scope FIRST, since the selection clamp measures against whatever
  container the scope left. `selectedAction` (spec §11 CI-1) is nil or one
  action of the SINGLE selected clip; `+SelectedAction` holds its queries,
  its one deliberate writer `selectAction(_:)` (which stores nil for an id
  that is not `singleSelectedClip`'s) and the ENTRY rule
  `syncSelectedAction()`, run from `playhead`'s and `selection`'s `didSet`
  against `lastInsideAction`. The clamp re-reads `lastInsideAction` BEFORE
  its last line writes the playhead, so an edit, undo or redo under a
  stationary playhead never enters a span — keep those two lines above
  that write. `nestPath` is a
  PATH of (nest, clip) steps, not a nest id, because two clips can show one
  nest at two starts; `editedProject` is a STORED, memoised `rc_project_scoped`
  handle, and `project` still means the parent for save, export and
  consolidate. A range is cleared on every scope change: a pair of ticks means
  one thing inside a nest and another to an export. `+UndoGroup`:
  `inUndoGroupIfRegistered` runs a body with an undo group pending, and
  `registerUndo(restoring:actionName:)`'s first statement
  (`openPendingUndoGroup()`) opens it at the body's first registration, at the
  body's level and never while undoing or redoing; a body that registers
  nothing leaves undo and redo untouched (#167); `registerUndo` stays the one
  registrar. `applyEdit(_:_:amending:)` (#272) undoes the step that ended at
  `step` before committing, when `project` is still that handle, so a strip's
  off-knob double-click is one step. `cacheDirectory` calls `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` when it
  creates `cache/` — only if the package's date, read through a fresh `URL`
  before the create, is still `fileModificationDate`, so an outside change made before it is not absorbed — and that method re-reads the date through a fresh
  `URL`, because `fileURL` still holds the date it cached at open (#138).
  `+CacheSaves` is the `save(to:ofType:for:completionHandler:)` override
  every save funnels through, bracketing it with the cache ledger's
  `saveBegan` / `saveEnded` (#115, #169).
  `+Import` is File ▸ Add Media… and every drop into an open project
  (`importMedia`, the probe chain and the one grouped commit), the opening
  read's probe (`probeForOpening`, a cancelled copy as `.userCancelled`), and the Media
  tab's Relink… and the missing-media sheet's body (`relinkMedia(_:)`: each
  file probed through `MediaImporter.probe`, one grouped "Relink Media" edit
  carrying each descriptor as `relink_media`'s `probe`, spec §11 #63, then
  `generateCaches()`; the missing-media sheet's door then alerts each
  unreadable file and each refused sentence (#180) through `present(_:)`).
  `+MissingCopies` re-copies, on open, a WebM/MKV copy that is missing or in
  the Trash from its recorded original (spec §11 #228-O), through
  `MediaImporter.probeBuiltInCopy` (never ffmpeg, never a question); a
  read on main or inside `withoutAsking` (an agent's `open_project`, off
  main since #231) passes no watch; and, after the media re-anchor and
  before the re-copy, `reanchoringCursorFiles` re-points a cursor file found
  again at `<package>/media/<same name>` (spec §11 CU-52).
  `+Alerts` is `present(_:)`: every error the document shows waits in one
  queue (`DocumentAlertQueue`) and shows one alert sheet at a time, each asked
  for a main-queue turn after the last one's `didPresent` or the window's last
  sheet end, and only while no sheet is attached, since AppKit drops an error
  sheet asked for while another is attached (#195, `relink_sheet_probe.py`
  A1–A5); with no window, it is app-modal at once. `+Graphics`
  is the document's side of the package's `graphics/`:
  `startGraphicStore()`, run from `makeWindowControllers()` and seeding an
  untitled document's root from `autosavedContentsFileURL/graphics`, and
  `graphicsWrapper()`, the lazy wrapper the save whitelist carries — for a
  SAVED document it reads `<fileURL>/graphics` itself and never asks the
  store, so a nil store can never drop a saved folder; for an untitled one
  it carries the store's root only when `GraphicStore.holdsContent` (an
  entry, file or directory, that is neither hidden nor the manual) says so

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is

traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

**The core's edge.**

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
  by `model_props.rs`.
- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `cursor_file.rs` — the cursor file, format v1 (road map "creator-jobs" CU1a, spec
  §11 CU-10): its module doc IS the format's specification (the header, the columns
  in integer µs and points × 100, the caps, every refusal's sentence, the parse
  order); `RC_CURSOR_FILE_VERSION` (the header's `#define` held to it by
  `core/tests/cursor_file.rs`), the caps, the types and `CursorFile::parse`, which
  reads the object, `format`, `version` and CU-7's `typed` keys loosely BEFORE the
  strict `deny_unknown_fields` read through `serde_path_to_error`, so a newer file is
  refused by its version and a project by its format. `cursor_file_check.rs` — its
  check (`check`, `check_typed`; a shortcut holds `cmd` or `ctrl`, or `opt` with
  `OPTION_SHORTCUT_KEYS`, CU-60) and the base64 decoder, a module of its own because
  the two together pass the 400-line cap for a new file. `ffi_cursor.rs` —
  `rc_cursor_open` (parse and check; an open is the recorder's read-back, CU-15),
  `rc_cursor_free` and `rc_cursor_query` (road map creator-jobs CU2, spec §11 CU-25).
  `cursor_track.rs` — `CursorTrack`, the handle: the parsed file and its prepared
  paths under a `Mutex` (a `state` holds it only to clone an `Arc`, a poisoned lock
  taken with `into_inner`), ticks ↔ µs through `time.rs`, CU-20's M2 mapping per
  geometry entry (`scale_factor`, not `pixels_per_point`; `to_movie`, the one function), the raw path, idle opacity (CU-22),
  the image in force and ripples (CU-23). `cursor_smooth.rs` — `hold_end`, the one
  hold rule, and `SmoothPath` (pins, RDP, centripetal Catmull–Rom; CU-21).
  `cursor_query.rs` — the request vocabulary (its module doc) and `query`.
  `cursor_query_reads.rs` — its `events` and `path` reads, a pure move out of it (road map
  creator-jobs CU11a's toll); `state` takes `ends` and answers the shutter's two positions (spec
  §11 CU-115).
  `cursor_bursts.rs` — typing stretches and scroll bursts, one run finder. Auto Zoom's
  planner (road map creator-jobs CU7, spec §11 CU-70…CU-75), `plan_zooms` in
  `rc_cursor_query` (one track per clip, and the project): `cursor_zoom.rs` its
  arguments, refusals in CU-75's order, Replace's removals (`is_zoom` only), the bases a
  hold across a cut sets, and the ops (`remove_action`, `set_video`, `add_zoom_action` in
  time order) and answer; `cursor_zoom_run.rs` a run (clips continuing one source on one
  track) — its anchors through S, scroll bursts, barriers, the 10 Hz follow cursor and
  `land` (only given clips, no straddled cut); `cursor_zoom_visits.rs` anchors → visits →
  planned actions in container time, pure. Add Shortcut Overlays' planner (road map
  creator-jobs CU8, spec §11 CU-80…CU-84), `plan_overlays` in `rc_cursor_query` (one track per
  clip, and the project): `cursor_overlays.rs` — its arguments and refusals, the presses through
  `cursor_zoom_run.rs`'s `media_in` and `clip_time`, CU-80's timing in grid frames
  (`min_frames`, D_min(n) = 10n + 25; the same chord merged as "×k"; a different chord more than
  0.5 s late dropped), CU-83's Shortcuts track rule (`TRACK_NAME`; the front-most one in front of
